content.text:
Review target: `bc0696d..cbf8bc9`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name

findings.summary: 組の検査を「2 つとも値の検査を通ったときだけ」にしたので、片方だけが値の誤りでデフォルト値になると、poll_minutes が wait_minutes 以上の組をそのまま返す。正本の文書の「以上なら 2 つともデフォルト値に戻す」と食い違い、テストはその組 (3, 2) を期待として確かめている。
findings.short_summary: 片方が誤りだと poll ≧ wait の組を返す
findings.failure_scenario: リポジトリの設定 {"poll_minutes": 0, "wait_minutes": 2} で config read が poll 3・wait 2 を返し、作業のセッションがそのまま --interval 3 --minutes 2 で待機を起動すると、U14 の決まりどおり argparse の終了コード 2 で拒否され、作業のセッションが止まる。{"poll_minutes": 90, "wait_minutes": 0} でも poll 90・wait 60 になる。一方、poll_minutes が未設定で wait_minutes が 2 のときは 2 つとも戻すので、未設定と値の誤りで結果が分かれる。

findings.summary: 末尾が /. のパターン (dist/. など) は、末尾の / が落ちて dist になり、ディレクトリを指すパターンがファイル名 dist だけに一致するパターンに変わる。docstring が posixpath.normpath を避けた理由と同じ変化が起きる。
findings.short_summary: 末尾の /. で末尾の / が落ちる
findings.failure_scenario: files の pattern に "dist/." と書くと normalize_pattern が ("dist", None) を返し、警告も出ずに、ディレクトリ dist の中のファイルに一致しない規則になる ("a/./" は "a/" になる)。

findings.summary: 条件 normalized == "/" は成り立たない (区切りが空なら末尾の / を付けないので、結果は "" になる)。
findings.short_summary: 成り立たない条件 normalized == "/"
findings.failure_scenario: 読む人が "/" になる入力があると誤解し、ルートを指すパターンの判定を直すときに、実際に効いている条件 ("") を取り違える。

content.text:
Review target: `b78f885..53899a3`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale

Review target: `b78f885..53899a3`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print

9	種類は、パスについて次の問いに上から順に答え、最初に当てはまったものにする。1 つのパスが種類の違う複数の規則に一致すれば、この表で先の種類にする (下の「照合の順」)。
10	
11	| 段 | 問い | 当てはまれば | 競合の可能性の判定 | 競合の可能性があるときに示す扱い |
12	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
13	| 1 | 内容を知らない (パスに一致するパターンが、リポジトリの設定にもデフォルトの表にも無い) | `unknown-content` | 同じパスなら、競合しうるかどうかを利用者に尋ねる | — |
14	| 2 | ツールが生成する | `generated` | 判定しない | — |
15	| 3 | 構造を知らない | `unknown-structure` | 同じパスなら競合しうる | 待つ・共通の変更を先に小さな PR にする・競合しうるまま進める、の 3 つ |
16	| 4 | 分割できない | `indivisible` | 節で判定する (下) | 同上 |
17	| 5 | 分割すると意味が変わる可能性がある | `unstable` | 節で判定する | 同上。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、分けるリファクタリングも行える (意味が変わりうる点を添える) |
18	| 6 | (上のどれでもない) | `divisible` | 節で判定する | 同上。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、分けるリファクタリングも行える |
19	
20	`unknown-content` は、どの規則にも一致しないパスの種類なので、規則の `kind` には書けない。規則に書ける種類は段 2〜6 の 5 つ。
21	
22	節 (unit) は種類ではなく、構造を知っている種類 (段 4〜6) の判定の細かさとして扱う。
23	
24	**レビューでの修正による競合の可能性は判定しない。** 競合しうる相手とのマージの衝突は利用者が解消する (レビューで変わる範囲は宣言の時点で決まらないため)。
25	
26	## 節で判定する
27	
28	構造を知っている種類 (`indivisible`・`unstable`・`divisible`) は、両方の宣言がそのパスに `units` を書いていれば、節が同じか、一方の配列が他方の配列の先頭部分 (`["dependencies"]` と `["dependencies", "react"]` など) のときだけ競合しうる。`["dependencies", "react"]` と `["dependencies", "zod"]` は競合しない。どちらかが `units` を省けば、同じパスで競合しうる。
29	
30	節は階層ごとの名前の配列で表す (`["dependencies", "zod"]`)。区切りの文字を使わないのは、名前に `.` や `/` が含まれることがあるため (`package.json` の `exports` のキー `./utils`、`go.mod` のモジュール名 `github.com/foo/bar`、見出し「v1.2 の変更」)。名前はファイルにある文字のまま比べ、正規化しない (`"./utils"` と `"utils"` は JSON では別のキー)。節の名前は作業のセッションがファイルを読んで書き、スクリプトは名前を比べるだけで、ファイルを構文解析しない。
31	
32	## 節の表記 (`unit_notation`)
33	
34	規則の `unit_notation` は、そのファイルの節をどの構造の名前で書くかを示す。宣言の `units` と混同しないよう名前を分けている。
35	
36	| 構造 | 表記 | 例 (節の配列) |
37	| --- | --- | --- |
38	| JSON のキー | `json-key` | `["dependencies", "zod"]`・`["exports", "./utils"]` |
39	| YAML のキー | `yaml-key` | `["jobs", "test"]` |
40	| TOML のテーブル | `toml-table` | `["tool", "ruff"]` |
41	| Markdown の見出しと frontmatter | `markdown-heading` | `["手順", "1. 入力を読む"]`・`["frontmatter", "title"]` |
42	| Makefile のターゲット | `make-target` | `["test"]` |
43	| `go.mod` のディレクティブ | `go-mod-directive` | `["require", "github.com/foo/bar"]` |
44	| Dockerfile のステージ | `dockerfile-stage` | `["builder"]` |
45	| Terraform のブロック | `terraform-block` | `["resource", "aws_s3_bucket", "logs"]` |
46	
47	値は、表記の名前の文字列 (`"markdown-heading"`) か、表記とキーの深さを持つオブジェクト `{"notation": "json-key", "keys": ["dependencies", "devDependencies"]}` のどちらか。`keys` は、そのキーの下を 1 つ下の階層ごとの節として扱うキーの配列で、`package.json` では `dependencies` の下を依存ごとの節にする。`keys` に無いキーは、そのキー全体が 1 つの節になる。`keys` は `json-key`・`yaml-key`・`toml-table` でだけ意味を持つ。
48	
49	`unit_notation` の無い規則のファイル (`.go`・`.ts` など) は、節の表記を決めていないので、宣言に `units` を書かない。
50	
51	## パターンの書き方
52	
53	- `*` は 1 つのディレクトリの名前の中だけで一致し (`/` を越えない)、`**` は 0 個以上のディレクトリに一致する。`?` は `/` 以外の 1 文字。
54	- パターンは、リポジトリのルートからのパス全体と照合する。`*.pb.go` はルートのファイルだけに一致し、どの階層にも一致させるには `**/*.pb.go` と書く。
55	- 末尾が `/` のパターン (`dist/`) は、そのディレクトリの下のすべて (`dist/**`) と同じに扱う。
56	
57	Python 3.13 の `PurePath.full_match` と同じ規則で、`.gitignore` や `.gitattributes` の規則 (`/` を含まないパターンがどの階層にも一致する) とは違う。Python 3.11 には `full_match` が無く、`fnmatch` は `*` が `/` を越えて一致するので、`filekinds` はパターンを正規表現に変換して照合する。
58	
59	| パターン | 一致する | 一致しない |
60	| --- | --- | --- |
61	| `*.pb.go` | `api.pb.go` | `gen/api.pb.go` |
62	| `**/*.pb.go` | `api.pb.go`・`gen/api.pb.go` | |
63	| `src/*.ts` | `src/app.ts` | `src/lib/a.ts` |
64	| `dist/` | `dist/app.js`・`dist/assets/a.js` | `dist` (ディレクトリそのものの名前)・`distribution/a.js` |
65	
66	## 照合の順
67	
68	1. リポジトリの設定の `files` の規則を先に、デフォルトの表を後に照合する。設定に一致する規則があれば、デフォルトの表は見ない。
69	2. 同じ側 (設定、またはデフォルトの表) で種類の違う複数の規則に一致すれば、6 段の表で先の種類の規則を選ぶ。規則の並び順では決めない。
70	3. どちらにも一致しなければ `unknown-content`。
71	
72	設定の規則がデフォルトの表より先なのは、同じ拡張子でも扱いがリポジトリで違うため (同じ `.js` でも、自前で書いたものと、`.ts` やビルドから生成したものがある)。種類は拡張子ではなくパスのパターンで決める。
73	
74	## 分けたときの参照のされ方 (`split_reference`)
75	
76	`unstable` と `divisible` の規則には、ほかのファイルがそのファイルをどう参照するか (`split_reference`) を書く。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、ファイルを分けるリファクタリングを行うときに、参照元を宣言に含めるかを決めるため。
77	
78	| 値 | 意味 | 例 |
79	| --- | --- | --- |
80	| `directory` | 参照元のファイルがディレクトリを指定する。同じディレクトリの中で分けるかぎり参照元は変わらない | Go の `import` のパッケージ、Terraform のモジュール |
81	| `file` | 参照元のファイルがファイルを指定する。分けると参照元も変わるので、リファクタリングの宣言には変わる参照元も含める | TypeScript の `import './app'`・Makefile の `include`・CSS の `@import` |
82	
83	## マージできないファイル (`mergeable`)
84	
85	画像など、差分でマージできないファイルは、規則に `"mergeable": false` を書く (省略は真)。そのファイルで「競合しうるまま進める」を選ぼうとしたら、後で衝突を直せないことを添えて尋ねる。
86	
87	## 共有の状態を持つファイル
88	
89	`terraform.tfstate` のように、ファイルが共有の状態 (実際のインフラ) を記録しているものは、種類 (`generated`) とは別に資源 (ラベル `resource:…`) として扱う。種類はファイルの変更の競合の可能性を判定するもので、共有の状態の取り合いは資源で判定する。
90	
91	## デフォルトの表
92	
93	表そのものの正本は `file-kinds.json` で、ここでは行を言い直さない。行は、パターンと種類と、この文書の各節の属性 (`unit_notation`・`split_reference`・`mergeable`) を持ち、`filekinds` は設定の規則と同じ規則で照合する。各行を選んだ理由は次のとおり。
94	
95	- **`generated`** — ツールが書き、人が編集しないもの: Protocol Buffers の出力 (`**/*.pb.go`)、生成の印を名前に持つ Go のファイル (`**/*_generated.go`)、パッケージマネージャのロックファイル (`**/package-lock.json`・`**/yarn.lock`・`**/pnpm-lock.yaml`・`**/go.sum`・`**/Cargo.lock`)、縮小した JavaScript と CSS (`**/*.min.js`・`**/*.min.css`)、Terraform の状態 (`**/terraform.tfstate*`。共有の状態は上のとおり資源でも扱う)。
96	- **`unknown-structure`** — 中身を読んで節を決められないもの: Excel のブック (`**/*.xlsx`)。
97	- **`indivisible` で `mergeable` が偽** — 画像とフォントとバイナリの文書 (`**/*.png`・`**/*.jpg`・`**/*.jpeg`・`**/*.gif`・`**/*.svg`・`**/*.ico`・`**/*.pdf`・`**/*.woff`・`**/*.woff2`)。分けられず、差分でマージできない。SVG はテキストだが、描画ツールが全体を書き直すので画像と同じに扱う。
98	- **`unstable`** — 分けると適用の順や意味が変わりうるもの: マイグレーション (`**/migrations/**`) と SQL (`**/*.sql`) は実行の順に意味があり、Protocol Buffers の定義 (`**/*.proto`) はフィールド番号の割り当てに意味がある。参照のされ方は `file`。
99	- **`divisible` で節の表記があるもの** — `**/package.json` (`json-key`。`dependencies` と `devDependencies` の下を依存ごとの節にする)、`**/go.mod` (`go-mod-directive`。参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.md` (`markdown-heading`)、`**/Makefile` (`make-target`)、`**/*.toml` (`toml-table`)、`**/*.yaml`・`**/*.yml` (`yaml-key`)、`**/Dockerfile` (`dockerfile-stage`)、`**/*.tf` (`terraform-block`。参照のされ方は `directory`)。
100	- **`divisible` で節の表記の無いもの** — 自前で書くソースコード: `**/*.go` (参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.ts`・`**/*.tsx`・`**/*.js`・`**/*.py`・`**/*.rb`・`**/*.css` (参照のされ方は `file`)。節の表記を決めていないので、宣言に `units` は書けない。
101	
102	リポジトリで扱いが違うもの (生成した `.js`・`.gitattributes` で `linguist-generated` にしたディレクトリなど) は、リポジトリの設定の `files` に書く。候補はスキル `repo-preflight` が示す。
103

# ファイルの種類

**このファイルが、ファイルの種類と、競合の可能性の判定の規則の正本。** パスから種類と属性を決めるモジュール `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/filekinds.py` と、同梱のデフォルトの表 `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/file-kinds.json` はこれに従う。リポジトリの設定の `files` の様式と、読み込むときにそろえる表記の正本は [project-config.md](project-config.md) で、ここでは言い直さない。ほかの文書は種類と属性の名前を参照するだけで、問いや判定の規則を言い直さない。

**種類は宣言に書かず、スクリプトがパスから決める。** 作業のセッションは宣言にパスと節の名前だけを書く ([issue-format.md](issue-format.md))。

## 6 段の問いと種類

種類は、パスについて次の問いに上から順に答え、最初に当てはまったものにする。1 つのパスが種類の違う複数の規則に一致すれば、この表で先の種類にする (下の「照合の順」)。

| 段 | 問い | 当てはまれば | 競合の可能性の判定 | 競合の可能性があるときに示す扱い |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 内容を知らない (パスに一致するパターンが、リポジトリの設定にもデフォルトの表にも無い) | `unknown-content` | 同じパスなら、競合しうるかどうかを利用者に尋ねる | — |
| 2 | ツールが生成する | `generated` | 判定しない | — |
| 3 | 構造を知らない | `unknown-structure` | 同じパスなら競合しうる | 待つ・共通の変更を先に小さな PR にする・競合しうるまま進める、の 3 つ |
| 4 | 分割できない | `indivisible` | 節で判定する (下) | 同上 |
| 5 | 分割すると意味が変わる可能性がある | `unstable` | 節で判定する | 同上。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、分けるリファクタリングも行える (意味が変わりうる点を添える) |
| 6 | (上のどれでもない) | `divisible` | 節で判定する | 同上。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、分けるリファクタリングも行える |

`unknown-content` は、どの規則にも一致しないパスの種類なので、規則の `kind` には書けない。規則に書ける種類は段 2〜6 の 5 つ。

節 (unit) は種類ではなく、構造を知っている種類 (段 4〜6) の判定の細かさとして扱う。

**レビューでの修正による競合の可能性は判定しない。** 競合しうる相手とのマージの衝突は利用者が解消する (レビューで変わる範囲は宣言の時点で決まらないため)。

## 節で判定する

構造を知っている種類 (`indivisible`・`unstable`・`divisible`) は、両方の宣言がそのパスに `units` を書いていれば、節が同じか、一方の配列が他方の配列の先頭部分 (`["dependencies"]` と `["dependencies", "react"]` など) のときだけ競合しうる。`["dependencies", "react"]` と `["dependencies", "zod"]` は競合しない。どちらかが `units` を省けば、同じパスで競合しうる。

節は階層ごとの名前の配列で表す (`["dependencies", "zod"]`)。区切りの文字を使わないのは、名前に `.` や `/` が含まれることがあるため (`package.json` の `exports` のキー `./utils`、`go.mod` のモジュール名 `github.com/foo/bar`、見出し「v1.2 の変更」)。名前はファイルにある文字のまま比べ、正規化しない (`"./utils"` と `"utils"` は JSON では別のキー)。節の名前は作業のセッションがファイルを読んで書き、スクリプトは名前を比べるだけで、ファイルを構文解析しない。

| 構造 | 表記 | 例 (節の配列) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON のキー | `json-key` | `["dependencies", "zod"]`・`["exports", "./utils"]` |
| YAML のキー | `yaml-key` | `["jobs", "test"]` |
| TOML のテーブル | `toml-table` | `["tool", "ruff"]` |
| Markdown の見出しと frontmatter | `markdown-heading` | `["手順", "1. 入力を読む"]`・`["frontmatter", "title"]` |
| Makefile のターゲット | `make-target` | `["test"]` |
| `go.mod` のディレクティブ | `go-mod-directive` | `["require", "github.com/foo/bar"]` |
| Dockerfile のステージ | `dockerfile-stage` | `["builder"]` |
| Terraform のブロック | `terraform-block` | `["resource", "aws_s3_bucket", "logs"]` |

値は、表記の名前の文字列 (`"markdown-heading"`) か、表記とキーの深さを持つオブジェクト `{"notation": "json-key", "keys": ["dependencies", "devDependencies"]}` のどちらか。`keys` は、そのキーの下を 1 つ下の階層ごとの節として扱うキーの配列で、`package.json` では `dependencies` の下を依存ごとの節にする。`keys` に無いキーは、そのキー全体が 1 つの節になる。`keys` は `json-key`・`yaml-key`・`toml-table` でだけ意味を持つ。

## パターンの書き方

Python 3.13 の `PurePath.full_match` と同じ規則で、`.gitignore` や `.gitattributes` の規則 (`/` を含まないパターンがどの階層にも一致する) とは違う。Python 3.11 には `full_match` が無く、`fnmatch` は `*` が `/` を越えて一致するので、`filekinds` はパターンを正規表現に変換して照合する。

| パターン | 一致する | 一致しない |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*.pb.go` | `api.pb.go` | `gen/api.pb.go` |
| `**/*.pb.go` | `api.pb.go`・`gen/api.pb.go` | |
| `src/*.ts` | `src/app.ts` | `src/lib/a.ts` |
| `dist/` | `dist/app.js`・`dist/assets/a.js` | `dist` (ディレクトリそのものの名前)・`distribution/a.js` |

## 照合の順

1. リポジトリの設定の `files` の規則を先に、デフォルトの表を後に照合する。設定に一致する規則があれば、デフォルトの表は見ない。
2. 同じ側 (設定、またはデフォルトの表) で種類の違う複数の規則に一致すれば、6 段の表で先の種類の規則を選ぶ。規則の並び順では決めない。
3. どちらにも一致しなければ `unknown-content`。

設定の規則がデフォルトの表より先なのは、同じ拡張子でも扱いがリポジトリで違うため (同じ `.js` でも、自前で書いたものと、`.ts` やビルドから生成したものがある)。種類は拡張子ではなくパスのパターンで決める。

## 分けたときの参照のされ方 (`split_reference`)

`unstable` と `divisible` の規則には、ほかのファイルがそのファイルをどう参照するか (`split_reference`) を書く。共通の変更を先にする小さな PR で、ファイルを分けるリファクタリングを行うときに、参照元を宣言に含めるかを決めるため。

| 値 | 意味 | 例 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | 参照元のファイルがディレクトリを指定する。同じディレクトリの中で分けるかぎり参照元は変わらない | Go の `import` のパッケージ、Terraform のモジュール |

## マージできないファイル (`mergeable`)

画像など、差分でマージできないファイルは、規則に `"mergeable": false` を書く (省略は真)。そのファイルで「競合しうるまま進める」を選ぼうとしたら、後で衝突を直せないことを添えて尋ねる。

## 共有の状態を持つファイル

`terraform.tfstate` のように、ファイルが共有の状態 (実際のインフラ) を記録しているものは、種類 (`generated`) とは別に資源 (ラベル `resource:…`) として扱う。種類はファイルの変更の競合の可能性を判定するもので、共有の状態の取り合いは資源で判定する。

## デフォルトの表

表そのものの正本は `file-kinds.json` で、ここでは行を言い直さない。行は、パターンと種類と、この文書の各節の属性 (`unit_notation`・`split_reference`・`mergeable`) を持ち、`filekinds` は設定の規則と同じ規則で照合する。各行を選んだ理由は次のとおり。

- **`generated`** — ツールが書き、人が編集しないもの: Protocol Buffers の出力 (`**/*.pb.go`)、生成の印を名前に持つ Go のファイル (`**/*_generated.go`)、パッケージマネージャのロックファイル (`**/package-lock.json`・`**/yarn.lock`・`**/pnpm-lock.yaml`・`**/go.sum`・`**/Cargo.lock`)、縮小した JavaScript と CSS (`**/*.min.js`・`**/*.min.css`)、Terraform の状態 (`**/terraform.tfstate*`。共有の状態は上のとおり資源でも扱う)。
- **`unknown-structure`** — 中身を読んで節を決められないもの: Excel のブック (`**/*.xlsx`)。
- **`indivisible` で `mergeable` が偽** — 画像とフォントとバイナリの文書 (`**/*.png`・`**/*.jpg`・`**/*.jpeg`・`**/*.gif`・`**/*.svg`・`**/*.ico`・`**/*.pdf`・`**/*.woff`・`**/*.woff2`)。分けられず、差分でマージできない。SVG はテキストだが、描画ツールが全体を書き直すので画像と同じに扱う。
- **`unstable`** — 分けると適用の順や意味が変わりうるもの: マイグレーション (`**/migrations/**`) と SQL (`**/*.sql`) は実行の順に意味があり、Protocol Buffers の定義 (`**/*.proto`) はフィールド番号の割り当てに意味がある。参照のされ方は `file`。
- **`divisible` で節の表記があるもの** — `**/package.json` (`json-key`。`dependencies` と `devDependencies` の下を依存ごとの節にする)、`**/go.mod` (`go-mod-directive`。参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.md` (`markdown-heading`)、`**/Makefile` (`make-target`)、`**/*.toml` (`toml-table`)、`**/*.yaml`・`**/*.yml` (`yaml-key`)、`**/Dockerfile` (`dockerfile-stage`)、`**/*.tf` (`terraform-block`。参照のされ方は `directory`)。
- **`divisible` で節の表記の無いもの** — 自前で書くソースコード: `**/*.go` (参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.ts`・`**/*.tsx`・`**/*.js`・`**/*.py`・`**/*.rb`・`**/*.css` (参照のされ方は `file`)。節の表記を決めていないので、宣言に `units` は書けない。

リポジトリで扱いが違うもの (生成した `.js`・`.gitattributes` で `linguist-generated` にしたディレクトリなど) は、リポジトリの設定の `files` に書く。候補はスキル `repo-preflight` が示す。

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.

to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `01b415b..0d3c617`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete

uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,

 - **`divisible` で節の表記の無いもの** — 自前で書くソースコード: `**/*.go` (参照のされ方は `directory`)、`**/*.ts`・`**/*.tsx`・`**/*.js`・`**/*.py`・`**/*.rb`・`**/*.css` (参照のされ方は `file`)。節の表記を決めていないので、宣言に `units` は書けない。

content.text:
Review target: `0d3c617..e1bbc1e`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `3c6f109..2c5aa58`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1	"""`gh` の実行。このモジュールの関数 `run` だけが `gh` を起動する (R31・KTD14)。ほかのモジュールは `subprocess` で `gh` を
     2	呼ばず、`run` に引数の配列を渡す。
     3	
     4	`run` は、終了コード・標準出力・標準エラー出力の末尾・タイムアウトで打ち切ったか・失敗の種類 (`failure`) を返す。
     5	失敗の種類は標準エラー出力と標準出力の文言から分け、再試行や再開時刻までの待ちはしない。待つかどうかと終了コード
     6	(KTD6 の 8・3・4) は呼び出し側 (待機のサブコマンドなど) が決める。
     7	
     8	テストは PATH の先頭に偽の `gh` (issue-dispatch/tests/fake-gh) のディレクトリを加えて差し替える。
     9	"""
    10	
    11	import json
    12	import re
    13	import subprocess
    14	import time
    15	
    16	DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60
    17	STDERR_TAIL_LINES = 20
    18	MUTATION_INTERVAL = 1.0  # 変更系の呼び出しの間隔 (秒。KTD14)
    19	
    20	# 失敗の種類。None は成功
    21	FAILURES = ("auth", "rate_limit", "network", "timeout", "other")
    22	
    23	_AUTH_RE = re.compile(r"HTTP 401|Bad credentials|gh auth login|not logged in", re.IGNORECASE)
    24	_RATE_LIMIT_RE = re.compile(r"rate limit|RATE_LIMITED|secondary rate|abuse detection", re.IGNORECASE)
    25	_NETWORK_RE = re.compile(
    26	    r"dial tcp|connection refused|connection reset|no such host|i/o timeout|TLS handshake|proxyconnect|"
    27	    r"network is unreachable|error connecting|could not resolve host",
    28	    re.IGNORECASE,
    29	)
    30	
    31	_last_mutation_end = None
    32	
    33	
    34	def classify(exit_code, stdout, stderr, timed_out):
    35	    """終了コードと出力から失敗の種類を決める。成功 (終了コード 0) なら None。"""
    36	    if timed_out:
    37	        return "timeout"
    38	    if exit_code == 0:
    39	        return None
    40	    text = f"{stderr}\n{stdout}"
    41	    if _AUTH_RE.search(text):
    42	        return "auth"
    43	    if _RATE_LIMIT_RE.search(text):
    44	        return "rate_limit"
    45	    if _NETWORK_RE.search(text):
    46	        return "network"
    47	    return "other"
    48	
    49	
    50	def _tail(text, lines=STDERR_TAIL_LINES):
    51	    return "\n".join(text.splitlines()[-lines:])
    52	
    53	
    54	def _text(value):
    55	    if value is None:
    56	        return ""
    57	    if isinstance(value, bytes):
    58	        return value.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    59	    return value
    60	
    61	
    62	def run(args, timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, mutation=False):
    63	    """`gh` を引数の配列で実行する。
    64	
    65	    mutation が真なら、前の変更系の呼び出しの終わりから MUTATION_INTERVAL 秒以上空けてから実行する。
    66	    返り値: {"args", "exit_code" (タイムアウトなら None), "stdout", "stderr_tail", "timed_out", "failure", "json"
    67	    (標準出力が JSON として読めればその値、読めなければ None)}
    68	    """
    69	    global _last_mutation_end
    70	    args = list(args)
    71	    if mutation and _last_mutation_end is not None:
    72	        wait = MUTATION_INTERVAL - (time.monotonic() - _last_mutation_end)
    73	        if wait > 0:
    74	            time.sleep(wait)
    75	    try:
    76	        completed = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    77	        exit_code, stdout, stderr, timed_out = completed.returncode, completed.stdout, completed.stderr, False
    78	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
    79	        exit_code, stdout, stderr, timed_out = None, _text(e.stdout), _text(e.stderr), True
    80	    finally:
    81	        if mutation:
    82	            _last_mutation_end = time.monotonic()
    83	    try:
    84	        parsed = json.loads(stdout) if stdout.strip() else None
    85	    except ValueError:
    86	        parsed = None
    87	    return {
    88	        "args": args,
    89	        "exit_code": exit_code,
    90	        "stdout": stdout,
    91	        "stderr_tail": _tail(stderr),
    92	        "timed_out": timed_out,
    93	        "failure": classify(exit_code, stdout, stderr, timed_out),
    94	        "json": parsed,
    95	    }
    96	
    97	
    98	def rate_limit_reset_at(timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT):
    99	    """GraphQL のレート制限の再開時刻 (UNIX 時刻の秒) を `gh api rate_limit` で読む。読めなければ None。
   100	    REST の rate_limit はレート制限に数えられないので、制限の間でも読める。"""

   102	    data = result["json"]
   103	    try:

   105	    except (TypeError, KeyError, ValueError):

     3	
     4	実際の gh の代わりに、環境変数の指示どおりに振る舞う (先例: review-triage/tests/fake-claude)。
     5	
     6	- FAKE_GH_ARGS: 受けた引数 (argv[1:]) と時刻と cwd を JSON の 1 行として追記するファイル
     7	- FAKE_GH_SLEEP: 応答の前に待つ秒数 (既定 0)

    11	    auth_expired    固定データ auth-invalid-token を返す (終了コード 1)
    12	    not_logged_in   固定データ auth-not-logged-in を返す (終了コード 4)
    13	    rate_limited    固定データ graphql-rate-limited を返す (終了コード 1)
    14	    network         固定データ network-unreachable を返す (終了コード 1)
    15	    hang            応答せずに終わらない (呼び出し側のタイムアウトを試す)

    17	- FAKE_GH_RESPONSES: 応答の指定の JSON ファイル。要素の配列で、受けた引数に最初に一致した要素を返す。要素のキー:
    18	    prefix    引数の先頭がこの配列と同じなら一致 (例: ["issue", "view"])
    19	    contains  この配列の要素をすべて含めば一致 (prefix と両方書けば両方)
    20	    stdout    標準出力に書く文字列。オブジェクトや配列なら JSON にして書く。{"fixture": "<場合>"} なら固定データの <場合>.stdout の中身
    21	    stderr    標準エラー出力に書く文字列 (既定は空)
    22	    exit      終了コード (既定 0)
    23	    once      真なら 1 回だけ使い、使ったら used を真にしてファイルに書き戻す (書き込みの直後に別の値を返す場合を表す)
    24	  一致する要素が無ければ、標準エラー出力に引数を書いて終了コード 99 で終わる (指定の漏れを、成功した応答と取り違えないため)
    25	"""
    26	
    27	import json
    28	import os
    29	import sys
    30	import time
    31	
    32	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))  # シンボリックリンクで gh の名前に置かれるので、実体の場所
    33	
    34	
    35	def fixture(name, kind):

    43

    46	    if path:

    49	
    50

    52	    sys.stdout.write(stdout)
    53	    sys.stdout.flush()
    54	    sys.stderr.write(stderr)
    55	    sys.stderr.flush()

    57

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""`gh` の実行 (issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/gh.py) と、偽の `gh` (issue-dispatch/tests/fake-gh) のテスト。

PATH の先頭に偽の `gh` のディレクトリを加えて `gh.run` を実行する。実物の `gh` は使わない。

  python3 -m unittest discover -s issue-dispatch/tests
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_SCRIPTS = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "scripts")
sys.path.insert(0, _SCRIPTS)

from issue_dispatch import gh  # noqa: E402

_FAKE = os.path.join(_HERE, "fake-gh")
_FIXTURES = os.path.join(_HERE, "fixtures", "gh")


class FakeGhTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """偽の `gh` を PATH の先頭に置き、環境変数で振る舞いを決める。"""

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = self._tmp.name
        self.bin = os.path.join(self.root, "bin")
        os.makedirs(self.bin)
        os.symlink(_FAKE, os.path.join(self.bin, "gh"))
        self.args_file = os.path.join(self.root, "args.jsonl")
        self.responses_file = os.path.join(self.root, "responses.json")
        self._saved = {k: os.environ.get(k) for k in
                       ("PATH", "FAKE_GH_ARGS", "FAKE_GH_RESPONSES", "FAKE_GH_MODE", "FAKE_GH_SLEEP", "FAKE_GH_EXIT")}
        os.environ["PATH"] = self.bin + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "")
        os.environ["FAKE_GH_ARGS"] = self.args_file
        os.environ["FAKE_GH_RESPONSES"] = self.responses_file
        for k in ("FAKE_GH_MODE", "FAKE_GH_SLEEP", "FAKE_GH_EXIT"):
            os.environ.pop(k, None)
        gh._last_mutation_end = None

    def tearDown(self):
        for k, v in self._saved.items():
            if v is None:
                os.environ.pop(k, None)
            else:
                os.environ[k] = v
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def responses(self, entries):
        with open(self.responses_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(entries, f, ensure_ascii=False)

    def recorded(self):
        with open(self.args_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]

    def fixture(self, name, kind):
        with open(os.path.join(_FIXTURES, f"{name}.{kind}"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return f.read()


class RunTest(FakeGhTest):

    def test_passes_args_and_returns_exit_code_and_stderr_tail(self):
        stderr = "\n".join(f"line {i}" for i in range(1, 31)) + "\n"
        self.responses([{"prefix": ["issue", "view"], "stdout": {"number": 1}, "stderr": stderr, "exit": 3}])
        r = gh.run(["issue", "view", "1", "-R", "o/r", "--json", "number"])
        self.assertEqual(self.recorded()[0]["args"], ["issue", "view", "1", "-R", "o/r", "--json", "number"],

        self.assertEqual(r["exit_code"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(r["stdout"], '{"number": 1}')
        self.assertEqual(r["json"], {"number": 1}, "標準出力が JSON なら読んだ値を返すこと")
        self.assertEqual(r["stderr_tail"].splitlines(), [f"line {i}" for i in range(11, 31)],

        self.assertFalse(r["timed_out"])

findings.summary: classify は標準出力も正規表現で調べるので、GraphQL が一部のデータとエラーを一緒に返した (終了コード 1) とき、Issue の本文など利用者の書いた文字列に引きずられて auth や rate_limit と判定する。

findings.failure_scenario: 本文に "run gh auth login" や "rate limit" を含む Issue を読む GraphQL の問い合わせが、別の node の NOT_FOUND で終了コード 1 になると failure が auth になり、呼び出し側は認証切れ (終了コード 8) として止まるか、レート制限として再開時刻まで待つ。

findings.summary: gh が PATH に無いと subprocess.run が FileNotFoundError を投げ、run は failure を持つ返り値を返さずに例外で終わる。
findings.short_summary: gh が無いと例外で落ちる
findings.failure_scenario: gh を入れていないマシンで待機や CLI が run を呼ぶと、traceback で終了コード 1 になり、呼び出し側は「gh が入っていない」という直し方を利用者に示せず、スクリプトの不具合として扱う。

findings.summary: 標準出力を 1 つの JSON としてだけ読むので、gh api --paginate が出す、ページごとの配列をつなげた出力では json が警告なしに None になる。
findings.short_summary: --paginate の出力で json が None になる
findings.failure_scenario: 後の単位がコメントの一覧を gh api --paginate で読むと、成功 (終了コード 0・failure None) なのに json が None になり、「コメントが無い」と取り違えうる。

findings.short_summary: 変更系の間隔がプロセスをまたいで守られない
findings.failure_scenario: スキルが CLI の変更系のサブコマンド (project set-status と comment など) を続けて別のプロセスで実行すると、_last_mutation_end が毎回 None から始まり、1 秒以内に 2 つの書き込みが GitHub に届いて secondary rate limit に当たりうる。

content.text:
Review target: `2c5aa58..e9ae7de`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `e9ae7de..9886aca`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.
