Review target: `4aacd53..2cdb0d1`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `8044150..776e7b7`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `b504696..c051a54`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1	"""Issue の参照の正規化。`owner/repo#番号` と URL (`https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/番号`) を同じ正規形
     2	(キー `owner/repo#番号`) にする。宣言の `blocked_by`・記録の項目のキー・`gh issue edit --add-blocked-by` に渡す URL の
     3	変換に使う。リポジトリの名前の形は config.REPO_NAME_PATTERN と同じ (名前に使える文字だけで決める)。
     4	"""
     5	
     6	import re
     7	
     8	REPO_NAME_PATTERN = r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"
     9	_KEY_RE = re.compile(rf"^(?P<repo>{REPO_NAME_PATTERN})#(?P<number>[1-9][0-9]*)$")
    10	_URL_RE = re.compile(rf"^https://github\.com/(?P<repo>{REPO_NAME_PATTERN})/(?P<kind>issues|pull)/(?P<number>[1-9][0-9]*)/?$")
    11	
    12	
    13	def parse_issue_ref(text):
    14	    """Issue の参照を読む。返り値は {"repo": "owner/name", "number": int, "key", "url"} か、読めなければ None。
    15	    URL は `/issues/<番号>` の形だけ (PR の URL `/pull/<番号>` は Issue の参照ではないので None)。"""
    16	    if not isinstance(text, str):
    17	        return None
    18	    text = text.strip()
    19	    m = _KEY_RE.match(text)
    20	    kind = "issues"
    21	    if not m:
    22	        m = _URL_RE.match(text)
    23	        if not m:
    24	            return None
    25	        kind = m.group("kind")
    26	    if kind != "issues":
    27	        return None
    28	    repo, number = m.group("repo"), int(m.group("number"))
    29	    return {"repo": repo, "number": number, "key": f"{repo}#{number}", "url": f"https://github.com/{repo}/issues/{number}"}
    30	
    31	
    32	def issue_key(text):
    33	    """参照を正規形 `owner/repo#番号` にする。読めなければ None。"""
    34	    parsed = parse_issue_ref(text)
    35	    return parsed["key"] if parsed else None
    36	
    37	
    38	def issue_url(text):
    39	    """参照を URL にする (`gh issue edit --add-blocked-by` は URL の形だけを受け付ける。U1)。読めなければ None。"""
    40	    parsed = parse_issue_ref(text)
    41	    return parsed["url"] if parsed else None
    42	
    43	
    44	def same_issue(a, b):
    45	    """2 つの参照が同じ Issue を指すか (リポジトリの名前は大文字小文字を区別しない)。どちらかが読めなければ偽。"""
    46	    pa, pb = parse_issue_ref(a), parse_issue_ref(b)
    47	    return bool(pa and pb and pa["repo"].lower() == pb["repo"].lower() and pa["number"] == pb["number"])
     1	"""Project (GitHub Projects) の読み書き。項目の一覧 (`items`)・フィールドと選択肢とワークフローの検査 (`check`)・
     2	不足の作成 (`add_fields`)・Status とフィールドの書き込み。様式の正本は
     3	issue-dispatch/skills/issue-dispatch/references/project-schema.md。
     4	
     5	GraphQL は同じディレクトリの graphql/*.graphql を `gh api graphql` で実行する (操作名で偽の gh が見分ける)。

    43	def load_query(name):
    44	    with open(os.path.join(GRAPHQL_DIR, f"{name}.graphql"), encoding="utf-8") as f:

    48	def graphql(name, variables, mutation=False, timeout=gh.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT):
    49	    """graphql/<name>.graphql を変数つきで実行する。返り値は (data, None) か (None, 失敗の説明)。"""
    50	    args = ["api", "graphql", "-f", f"query={load_query(name)}"]
    51	    for key, value in variables.items():
    52	        if value is None:
    53	            continue
    54	        args += (["-F", f"{key}={value}"] if isinstance(value, (int, bool)) and not isinstance(value, str) else ["-f", f"{key}={value}"])
    55	    r = gh.run(args, timeout=timeout, mutation=mutation, expect_json=True)
    56	    if r["failure"] or r["json"] is None:
    57	        return None, {"failure": r["failure"] or "other", "message": r["stderr_tail"] or r["json_error"] or "", "exit_code": r["exit_code"]}
    58	    data = r["json"].get("data") if isinstance(r["json"], dict) else None
    59	    if r["json"].get("errors") or data is None:
    60	        return None, {"failure": "other", "message": json.dumps(r["json"].get("errors"), ensure_ascii=False), "exit_code": r["exit_code"]}
    61	    return data, None

    90	def check(meta_project):
    91	    """フィールド・Status の選択肢・ワークフローの不足と案内を列挙する (gh は実行しない)。"""
    92	    fields = meta_project["fields"]

    94	    for name, data_type in CUSTOM_FIELDS.items():
    95	        f = fields.get(name)
    96	        if f is None:
    97	            missing_fields.append({"name": name, "data_type": data_type, "options": list(STUCK_STATES) if name == "Agent stuck state" else []})
    98	        elif f["data_type"] != data_type:
    99	            missing_fields.append({"name": name, "data_type": data_type, "problem": f"型が {f['data_type']} (期待は {data_type})"})
   100	        elif name == "Agent stuck state":
   101	            have = {o["name"] for o in f["options"]}
   102	            lacking = [v for v in STUCK_STATES if v not in have]
   103	            if lacking:
   104	                missing_fields.append({"name": name, "data_type": data_type, "problem": f"値 {', '.join(lacking)} が無い", "options": lacking})
   105	    status = fields.get("Status")
   106	    missing_options = []
   107	    proposal = None
   108	    if status is None or status["data_type"] != "SINGLE_SELECT":
   109	        missing_options = list(STATUS_OPTIONS)
   110	    else:
   111	        have = {o["name"] for o in status["options"]}
   112	        missing_options = [name for name in STATUS_OPTIONS if name not in have]
   113	        if missing_options:
   114	            options = [{"id": o["id"], "name": o["name"], "color": o["color"] or "GRAY", "description": o["description"] or ""}
   115	                       for o in status["options"]]
   116	            for name in missing_options:
   117	                color, description = ADDED_STATUS_OPTIONS.get(name, ("GRAY", ""))
   118	                options.append({"name": name, "color": color, "description": description})
   119	            proposal = {"fieldId": status["id"], "options": options}
   120	    workflows = meta_project["workflows"]
   121	    enabled = {name for name, w in workflows.items() if w["enabled"]}
   122	    wf = {
   123	        "required_disabled": [n for n in REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS if n not in enabled],
   124	        "recommended_disabled": [n for n in RECOMMENDED_WORKFLOWS if n not in enabled],  # 一覧に無いものも無効として数える
   125	        "notice_enabled": [n for n in NOTICE_IF_ENABLED_WORKFLOWS if n in enabled],
   126	        "discouraged_enabled": [n for n in DISCOURAGED_WORKFLOWS if n in enabled],

   135	               "--data-type", f["data_type"]]
   136	        if f["options"]:
   137	            cmd += ["--single-select-options", ",".join(f["options"])]

   140	            "missing_fields": missing_fields, "missing_status_options": missing_options, "workflows": wf,

   192	def _more_pages(name, repo, number, first_page, key, convert):
   193	    """コメントか出来事の続きのページを読んで、変換した要素の配列を返す。読めなければ問題を返す。"""
   194	    nodes = [convert(n) for n in first_page["nodes"] if n]
   195	    info = first_page.get("pageInfo") or {}
   196	    owner, _, repo_name = repo.partition("/")
   197	    while info.get("hasNextPage"):
   198	        data, problem = graphql(name, {"owner": owner, "name": repo_name, "number": number, "after": info.get("endCursor")})
   199	        if problem:
   200	            return nodes, problem
   201	        page = data["repository"]["issue"][key]
   202	        nodes += [convert(n) for n in page["nodes"] if n]
   203	        info = page.get("pageInfo") or {}
   204	    return nodes, None

   207	def simplify_item(node, position):
   208	    """GraphQL の項目を、後の単位が読む形にする。Issue 以外の項目 (draft issue・PR) は content を None にして返す。"""
   209	    content = node.get("content") or {}
   210	    fields = {}
   211	    status = None
   212	    for fv in node["fieldValues"]["nodes"]:
   213	        if not fv or not fv.get("field"):
   214	            continue
   215	        name = fv["field"]["name"]
   216	        if name == "Status":
   217	            status = {"name": fv.get("name"), "option_id": fv.get("optionId"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   218	        elif "text" in fv:
   219	            fields[name] = {"text": fv.get("text"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   220	        else:
   221	            fields[name] = {"name": fv.get("name"), "option_id": fv.get("optionId"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   222	    item = {"item_id": node["id"], "position": position, "item_updated_at": node.get("updatedAt"), "status": status, "fields": fields,
   223	            "content_type": content.get("__typename"), "key": None}
   224	    if content.get("__typename") != "Issue":
   225	        return item, []
   226	    repo = content["repository"]["nameWithOwner"]
   227	    sub = content.get("subIssuesSummary") or {}
   228	    parent = content.get("parent")
   229	    item.update({
   230	        "key": _ref(content), "repo": repo, "number": content["number"], "url": content["url"], "title": content["title"],
   231	        "state": content["state"], "created_at": content.get("createdAt"), "author": (content.get("author") or {}).get("login"),
   232	        "visibility": content["repository"].get("visibility"), "in_organization": content["repository"].get("isInOrganization"),
   233	        "assignees": [a["login"] for a in content["assignees"]["nodes"]],
   234	        "labels": [l["name"] for l in content["labels"]["nodes"]],
   235	        "parent": _ref(parent) if parent and parent.get("repository") else None,
   236	        "sub_issues": {"total": sub.get("total", 0), "completed": sub.get("completed", 0)},
   237	        "is_parent": bool(sub.get("total")),
   238	        "blocked_by": [{"key": _ref(b), "url": b["url"], "state": b["state"]} for b in content["blockedBy"]["nodes"]],
   239	        "body_edits": [{"editor": (e.get("editor") or {}).get("login"), "edited_at": e.get("editedAt"), "deleted_at": e.get("deletedAt")}
   240	                       for e in content["userContentEdits"]["nodes"]],
   241	        "prs": [{"number": p["number"], "url": p["url"], "state": p["state"], "draft": p["isDraft"], "merged": p["merged"],
   242	                 "created_at": p.get("createdAt"), "merged_at": p.get("mergedAt"), "closed_at": p.get("closedAt"),
   243	                 "author": (p.get("author") or {}).get("login"), "base_ref": p.get("baseRefName")}
   244	                for p in content["closedByPullRequestsReferences"]["nodes"]],
   245	    })
   246	    problems = []
   247	    comments, problem = _more_pages("issue-comments", repo, content["number"], content["comments"], "comments", _comment)
   248	    if problem:
   249	        problems.append({"item": item["key"], "what": "comments", **problem})
   250	    events, problem = _more_pages("issue-timeline", repo, content["number"], content["timelineItems"], "timelineItems", _event)
   251	    if problem:
   252	        problems.append({"item": item["key"], "what": "events", **problem})
   253	    item["comments"] = comments
   254	    item["events"] = sorted(events, key=lambda e: (e.get("at") or "", EVENT_TYPES.index(e["type"]) if e["type"] in EVENT_TYPES else 99))
   255	    return item, problems

   258	def items(project):
   259	    """項目の一覧を位置の順に全部読む。返り値: {"status": "ok", "project_id", "items": [...], "problems": [...], "rate_limit"} か
   260	    {"status": "error", ...} (最初のページが読めないとき)。続きのページやコメントの続きが読めなかったときは problems に入れて止める。"""
   261	    result_items = []
   262	    problems = []
   263	    after = None
   264	    project_id = None
   265	    rate = None
   266	    position = 0
   267	    while True:
   268	        data, problem = graphql("items", {"owner": project["owner"], "number": project["number"], "after": after})
   269	        if problem:
   270	            if not result_items:
   271	                return {"status": "error", **problem}
   272	            problems.append({"what": "items-page", "after": after, **problem})
   273	            break
   274	        node = _project_node(data)
   275	        if node is None:
   276	            return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "message": f"Project {project['owner']}/{project['number']} が無いか読めない", "exit_code": 0}
   277	        project_id = node["id"]
   278	        rate = data.get("rateLimit")
   279	        for n in node["items"]["nodes"]:
   280	            if not n:
   281	                continue
   282	            position += 1
   283	            item, item_problems = simplify_item(n, position)
   284	            result_items.append(item)
   285	            problems += item_problems
   286	        info = node["items"].get("pageInfo") or {}
   287	        if not info.get("hasNextPage"):
   288	            break
   289	        after = info.get("endCursor")
   290	    return {"status": "ok" if not problems else "partial", "project_id": project_id, "items": result_items, "problems": problems, "rate_limit": rate}

   295	def set_status(meta_project, item_id, status):
   296	    """Status を書く。管理のセッションが書く 5 つ以外 (Done を含む) は gh を実行せずに拒否する (R2)。"""
   297	    if status not in MANAGER_STATUSES:
   298	        return {"status": "rejected", "message": f"Status {status!r} は書かない (書けるのは {', '.join(MANAGER_STATUSES)}。Done は組み込みワークフローが書く)"}
   299	    field = meta_project["fields"].get("Status")
   300	    option = next((o for o in (field or {}).get("options", []) if o["name"] == status), None)
   301	    if field is None or option is None:
   302	        return {"status": "rejected", "message": f"Project の Status に選択肢 {status!r} が無い (project check で足す)"}
   303	    r = gh.run(["project", "item-edit", "--project-id", meta_project["id"], "--id", item_id, "--field-id", field["id"],
   304	                "--single-select-option-id", option["id"]], mutation=True)
   305	    if r["failure"]:
   306	        return {"status": "error", "failure": r["failure"], "message": r["stderr_tail"]}
   307	    return {"status": "ok", "item_id": item_id, "field": "Status", "value": status}

    43	def load_query(name):
    44	    with open(os.path.join(GRAPHQL_DIR, f"{name}.graphql"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
    45	        return "".join(line for line in f if not line.lstrip().startswith("#"))

    48	def graphql(name, variables, mutation=False, timeout=gh.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT):
    49	    """graphql/<name>.graphql を変数つきで実行する。返り値は (data, None) か (None, 失敗の説明)。"""
    50	    args = ["api", "graphql", "-f", f"query={load_query(name)}"]
    51	    for key, value in variables.items():
    52	        if value is None:
    53	            continue
    54	        args += (["-F", f"{key}={value}"] if isinstance(value, (int, bool)) and not isinstance(value, str) else ["-f", f"{key}={value}"])
    55	    r = gh.run(args, timeout=timeout, mutation=mutation, expect_json=True)
    56	    if r["failure"] or r["json"] is None:
    57	        return None, {"failure": r["failure"] or "other", "message": r["stderr_tail"] or r["json_error"] or "", "exit_code": r["exit_code"]}
    58	    data = r["json"].get("data") if isinstance(r["json"], dict) else None
    59	    if r["json"].get("errors") or data is None:
    60	        return None, {"failure": "other", "message": json.dumps(r["json"].get("errors"), ensure_ascii=False), "exit_code": r["exit_code"]}
    61	    return data, None

    84	    workflows = {w["name"]: {"id": w["id"], "number": w["number"], "enabled": w["enabled"]} for w in node["workflows"]["nodes"]}
    85	    return {"status": "ok", "project": {"id": node["id"], "title": node["title"], "url": node["url"], "owner": project["owner"],

    90	def check(meta_project):
    91	    """フィールド・Status の選択肢・ワークフローの不足と案内を列挙する (gh は実行しない)。"""
    92	    fields = meta_project["fields"]
    93	    missing_fields = []
    94	    for name, data_type in CUSTOM_FIELDS.items():
    95	        f = fields.get(name)
    96	        if f is None:
    97	            missing_fields.append({"name": name, "data_type": data_type, "options": list(STUCK_STATES) if name == "Agent stuck state" else []})
    98	        elif f["data_type"] != data_type:
    99	            missing_fields.append({"name": name, "data_type": data_type, "problem": f"型が {f['data_type']} (期待は {data_type})"})
   100	        elif name == "Agent stuck state":
   101	            have = {o["name"] for o in f["options"]}
   102	            lacking = [v for v in STUCK_STATES if v not in have]
   103	            if lacking:
   104	                missing_fields.append({"name": name, "data_type": data_type, "problem": f"値 {', '.join(lacking)} が無い", "options": lacking})
   105	    status = fields.get("Status")
   106	    missing_options = []
   107	    proposal = None
   108	    if status is None or status["data_type"] != "SINGLE_SELECT":
   109	        missing_options = list(STATUS_OPTIONS)
   110	    else:
   111	        have = {o["name"] for o in status["options"]}
   112	        missing_options = [name for name in STATUS_OPTIONS if name not in have]
   113	        if missing_options:
   114	            options = [{"id": o["id"], "name": o["name"], "color": o["color"] or "GRAY", "description": o["description"] or ""}
   115	                       for o in status["options"]]
   116	            for name in missing_options:
   117	                color, description = ADDED_STATUS_OPTIONS.get(name, ("GRAY", ""))
   118	                options.append({"name": name, "color": color, "description": description})
   119	            proposal = {"fieldId": status["id"], "options": options}
   120	    workflows = meta_project["workflows"]
   121	    enabled = {name for name, w in workflows.items() if w["enabled"]}
   122	    wf = {
   123	        "required_disabled": [n for n in REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS if n not in enabled],
   124	        "recommended_disabled": [n for n in RECOMMENDED_WORKFLOWS if n not in enabled],  # 一覧に無いものも無効として数える
   125	        "notice_enabled": [n for n in NOTICE_IF_ENABLED_WORKFLOWS if n in enabled],
   126	        "discouraged_enabled": [n for n in DISCOURAGED_WORKFLOWS if n in enabled],
   127	    }
   128	    field_create = []
   129	    for f in missing_fields:
   130	        if "problem" in f and not f.get("options"):
   131	            continue  # 型の違いは作り直しが要るので案を出さず、報告だけ
   132	        if "problem" in f:
   133	            continue  # 既にあるフィールドの値の追加は、案だけ (問題の文で報告)
   134	        cmd = ["project", "field-create", str(meta_project["number"]), "--owner", meta_project["owner"], "--name", f["name"],
   135	               "--data-type", f["data_type"]]
   136	        if f["options"]:
   137	            cmd += ["--single-select-options", ",".join(f["options"])]
   138	        field_create.append(cmd)
   139	    return {"ok": not missing_fields and not missing_options and not wf["required_disabled"],
   140	            "missing_fields": missing_fields, "missing_status_options": missing_options, "workflows": wf,
   141	            "proposals": {"field_create": field_create, "update_status_options": proposal}}

   144	def add_fields(meta_project, checked):
   145	    """check の案を実行する (承認を得た後に呼ぶ)。不足のフィールドを gh project field-create で作り、Status の選択肢を
   146	    既存の id を保って足す。返り値は実行ごとの結果の配列。"""
   147	    results = []
   148	    for cmd in checked["proposals"]["field_create"]:
   149	        r = gh.run(cmd, mutation=True, expect_json=False)
   150	        results.append({"action": "field-create", "args": cmd, "ok": r["failure"] is None, "failure": r["failure"], "stderr": r["stderr_tail"]})
   151	    proposal = checked["proposals"]["update_status_options"]
   152	    if proposal:
   153	        args = ["api", "graphql", "-f", f"query={load_query('update-status-options')}", "-F", f"fieldId={proposal['fieldId']}",
   154	                "-F", "options=" + json.dumps(proposal["options"], ensure_ascii=False)]
   155	        r = gh.run(args, mutation=True, expect_json=True)
   156	        ok = r["failure"] is None and isinstance(r["json"], dict) and not r["json"].get("errors")
   157	        results.append({"action": "update-status-options", "ok": ok, "failure": r["failure"],
   158	                        "stderr": r["stderr_tail"], "errors": (r["json"] or {}).get("errors") if isinstance(r["json"], dict) else None})
   159	    return results

   192	def _more_pages(name, repo, number, first_page, key, convert):
   193	    """コメントか出来事の続きのページを読んで、変換した要素の配列を返す。読めなければ問題を返す。"""
   194	    nodes = [convert(n) for n in first_page["nodes"] if n]
   195	    info = first_page.get("pageInfo") or {}
   196	    owner, _, repo_name = repo.partition("/")
   197	    while info.get("hasNextPage"):
   198	        data, problem = graphql(name, {"owner": owner, "name": repo_name, "number": number, "after": info.get("endCursor")})
   199	        if problem:
   200	            return nodes, problem
   201	        page = data["repository"]["issue"][key]
   202	        nodes += [convert(n) for n in page["nodes"] if n]
   203	        info = page.get("pageInfo") or {}
   204	    return nodes, None

   207	def simplify_item(node, position):
   208	    """GraphQL の項目を、後の単位が読む形にする。Issue 以外の項目 (draft issue・PR) は content を None にして返す。"""
   209	    content = node.get("content") or {}
   210	    fields = {}
   211	    status = None
   212	    for fv in node["fieldValues"]["nodes"]:
   213	        if not fv or not fv.get("field"):
   214	            continue
   215	        name = fv["field"]["name"]
   216	        if name == "Status":
   217	            status = {"name": fv.get("name"), "option_id": fv.get("optionId"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   218	        elif "text" in fv:
   219	            fields[name] = {"text": fv.get("text"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   220	        else:
   221	            fields[name] = {"name": fv.get("name"), "option_id": fv.get("optionId"), "updated_at": fv.get("updatedAt")}
   222	    item = {"item_id": node["id"], "position": position, "item_updated_at": node.get("updatedAt"), "status": status, "fields": fields,
   223	            "content_type": content.get("__typename"), "key": None}
   224	    if content.get("__typename") != "Issue":
   225	        return item, []
   226	    repo = content["repository"]["nameWithOwner"]
   227	    sub = content.get("subIssuesSummary") or {}
   228	    parent = content.get("parent")
   229	    item.update({
   230	        "key": _ref(content), "repo": repo, "number": content["number"], "url": content["url"], "title": content["title"],
   231	        "state": content["state"], "created_at": content.get("createdAt"), "author": (content.get("author") or {}).get("login"),
   232	        "visibility": content["repository"].get("visibility"), "in_organization": content["repository"].get("isInOrganization"),
   233	        "assignees": [a["login"] for a in content["assignees"]["nodes"]],
   234	        "labels": [l["name"] for l in content["labels"]["nodes"]],
   235	        "parent": _ref(parent) if parent and parent.get("repository") else None,
   236	        "sub_issues": {"total": sub.get("total", 0), "completed": sub.get("completed", 0)},
   237	        "is_parent": bool(sub.get("total")),
   238	        "blocked_by": [{"key": _ref(b), "url": b["url"], "state": b["state"]} for b in content["blockedBy"]["nodes"]],
   239	        "body_edits": [{"editor": (e.get("editor") or {}).get("login"), "edited_at": e.get("editedAt"), "deleted_at": e.get("deletedAt")}
   240	                       for e in content["userContentEdits"]["nodes"]],
   241	        "prs": [{"number": p["number"], "url": p["url"], "state": p["state"], "draft": p["isDraft"], "merged": p["merged"],
   242	                 "created_at": p.get("createdAt"), "merged_at": p.get("mergedAt"), "closed_at": p.get("closedAt"),
   243	                 "author": (p.get("author") or {}).get("login"), "base_ref": p.get("baseRefName")}
   244	                for p in content["closedByPullRequestsReferences"]["nodes"]],
   245	    })
   246	    problems = []
   247	    comments, problem = _more_pages("issue-comments", repo, content["number"], content["comments"], "comments", _comment)
   248	    if problem:
   249	        problems.append({"item": item["key"], "what": "comments", **problem})
   250	    events, problem = _more_pages("issue-timeline", repo, content["number"], content["timelineItems"], "timelineItems", _event)
   251	    if problem:
   252	        problems.append({"item": item["key"], "what": "events", **problem})
   253	    item["comments"] = comments
   254	    item["events"] = sorted(events, key=lambda e: (e.get("at") or "", EVENT_TYPES.index(e["type"]) if e["type"] in EVENT_TYPES else 99))
   255	    return item, problems

   258	def items(project):
   259	    """項目の一覧を位置の順に全部読む。返り値: {"status": "ok", "project_id", "items": [...], "problems": [...], "rate_limit"} か
   260	    {"status": "error", ...} (最初のページが読めないとき)。続きのページやコメントの続きが読めなかったときは problems に入れて止める。"""
   261	    result_items = []
   262	    problems = []
   263	    after = None
   264	    project_id = None
   265	    rate = None
   266	    position = 0
   267	    while True:
   268	        data, problem = graphql("items", {"owner": project["owner"], "number": project["number"], "after": after})
   269	        if problem:
   270	            if not result_items:
   271	                return {"status": "error", **problem}
   272	            problems.append({"what": "items-page", "after": after, **problem})
   273	            break
   274	        node = _project_node(data)
   275	        if node is None:
   276	            return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "message": f"Project {project['owner']}/{project['number']} が無いか読めない", "exit_code": 0}
   277	        project_id = node["id"]
   278	        rate = data.get("rateLimit")
   279	        for n in node["items"]["nodes"]:
   280	            if not n:
   281	                continue
   282	            position += 1
   283	            item, item_problems = simplify_item(n, position)
   284	            result_items.append(item)
   285	            problems += item_problems
   286	        info = node["items"].get("pageInfo") or {}
   287	        if not info.get("hasNextPage"):
   288	            break
   289	        after = info.get("endCursor")
   290	    return {"status": "ok" if not problems else "partial", "project_id": project_id, "items": result_items, "problems": problems, "rate_limit": rate}

   295	def set_status(meta_project, item_id, status):
   296	    """Status を書く。管理のセッションが書く 5 つ以外 (Done を含む) は gh を実行せずに拒否する (R2)。"""
   297	    if status not in MANAGER_STATUSES:
   298	        return {"status": "rejected", "message": f"Status {status!r} は書かない (書けるのは {', '.join(MANAGER_STATUSES)}。Done は組み込みワークフローが書く)"}
   299	    field = meta_project["fields"].get("Status")
   300	    option = next((o for o in (field or {}).get("options", []) if o["name"] == status), None)
   301	    if field is None or option is None:
   302	        return {"status": "rejected", "message": f"Project の Status に選択肢 {status!r} が無い (project check で足す)"}
   303	    r = gh.run(["project", "item-edit", "--project-id", meta_project["id"], "--id", item_id, "--field-id", field["id"],
   304	                "--single-select-option-id", option["id"]], mutation=True)
   305	    if r["failure"]:
   306	        return {"status": "error", "failure": r["failure"], "message": r["stderr_tail"]}
   307	    return {"status": "ok", "item_id": item_id, "field": "Status", "value": status}

| 作業のセッションの待機の費用 | `wait-assignment` 相当 (項目 100 件の `fieldValues`・`state`・`labels`・`blockedBy`・`comments(first:50)`) は 1 回 4、`wait-decision` 相当 (Issue 1 件のコメント・Status・閉じる参照の PR) は 1 回 1。3 分おきに作業のセッション 3 個が `wait-assignment` を動かしても 240 ポイント/時で、管理のセ
| 個人のリポジトリの Issue に組織のリポジトリの Issue を `blockedBy` で足す | `gh issue edit 3 -R akm/issue-dispatch-verify-a --add-blocked-by https://github.com/tecowl/lappds/issues/641` (組織 `tecowl` の private リポジトリ。利用者の権限は ADMIN) で足せた。`owner/repo#番号` の形は `gh` 2.102.0 が「invalid issue format」で受け付けず、URL �

## 止まる条件との照らし合わせ (項目 4 の範囲)

- (2) 書き込みの直後に読み直せない: 当たらない。5 種類とも 1 回目の読み取りで返った。
- (3) 組み込みワークフローを無効にしなければ成り立たない: 当たらない。有効なまま計測した。ただし「reopen で `Todo` になる」ワークフローはデフォルトには無いので、reopen した Issue の Status は `Done` のまま残る。計画の KTD19 の表と R24 がこの前提を使っていれば、U13 で「`Done` のまま開いている
- (4) 導出の出どころを読めない: 当たらない。Issue のタイムラインの出来事と閉じた PR (`includeClosedPrs:true`) を、項目の一覧と同じクエリで時刻付きで読めた。費用も収まる。
- (1) は項目 2 (セッション間の合図) で確かめる。

## まだ確かめていないこと

- 依存先のリポジトリで要る権限 (ADMIN で足せたことしか確かめていない。read 権限だけの組織のリポジトリを依存先にできるかは不明)。
- 版を消された編集 (`deletedAt` のある件) の見え方 (API に消す操作が無い)。

| 一覧のクエリの費用 (項目・フィールド・blocker・PR・コメント・タイムラインの出来事を入れ子で取る。`items_query.graphql`) | 項目 20 件で `rateLimit.cost` 1、50 件で 4、100 件で 7 (1 回の呼び出しで 100 件すべてを取れた。コメント `first:50`・タイムライン `first:100` で、2 ページ目が要る項目は無かった)。�
| 作業のセッションの待機の費用 | `wait-assignment` 相当 (項目 100 件の `fieldValues`・`state`・`labels`・`blockedBy`・`comments(first:50)`) は 1 回 4、`wait-decision` 相当 (Issue 1 件のコメント・Status・閉じる参照の PR) は 1 回 1。3 分おきに作業のセッション 3 個が `wait-assignment` を動かしても 240 ポイント/時で、管理のセ
| 個人のリポジトリの Issue に組織のリポジトリの Issue を `blockedBy` で足す | `gh issue edit 3 -R akm/issue-dispatch-verify-a --add-blocked-by https://github.com/tecowl/lappds/issues/641` (組織 `tecowl` の private リポジトリ。利用者の権限は ADMIN) で足せた。`owner/repo#番号` の形は `gh` 2.102.0 が「invalid issue format」で受け付けず、URL �

## 止まる条件との照らし合わせ (項目 4 の範囲)

- (2) 書き込みの直後に読み直せない: 当たらない。5 種類とも 1 回目の読み取りで返った。
- (3) 組み込みワークフローを無効にしなければ成り立たない: 当たらない。有効なまま計測した。ただし「reopen で `Todo` になる」ワークフローはデフォルトには無いので、reopen した Issue の Status は `Done` のまま残る。計画の KTD19 の表と R24 がこの前提を使っていれば、U13 で「`Done` のまま開いている
- (4) 導出の出どころを読めない: 当たらない。Issue のタイムラインの出来事と閉じた PR (`includeClosedPrs:true`) を、項目の一覧と同じクエリで時刻付きで読めた。費用も収まる。
- (1) は項目 2 (セッション間の合図) で確かめる。

## まだ確かめていないこと

- 依存先のリポジトリで要る権限 (ADMIN で足せたことしか確かめていない。read 権限だけの組織のリポジトリを依存先にできるかは不明)。
- 版を消された編集 (`deletedAt` のある件) の見え方 (API に消す操作が無い)。

content.content:
## 作り方 (`project check` と `project add-fields`)

`project check` は、フィールド 3 つの有無と型、`Agent stuck state` の値、Status の選択肢、ワークフローを確かめ、不足と作る手順の案を返す (読むだけ)。利用者の承認を得てから `project add-fields` が案を実行する。

- フィールドは `gh project field-create <番号> --owner <owner> --name <名前> --data-type TEXT|SINGLE_SELECT [--single-select-options <値,…>]` で作る。
- Status の選択肢は GraphQL の `updateProjectV2Field` (`singleSelectOptions`) で足す。**既存の選択肢を `id` 付きで含めて渡す** — 含めないと既存の値が消える (U1 で確かめた)。足す選択肢の色と説明: `Ready` は GREEN「着手してよい」、`In review` は BLUE「PR が ready for review」、`Blocked` は RED「ほかの Issue か小さな PR を待つ」。既存の項目の Status の値は変わらない。
- 既にあるフィールドの型が違うとき (`Agent stuck state` が単一選択でないなど) は作り直しが要るので、案を出さずに報告だけする。

## CLI

| サブコマンド | 入力 | 出力 (JSON) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project check --project <owner>/<番号>` | | `status`・`project` (`id`・`title`・`url`・`owner`・`number`)・`check` (`ok`・`missing_fields`・`missing_status_options`・`workflows` (`required_disabled`・`recommended_disabled`・`notice_enabled`・`discouraged_enabled`)・`proposals` (`field_create` の引数の配列と `update_status_options` の入力))・`rate_limit`・`errors` |
| `project items --project <owner>/<番号>` | | `status` (`ok` / `partial` 続きのページが読めなかった / `error`)・`project_id`・`items` (下の表)・`problems`・`rate_limit`・`errors` |
| `project set-status --project <owner>/<番号> --item <項目の ID> --status <値>` | 値は 5 つのどれか | `status` (`ok` / `rejected` / `error`)・`item_id`・`field`・`value`・`errors` |
        self.assertIn(",".join(project.STUCK_STATES), cmds[1])

    def test_add_fields_runs_proposals(self):
        """Covers AE21. add-fields は不足のフィールドを作り、Status の選択肢を既存の id を含めて足す。不足が無ければ何も実行しない。"""
        data = fixture_json("project-meta-ok")
        node = data["data"]["repositoryOwner"]["projectV2"]
        node["fields"]["nodes"] = [f for f in node["fields"]["nodes"] if f and f["name"] != "Agent session title"]
        status = next(f for f in node["fields"]["nodes"] if f["name"] == "Status")
        status["options"] = [o for o in status["options"] if o["name"] != "Blocked"]

## 作り方 (`project check` と `project add-fields`)

`project check` は、フィールド 3 つの有無と型、`Agent stuck state` の値、Status の選択肢、ワークフローを確かめ、不足と作る手順の案を返す (読むだけ)。利用者の承認を得てから `project add-fields` が案を実行する。

- フィールドは `gh project field-create <番号> --owner <owner> --name <名前> --data-type TEXT|SINGLE_SELECT [--single-select-options <値,…>]` で作る。
- Status の選択肢は GraphQL の `updateProjectV2Field` (`singleSelectOptions`) で足す。**既存の選択肢を `id` 付きで含めて渡す** — 含めないと既存の値が消える (U1 で確かめた)。足す選択肢の色と説明: `Ready` は GREEN「着手してよい」、`In review` は BLUE「PR が ready for review」、`Blocked` は RED「ほかの Issue か小さな PR を待つ」。既存の項目の Status の値は変わらない。
- 既にあるフィールドの型が違うとき (`Agent stuck state` が単一選択でないなど) は作り直しが要るので、案を出さずに報告だけする。

## CLI

| サブコマンド | 入力 | 出力 (JSON) |
| --- | --- | --- |

ブランチ `feat/issue-dispatch-u7-project-114` の全量 (`b504696..c051a54`) をレビューし、指摘は 4 件でした。

**ひとつ、私の誤りを報告します。** 確認用のスクリプトの 1 回目で、偽の gh の置き場として PATH に存在しないディレクトリを書いてしまいました。そのため、偽物ではなく本物の gh が、利用者の認証で GraphQL のクエリ `ProjectMeta` を 1 回実行しました。
- 実行されたのは、Project `akm/3` のフィールドとワークフローを読む読み取りのクエリだけです (`rateLimit` の cost は 1)。
- mutation・`field-create`・`item-edit` などの書き込みは実行されていません。
- 2 回目以降は、偽の gh に届いたことを、偽の gh が受けた引数を書き出すファイル (環境変数 `FAKE_GH_ARGS` で指定) で確かめています。
- この件は YAML の `attrs.probe_incident` に記録しました。

**結果のファイル:** `tmp/review-20261022-0708-feat-issue-dispatch-u7-project-114-1-code-review-opus.yaml`

**レビューの実行**
- Skill ツールで code-review を、引数 `high b504696..c051a54` で呼びました。
- effort は `high` を渡しました。
- モデルはこのセッションの opus です。code-review は sub-agent を使わずにこの文脈で進める手順なので、モデルを別に渡す場所はありませんでした。
- ReportFindings も呼び、同じ 4 件を渡しました。

**指摘**
1. **P2・confidence medium** — ファイル `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/project.py` の L154
   - 関数 `add_fields` は、Status の選択肢を `-F options=<JSON の文字列>` で渡しています。
   - gh 2.102.0 の `gh api --help` によると、`-F` が型を変換するのは `true`・`false`・`null`・整数と、`@` で始まるファイルだけです。そのため、配列を期待する GraphQL の変数に文字列が届き、GitHub では選択肢を足せないと考えられます。
   - 本物の GitHub では確かめていません。テストは、偽の gh が受けた引数の文字列を見ているだけです。
2. **P3** — 同じファイルの L130
   - 関数 `check` は、フィールド `Agent stuck state` の値の不足を報告しますが、それを直す手順の案を作りません。
   - そのため、`project add-fields` を実行してもこの不足は直らず、`check` の `ok` は偽のままです。
   - 値を 1 つ除いたデータで `check` を呼んで確かめました。
3. **P3** — ファイル `graphql/items.graphql` の L35
   - 項目の一覧のクエリでは、入れ子の connection (`fieldValues`・`labels`・`blockedBy`・`userContentEdits` など) が `pageInfo` を取っていません。
   - さらに、取っている `userContentEdits` の `totalCount` は捨てられています。
   - そのため、最初のページ (30 件など) を超えた値が、何の知らせもなく欠けます。
4. **P3・confidence low** — ファイル `project.py` の L59
   - 関数 `graphql()` は、応答に `data` があっても、`errors` があれば全体を失敗として扱います。
   - 偽の gh に、SAML の FORBIDDEN のエラーとデータを一緒に返させると、関数 `read_meta` は `error` になりました。
   - 本物の GitHub が SAML の組織の Issue に対してこの形で返すかどうかは確かめていません。

**`residual` に入れたもの (4 件)**
- 関数 `items()` は、2 ページ目以降で Project が読めないと、それまでに読んだ項目を捨てます。
- 名前の正規表現の文字列が 3 か所にあります。
- CLI の `set-status` は、書ける Status の検査を関数 `set_status` と重ねて持っています。
- 関数 `_more_pages` は、Issue が null だと例外で終わります。

**テスト**
- 153 件すべて成功しました。

**作業ツリー**
- HEAD はレビューの前後とも c051a54 です。
- `git status --porcelain` と `git status --porcelain --ignored issue-dispatch` は、どちらも何も出しませんでした。
- `__pycache__` は作られていません。
- 確認のためのファイルは scratchpad にだけ作りました。作業ツリーに作ったのは結果の YAML の 1 つだけで、コミットはしていません。

Review target: `a583863..8528090`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

content.text:
Review target: `f9995ce..5e7aa72`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like

produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.

1	# Issue の様式
     2	
     3	このファイルが、この仕組み (issue-dispatch) が扱う Issue と PR の様式の正本。管理のセッションと作業のセッションが Issue のどこを読み、どこに何を書くかをここで決める。Project のフィールドと Status の様式は [project-schema.md](project-schema.md)、リポジトリの設定は [project-config.md](project-config.md) が�
     4	
     5	## Issue が持つもの
     6	
     7	| 項目 | 書き方 | 誰が書くか | 読み方 |
     8	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
     9	| 依存関係 | GitHub の Issue の blocked by (`blockedBy`) | 利用者。この仕組みも足す (下の「`blockedBy` の追加」) | 項目の一覧 (`project items`) の `blocked_by` に、blocker ごとの開閉が付く。開いた blocker があれば着手しない |
    10	| 必要な資源 | ラベル `resource:<名前>` (例: `resource:staging-db`) | 利用者。この仕組みも、利用者の承認を得て足す (下の「ラベルの追加」) | 同じ資源のラベルを持つ Issue は同時に 1 つだけ進める |
    11	| 人が行う Issue | ラベル `human-handed` を付けるか、担当者をほかの人にする | 利用者 | 割り当ての対象にしない |
    12	| 担当者 (assignee) | 認証しているアカウント (`gh` のトークンのログイン) 1 つだけ | 利用者 | `human-handed` が無く、担当者がトークンのログイン 1 つだけの Issue が、作業のセッションの対象になる。担当者が未設定の Issue は対象にならないので、`Ready` にする前に担当者を決める |
    13	| 親 Issue | sub-issue を持つ Issue | 利用者 | 親 Issue は割り当ての対象にしない (sub-issue は対象にする)。項目の一覧の `is_parent` |
    14	| 大きさ | 1 つの PR で閉じる大きさ | 利用者 | 作る時点で分ける規則は定めない。着手の後に分ける必要が分かったときの扱いは「分割で作る Issue」 |
    15	| PR との結び付き | PR の本文に Issue を閉じる記法 (`Closes #<番号>`) | 作業のセッション | マージで Issue が閉じ、`Done` と資源の解放がそれに続く (`Done` を書く組み込みワークフローの正本は [project-schema.md](project-schema.md) の「組み込みワークフロー」)。PR の側から読むのは `closingIssuesReferences` (下�
    16	
    17	## `blockedBy` の追加 (`blocked-by add`)
    18	
    19	`gh issue edit <Issue の URL> --add-blocked-by <blocker の URL>` で足す。`--add-blocked-by` は URL の形だけを受け付ける (番号だけや `owner/repo#番号` は受け付けない。U1 の実測) ので、CLI は参照 (`owner/repo#番号` か URL) を URL に直してから渡す。
    20	
    21	失敗 (blocker が無い・権限が無い・レート制限など) は理由付きの JSON (`status: error`・`failure`・`message`・`exit_code`) で返し、CLI は再試行しない。再試行するかは呼び出し元のスキルが決める。自分が足した `blockedBy` の削除は U13 で足す (自分が足したものかの導出が要るため)。
    22	
    23	## ラベルの追加 (`issue add-label`)
    24	
    25	利用者の承認を得た後に呼ぶ (承認なしに行う操作ではない)。手順は次の順で、途中で失敗すればそこで止めて理由を返す。
    26	
    27	1. `gh issue view <URL> --json labels` で、既に付いていれば何もしない (`added: false`)。
    28	2. `gh label list` でリポジトリにラベルが無ければ、`gh label create <名前> [--description <説明>]` で作る (`label_created: true`)。色は `gh` のデフォルトに任せる (この仕組みは色を決めない)。説明は呼び出し元が任意で渡す。
    29	3. `gh issue edit <URL> --add-label <名前>` で足す (`added: true`)。
    30	
    31	## 分割で作る Issue (`issue create`)
    32	
    33	着手の後に Issue を分ける必要が分かったとき (計画の R20) に、分けた部分を新しい Issue にする。新しい Issue は次の様式で作る。
    34	
    35	- **本文の先頭行** は `split-from: <宣言のコメントの URL>`。URL は `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<番号>#issuecomment-<コメントの id>` の形で、分割の元の Issue と宣言のコメントの両方を指す (GitHub ではリンクとして表示される)。先頭行の後に空行を 1 つ挟み、呼び出し元が渡した本文を続ける。
    36	- **同じ先頭行を持つ開いた Issue が既にあれば作らず、その番号を返す** (`created: false`)。管理のセッションが途中で止まって再開したときに、同じ分割で 2 つ作らないため。比べるのは先頭行の文字列の完全一致で、開いた Issue の一覧 (`gh issue list --state open`) が読めなければ作らない (既にあ�
    37	- Status と sub-issue の関係は書かない。進行中の Issue の sub-issue にはしない (親 Issue は割り当ての対象から外れるため)。ラベルと担当者は、呼び出し元が渡したものをそのまま付ける。
    38	
    39	## PR の観測 (`pr observe`)
    40	
    41	PR の URL を受けて読むだけで、書き込みは無い。`PR の報告` と `小さな PR の報告` (コメントの様式は U8) に書かれた PR と、項目の一覧の `prs` にある PR に使う。読むのは GraphQL (`graphql/pr-observe.graphql`) で、PR の状態・draft・作者・`closingIssuesReferences` (参照する Issue とその開閉)・変えたファイルの
    42	
    43	**作者 (`author.login`) がトークンのログイン (`gh api user`) と違う PR は、無いものとして扱う** (種類 `other_author`。中身 `pr` は返さず、`author` だけを返す)。公開リポジトリでは第三者も PR を作れるので、本文の `Closes` やコメントの URL だけでこの仕組みの PR とは見なさない。
    44	
    45	| 種類 (`kind`) | 条件 | 管理のセッションがすること |
    46	| --- | --- | --- |
    47	| `other_author` | 作者がトークンのログインと違う | 無いものとして扱う |
    48	| `draft` | 開いていて draft | `In review` にしない |
    49	| `needs_closing_reference` | 開いていて draft ではなく、参照する Issue が無い | 本文に `Closes #<番号>` を足すよう作業のセッションに頼む (本文の追記が要る) |
    50	| `in_review` | 開いていて draft ではなく、参照する Issue がある | Status を `In review` にする |
    51	| `merged` | マージ済みで、参照する Issue がすべて閉じている | 何もしない (`Done` の書き手は [project-schema.md](project-schema.md) の「Status の選択肢」) |
    52	| `merged_issue_open` | マージ済みなのに、参照する Issue に開いたものがある | 書き込まず、利用者に知らせる (組み込みワークフローが無効か、参照が適用されなかった) |
    53	| `closed` | マージせずに閉じた | 作業のセッションに確かめる |
    54	
    55	出力の `pr` のキー: `number`・`title`・`url`・`state` (`OPEN` / `MERGED` / `CLOSED`)・`draft`・`created_at`・`merged_at`・`closed_at`・`author`・`base_ref`・`head_ref`・`issues` (参照する Issue の配列。要素は `key` (`owner/repo#番号`)・`number`・`url`・`state`)・`issues_truncated` (参照が 50 を超えて一部しか読めていない)・`files` (変え�
    56	
    57	## CLI
    58	
    59	| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
    60	| --- | --- | --- |
    61	| `issue create --repo <owner/name> --title <題> (--body <本文> \| --body-file <ファイル \| ->) --split-from <宣言のコメントの URL> [--label <名前>]... [--assignee <ログイン>]...` | `gh issue create` (既にあれば無し) | `created`・`number`・`url` |
    62	| `issue add-label --issue <参照> --label <名前> [--description <説明>]` | `gh label create` (無ければ)・`gh issue edit --add-label` (付いていなければ) | `label_created`・`added` |
    63	| `blocked-by add --issue <参照> --blocker <参照>` | `gh issue edit --add-blocked-by` | `issue`・`blocker` (キー) |
    64	| `pr observe --url <PR の URL>` | 無し | `kind`・`pr`・`author`・`rate_limit`・`warnings` |
    65	
    66	`<参照>` は `owner/repo#番号` か Issue の URL。どのサブコマンドも JSON を出せれば終了コード 0 で、失敗は `status: error` と `errors` (`key`・`message`・`failure`) で伝える。参照や URL の形が読めないときは `gh` を実行せずに返す。
-| `In review` | 管理のセッション | 今の割り当ての PR が draft でなく開いていて、Issue を閉じる参照を持つ |
+| `In review` | 管理のセッション | 今の割り当ての PR の観測の種類が `in_review` (条件の正本は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「PR の観測」) |
 | `Blocked` | 管理のセッション・利用者 | ほかの Issue か小さな PR を待つ |
 | `Done` | 組み込みワークフロー (管理のセッションは書かない) | Issue が閉じた |
