content.text:
Review target: `5e7aa72..b57c619`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or

Review target: `5e7aa72..b57c619`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the

stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `17d3247..49c3f29`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1	"""Issue のコメント。先頭行 (書いたセッションの種類と識別子とコメントの種類と値。R6) の生成と解析、コメントの一覧 (書き手が
     2	トークンのログインと違うものを除く)、投稿 (同じ出来事への同じコメントが既にあれば投稿しない。KTD2)、小さな PR の報告と依頼の
     3	対応づけ。様式の正本は issue-dispatch/skills/issue-dispatch/references/issue-format.md の「コメント」。
     4	
     5	読むのは GraphQL (graphql/issue-comments.graphql。実行は project.graphql) と `gh api user`、書くのは `gh issue comment <URL>
     6	--body-file -` (本文を標準入力で渡す。gh.run の mutation=True)。
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import re
    10	
    11	from issue_dispatch import gh, ids
    12	from issue_dispatch.project import graphql
    13	
    14	PREFIX = "issue-dispatch"
    15	SEP = " | "
    16	ROLES = {"manager": "管理のセッション", "worker": "作業のセッション"}
    17	_ROLE_OF = {v: k for k, v in ROLES.items()}
    18	MANAGER_KINDS = ("割り当て", "開始可", "待機", "解放", "引き継ぎ", "停滞", "依存の待ち", "依存の解消", "依頼")
    19	WORKER_KINDS = ("着手の宣言", "宣言の更新", "小さな PR の報告", "PR の報告")
    20	# 宛先 (対象) と割り当ての番号を持つ種類
    21	ADDRESSED_KINDS = ("割り当て", "開始可", "待機", "解放", "停滞", "依頼")
    22	REQUEST_KINDS = ("宣言の書き直し", "本文の追記", "小さな PR")
    23	RELEASE_REASONS = ("解除", "close", "ID の変更", "除去")
    24	WAIT_KINDS = ("利用者の答え", "Issue", "小さな PR", "資源", "設定")
    25	# 先頭行の値の見出し語 (値は `<見出し語> <値>` の 1 区切り)。解析は右からこの語で始まる区切りを値として取る
    26	VALUE_WORDS = ("対象", "割り当て", "宣言", "種類", "待つ Issue", "待つ側の宣言", "前の PR", "PR", "理由", "値", "Issue")
    27	
    28	# 種類ごとに持つ値 (キー) と並び。waits と blockers は配列で、1 要素 1 区切り
    29	_SHAPE = {
    30	    "割り当て": ("to", "assignment"),
    31	    "開始可": ("to", "assignment", "declaration"),
    32	    "待機": ("to", "assignment", "declaration", "waits"),
    33	    "解放": ("to", "assignment", "release_reason"),
    34	    "停滞": ("to", "assignment", "stuck_state"),
    35	    "依頼": ("to", "assignment", "request_kind"),  # 種類ごとの値は _REQUEST_SHAPE
    36	    "引き継ぎ": (),
    37	    "依存の待ち": ("blockers",),
    38	    "依存の解消": (),
    39	    "着手の宣言": (),
    40	    "宣言の更新": (),
    41	    "小さな PR の報告": ("waiting_issue", "waiting_declaration", "previous_pr?"),
    42	    "PR の報告": (),
    43	}
    44	_REQUEST_SHAPE = {"宣言の書き直し": ("declaration",), "本文の追記": ("pr",), "小さな PR": ("waiting_issue", "waiting_declaration", "previous_pr?")}
    45	_WORD_OF = {"to": "対象", "assignment": "割り当て", "declaration": "宣言", "request_kind": "種類", "waiting_issue": "待つ Issue",
    46	            "waiting_declaration": "待つ側の宣言", "previous_pr": "前の PR", "pr": "PR", "release_reason": "理由", "stuck_state": "値",
    47	            "waits": "理由", "blockers": "Issue"}
    48	_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[1-9][0-9]*$")
    49	
    50	
    51	def _shape(kind, request_kind=None):
    52	    keys = list(_SHAPE[kind])
    53	    if kind == "依頼" and request_kind in _REQUEST_SHAPE:
    54	        keys += _REQUEST_SHAPE[request_kind]
    55	    return keys
    56	
    57	
    58	# --- 値の正規化と検査 ------------------------------------------------------------
    59	
    60	def _issue_ref(value, what):
    61	    key = ids.issue_key(value)
    62	    if key is None:
    63	        raise ValueError(f"{what} は Issue の参照 (owner/repo#番号 か URL) で書く: {value!r}")
    64	    return key
    65	
    66	
    67	def _pr_url(value, what):
    68	    parsed = ids.parse_pr_url(value)
    69	    if parsed is None:
    70	        raise ValueError(f"{what} は PR の URL で書く: {value!r}")
    71	    return parsed["url"]
    72	
    73	
    74	def _comment_id(value, what):
    75	    text = str(value).strip()
    76	    if not _ID_RE.match(text):
    77	        raise ValueError(f"{what} はコメントの ID (URL の末尾 #issuecomment-<数値> の数値) で書く: {value!r}")
    78	    return int(text)
    79	
    80	
    81	def _wait(item):
    82	    if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("kind") not in WAIT_KINDS:
    83	        raise ValueError(f"待つ理由は {', '.join(WAIT_KINDS)} のどれか: {item!r}")
    84	    kind = item["kind"]
    85	    out = {"kind": kind}
    86	    if kind == "Issue":
    87	        out["issue"] = _issue_ref(item.get("issue"), "待つ Issue")
    88	    elif kind == "小さな PR":
    89	        out["issue"] = _issue_ref(item.get("issue"), "小さな PR の依頼先の Issue")
    90	        if item.get("pr") is not None:
    91	            out["pr"] = _pr_url(item["pr"], "小さな PR")
    92	    elif kind == "資源":
    93	        name = item.get("resource")
    94	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip() or SEP in name:
    95	            raise ValueError(f"資源の名前が無いか、区切り文字を含む: {name!r}")
    96	        out["resource"] = name.strip()
    97	    return out
    98	
    99	
   100	def normalize_values(kind, values):
   101	    """種類に合わせて値をそろえ、検査する。返り値はそろえた値 (dict)。足りない・余分・形が違えば ValueError。"""
   102	    values = dict(values or {})
   103	    if kind not in _SHAPE:
   104	        raise ValueError(f"コメントの種類ではない: {kind!r}")
   105	    request_kind = values.get("request_kind")
   106	    if kind == "依頼" and request_kind not in REQUEST_KINDS:
   107	        raise ValueError(f"依頼の種類は {', '.join(REQUEST_KINDS)} のどれか: {request_kind!r}")
   108	    keys = _shape(kind, request_kind)
   109	    required = [k.rstrip("?") for k in keys if not k.endswith("?")]
   110	    allowed = [k.rstrip("?") for k in keys]
   111	    extra = [k for k, v in values.items() if k not in allowed and v not in (None, [], ())]
   112	    if extra:
   113	        raise ValueError(f"種類 {kind} は値 {', '.join(extra)} を持たない")
   114	    missing = [k for k in required if values.get(k) in (None, [], ())]
   115	    if missing:
   116	        raise ValueError(f"種類 {kind} に値 {', '.join(missing)} が無い")
   117	    out = {}
   118	    for key in allowed:
   119	        v = values.get(key)
   120	        if v in (None, [], ()):
   121	            continue
   122	        if key == "to":
   123	            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v.strip() or SEP in v:
   124	                raise ValueError(f"対象 (作業のセッションの ID) が無いか、区切り文字を含む: {v!r}")
   125	            out[key] = v.strip()
   126	        elif key == "assignment":
   127	            if not _ID_RE.match(str(v).strip()):
   128	                raise ValueError(f"割り当ての番号は 1 以上の整数: {v!r}")
   129	            out[key] = int(str(v).strip())
   130	        elif key in ("declaration", "waiting_declaration"):
   131	            out[key] = _comment_id(v, _WORD_OF[key])
   132	        elif key == "request_kind":
   133	            out[key] = v
   134	        elif key == "waiting_issue":
   135	            out[key] = _issue_ref(v, "待つ Issue")
   136	        elif key in ("previous_pr", "pr"):
   137	            out[key] = _pr_url(v, _WORD_OF[key])
   138	        elif key == "release_reason":
   139	            if v not in RELEASE_REASONS:
   140	                raise ValueError(f"解放の理由は {', '.join(RELEASE_REASONS)} のどれか: {v!r}")
   141	            out[key] = v
   142	        elif key == "stuck_state":
   143	            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v.strip() or SEP in v:
   144	                raise ValueError(f"停滞の値が無いか、区切り文字を含む: {v!r}")
   145	            out[key] = v.strip()
   146	        elif key == "waits":
   147	            out[key] = [_wait(w) for w in v]
   148	        elif key == "blockers":
   149	            out[key] = [_issue_ref(b, "待つ Issue") for b in v]
   150	    return out
   151	
   152	
   153	# --- 先頭行の生成 ----------------------------------------------------------------
   154	
   155	def _wait_text(w):
   156	    if w["kind"] == "Issue":
   157	        return f"Issue {w['issue']}"
   158	    if w["kind"] == "小さな PR":
   159	        return f"小さな PR {w['issue']}" + (f" PR {w['pr']}" if w.get("pr") else "")
   160	    if w["kind"] == "資源":
   161	        return f"資源 {w['resource']}"
   162	    return w["kind"]
   163	
   164	
   165	def _value_fields(kind, values):
   166	    fields = []
   167	    for key in _shape(kind, values.get("request_kind")):
   168	        key = key.rstrip("?")
   169	        v = values.get(key)
   170	        if v is None:
   171	            continue
   172	        word = _WORD_OF[key]
   173	        if key == "waits":
   174	            fields += [f"{word} {_wait_text(w)}" for w in v]
   175	        elif key == "blockers":
   176	            fields += [f"{word} {b}" for b in v]
   177	        else:
   178	            fields.append(f"{word} {v}")
   179	    return fields
   180	
   181	
   182	def format_header(role, name, session_id, kind, values=None):
   183	    """先頭行を作る。role は manager / worker。値の形は normalize_values。名前は区切り文字を含んでもよい (解析は右から読む) が、
   184	    セッション ID は含めない。種類が役割のものでない・値が足りないなどは ValueError。"""
   185	    if role not in ROLES:
   186	        raise ValueError(f"役割は manager か worker: {role!r}")
   187	    if kind not in (MANAGER_KINDS if role == "manager" else WORKER_KINDS):
   188	        raise ValueError(f"種類 {kind!r} は {ROLES[role]}のコメントではない")
   189	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip() or "\n" in name:
   190	        raise ValueError(f"セッションの名前が無いか、改行を含む: {name!r}")
   191	    if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id.strip() or SEP in session_id or "\n" in session_id or session_id.strip() in _SHAPE:
   192	        raise ValueError(f"セッション ID が無いか、区切り文字か改行を含むか、種類の語と同じ: {session_id!r}")
   193	    normalized = normalize_values(kind, values)
   194	    return SEP.join([PREFIX, ROLES[role], name.strip(), session_id.strip(), kind] + _value_fields(kind, normalized))
   195	
   196	
   197	# --- 先頭行の解析 ----------------------------------------------------------------
   198	
   199	def _split_value(field):
   200	    """区切り 1 つを (見出し語, 値) にする。見出し語で始まらなければ None。長い語 (`待つ Issue`) を先に試す。"""
   201	    for word in sorted(VALUE_WORDS, key=len, reverse=True):
   202	        if field.startswith(word + " "):
   203	            return word, field[len(word) + 1:]
   204	    return None
   205	
   206	
   207	def _parse_wait(text):
   208	    for kind in ("利用者の答え", "設定"):
   209	        if text == kind:
   210	            return {"kind": kind}
   211	    if text.startswith("Issue "):
   212	        return {"kind": "Issue", "issue": text[len("Issue "):]}
   213	    if text.startswith("小さな PR "):
   214	        rest = text[len("小さな PR "):]
   215	        issue, _, pr = rest.partition(" PR ")
   216	        out = {"kind": "小さな PR", "issue": issue}
   217	        if pr:
   218	            out["pr"] = pr
   219	        return out
   220	    if text.startswith("資源 "):
   221	        return {"kind": "資源", "resource": text[len("資源 "):]}
   222	    raise ValueError(f"待つ理由の形ではない: {text!r}")
   223	
   224	
   225	def parse_wait_reason(text):
   226	    """`理由 ` の後の文字列 (`利用者の答え` / `Issue <参照>` / `小さな PR <参照> [PR <URL>]` / `資源 <名前>` / `設定`) を
   227	    待つ理由の dict にする。CLI の --reason も同じ形。形が違えば ValueError。"""
   228	    return _wait(_parse_wait(text.strip()))
   229	
   230	
   231	def parse_header(line):
   232	    """先頭行を読む。返り値は {"role", "name", "session_id", "kind", "values"} か、先頭行の形でなければ None。
   233	
   234	    右から読む: 値の見出し語で始まる区切りを値として取り、次が種類、その前がセッション ID、残りがすべて名前。名前が
   235	    区切り文字を含んでもよいのはこのため (セッション ID は含まない前提)。値の形が種類に合わなければ None。
   236	    """
   237	    if not isinstance(line, str) or "\n" in line:
   238	        return None
   239	    fields = line.rstrip().split(SEP)
   240	    if len(fields) < 5 or fields[0] != PREFIX or fields[1] not in _ROLE_OF:
   241	        return None
   242	    role = _ROLE_OF[fields[1]]
   243	    value_fields = []
   244	    index = len(fields) - 1
   245	    while index >= 4 and fields[index] not in _SHAPE and _split_value(fields[index]) is not None:
   246	        value_fields.insert(0, _split_value(fields[index]))
   247	        index -= 1
   248	    if index < 4 or fields[index] not in _SHAPE:
   249	        return None
   250	    kind = fields[index]
   251	    if kind not in (MANAGER_KINDS if role == "manager" else WORKER_KINDS):
   252	        return None
   253	    session_id = fields[index - 1]
   254	    name = SEP.join(fields[2:index - 1])
   255	    if not name or not session_id:
   256	        return None
   257	    raw = {}
   258	    try:
   259	        for word, text in value_fields:
   260	            if word == "理由" and kind == "待機":
   261	                raw.setdefault("waits", []).append(_parse_wait(text))
   262	            elif word == "理由" and kind == "解放":
   263	                raw["release_reason"] = text
   264	            elif word == "Issue" and kind == "依存の待ち":
   265	                raw.setdefault("blockers", []).append(text)
   266	            else:
   267	                key = next((k for k, w in _WORD_OF.items() if w == word and k not in ("waits", "blockers", "release_reason")), None)
   268	                if key is None or key in raw:
   269	                    return None
   270	                raw[key] = text
   271	        values = normalize_values(kind, raw)
   272	    except ValueError:
   273	        return None
   274	    return {"role": role, "name": name, "session_id": session_id, "kind": kind, "values": values}
   275	
   276	
   277	def split_body(body):
   278	    """コメントの本文を (先頭行の解析結果か None, 先頭行と空行を除いた本文) にする。先頭行の形でなければ本文はそのまま。"""
   279	    text = body or ""
   280	    first, _, rest = text.partition("\n")
   281	    parsed = parse_header(first)
   282	    if parsed is None:
   283	        return None, text
   284	    return parsed, rest.lstrip("\n")
   285	
   286	
   287	# --- 一覧 -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   288	
   289	def token_login():
   290	    r = gh.run(["api", "user"], expect_json=True)
   291	    login = (r["json"] or {}).get("login") if isinstance(r["json"], dict) else None
   292	    if r["failure"] or not login:
   293	        return None, {"status": "error", "failure": r["failure"] or "other", "exit_code": r["exit_code"],
   294	                      "message": r["stderr_tail"] or r.get("json_error") or "gh api user でログインを読めない"}
   295	    return login, None
   296	
   297	
   298	def list_comments(issue, login=None):
   299	    """Issue のコメントを時刻の順に全部読む。書き手がトークンのログイン (login。None なら `gh api user`) と違うコメントは除く
   300	    (R6。公開リポジトリでは第三者も書けるため)。返り値: {"status": "ok", "login", "comments": [{id, database_id, url,
   301	    created_at, author, header (parse_header の結果か None), body (先頭行を除いた本文)}], "excluded" (除いた件数), "rate_limit"}
   302	    か失敗の説明。"""
   303	    ref = ids.parse_issue_ref(issue)
   304	    if ref is None:
   305	        return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "exit_code": None, "message": f"Issue の参照ではない: {issue!r}"}
   306	    if login is None:
   307	        login, problem = token_login()
   308	        if problem:
   309	            return problem
   310	    owner, _, name = ref["repo"].partition("/")
   311	    nodes, after, rate_limit = [], None, None
   312	    while True:
   313	        data, problem, errors = graphql("issue-comments", {"owner": owner, "name": name, "number": ref["number"], "after": after})
   314	        if problem:
   315	            return {"status": "error", **problem}
   316	        issue_node = (data.get("repository") or {}).get("issue")
   317	        if not issue_node or errors:
   318	            return {"status": "error", "failure": "other", "exit_code": 0,
   319	                    "message": f"Issue {ref['key']} のコメントを読めない: {errors!r}"}
   320	        page = issue_node["comments"]
   321	        nodes += [n for n in page["nodes"] if n]
   322	        rate_limit = data.get("rateLimit") or rate_limit
   323	        info = page.get("pageInfo") or {}
   324	        if not info.get("hasNextPage"):
   325	            break
   326	        after = info.get("endCursor")
   327	    out, excluded = [], 0
   328	    for n in sorted(nodes, key=lambda n: (n.get("createdAt") or "", n.get("databaseId") or 0)):
   329	        if (n.get("author") or {}).get("login") != login:
   330	            excluded += 1
   331	            continue
   332	        header, body = split_body(n.get("body"))
   333	        out.append({"id": n["id"], "database_id": n.get("databaseId"), "url": n.get("url"), "created_at": n.get("createdAt"),
   334	                    "author": login, "header": header, "body": body})
   335	    return {"status": "ok", "login": login, "comments": out, "excluded": excluded, "rate_limit": rate_limit}
   336	
   337	
   338	# --- 既投稿の見分けと投稿 ---------------------------------------------------------
   339	
   340	def header_key(parsed):
   341	    """同じ出来事かを比べるための鍵。名前は比べない (変わりうる)。書き手の ID・種類・値を比べる。"""
   342	    return (parsed["role"], parsed["session_id"], parsed["kind"], _freeze(parsed["values"]))
   343	
   344	
   345	def _freeze(value):
   346	    if isinstance(value, dict):
   347	        return tuple(sorted((k, _freeze(v)) for k, v in value.items()))
   348	    if isinstance(value, list):
   349	        return tuple(_freeze(v) for v in value)
   350	    return value
   351	
   352	
   353	def already_posted(parsed, own_comments):
   354	    """同じ出来事への同じコメントが既にあればそのコメント (list_comments の要素) を、無ければ None を返す (KTD2)。
   355	
   356	    own_comments は list_comments が返した、書き手が自分のコメントの配列 (時刻の順)。種類ごとの規則:
   357	    `待機` は同じ宣言への最新の `待機` とだけ比べる。`依存の待ち` は最新の `依存の待ち` と比べ、間に `依存の解消` があれば
   358	    投稿する。`依存の解消` は最新の `依存の待ち` より後のコメントとだけ比べる。`停滞` は同じ対象・割り当て・値なら、間に
   359	    別のコメントがあっても既投稿。ほかの種類は、先頭行の鍵 (header_key) が同じコメントがあれば既投稿。
   360	    """
   361	    kind = parsed["kind"]
   362	    key = header_key(parsed)
   363	    headed = [c for c in own_comments if c.get("header")]
   364	    if kind == "待機":

+### 既投稿の見分け (`comment post`)
+
+投稿の前に、同じ出来事への同じコメントが既に無いことを確かめる (冪等。やり直しで同じ出来事をもう一度書こうとしたときに二重に書かないため)。同じ出来事かは、先頭行の書き手のセッション ID・種類・値で見分け、**名前は比べない** (名前は変わりうる)。種類ごとの規則:

+| --- | --- | --- |

+| ほか | 全部のコメント | 先頭行 (名前を除く) が同じ。宛先・割り当ての番号・宣言の ID・依頼の PR・待つ Issue が違えば投稿する |

+## コメント
+
+管理のセッションと作業のセッションは、Issue への書き込みの理由と宣言を Issue のコメントに書く。コメントは人にも見え、記録を失っても GitHub から復元できる。**先頭行で、書いたセッションの種類と識別子とコメントの種類を見分ける** (計画の R6・KTD2)。
+
+### 先頭行
+
+```
+issue-dispatch | <管理のセッション | 作業のセッション> | <セッションの名前> | <セッション ID> | <種類> | <値>...
+```
+
+- 区切りは ` | ` (前後に空白 1 つ)。値は `<見出し語> <値>` を 1 区切りに 1 つ書き、種類ごとに決まった並びで続ける (下の表)。先頭行の後に空行を 1 つ挟み、本文を続ける。
+- **解析は右から読む。** 見出し語で始まる区切りを値として取り、次が種類、その前がセッション ID、残りがすべて名前。セッションの名前は ` | ` を含んでもよいが、セッション ID は ` | ` を含まず、種類の語とも同じにしない。
+- 例 (管理のセッション): `issue-dispatch | 管理のセッション | mgr | M-1 | 開始可 | 対象 W-7 | 割り当て 1 | 宣言 6262508430`
+- 例 (作業のセッション): `issue-dispatch | 作業のセッション | worker 1 | W-7 | 小さな PR の報告 | 待つ Issue akm/repo#5 | 待つ側の宣言 777`
+- 先頭行の形をしていても、**書き手 (`author.login`) がトークンのログイン (`gh api user`) と違うコメントは、この仕組みのコメントとして扱わない** (一覧から除き、既投稿の確認にも数えない)。公開リポジトリでは第三者もコメントを書けるので、先頭行の形だけで受け入れると、第三者の 1 件のコメントで競合の可能性の判定を省いて作業を始めさせる・正規のコメントを既投稿と見せて書かせない、ができてしまう。この仕組みのセッションは
+
+### 値の見出し語
+
+| 見出し語 | 値 | 書き方 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `対象 ` | 宛先 (作業のセッションの ID) | ` | ` を含まない文字列 |
+| `割り当て ` | 割り当ての番号 (その Issue で何回目の割り当てか。1 から数える) | 1 以上の整数 |
+| `宣言 ` | 判定した宣言のコメントの ID | コメントの URL の末尾 `#issuecomment-<数値>` の数値 (REST の `id`、GraphQL の `databaseId`)。人がコメントの URL から見つけられ、分割で作る Issue の先頭行の URL と同じ数値 |
+| `種類 ` | 依頼の種類 | `宣言の書き直し` / `本文の追記` / `小さな PR` |
+| `待つ Issue ` | 小さな PR を待つほうの Issue | Issue の参照 (`owner/repo#番号`。URL で書いても正規形にそろえる) |
+| `待つ側の宣言 ` | 待つほうの Issue の、競合の可能性を判定した宣言のコメントの ID | `宣言` と同じ数値 |
+| `前の PR ` | 作り直しの依頼で、マージされずに閉じた前の小さな PR | PR の URL |
+| `PR ` | 本文の追記を頼む PR | PR の URL |
+| `理由 ` | `待機` の待つ理由と相手 / `解放` の理由 | 下の種類の表 |
+| `値 ` | `停滞` で書いた `Agent stuck state` の値 | ` | ` を含まない文字列 |
+| `Issue ` | `依存の待ち` で待つ Issue | Issue の参照。待つ Issue の数だけ繰り返す |
+
+### 種類
+
+| 種類 | 書き手 | 値 (この並び) | 何を書くか |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `割り当て` | 管理のセッション | `対象`・`割り当て` | 割り当てた経緯 |
+| `開始可` | 管理のセッション | `対象`・`割り当て`・`宣言` | 宣言に競合の可能性が無いという判定の結果 |
+| `待機` | 管理のセッション | `対象`・`割り当て`・`宣言`・`理由` (待つものの数だけ繰り返す) | 待つ理由。`理由` の値は `利用者の答え` / `Issue <参照>` / `小さな PR <依頼先の Issue の参照>` (PR ができていれば続けて ` PR <URL>`) / `資源 <名前>` / `設定`。その宣言がその時点で待っているものをすべて並べる (最新の `待機` で、ほかの待ちも分かるようにするため) |
+| `解放` | 管理のセッション | `対象`・`割り当て`・`理由` | 解放の理由。値は `解除` (フィールドを空にして `Todo`) / `close` (フィールドを跡として残す) / `ID の変更` (Status だけ `Todo`) / `除去` (項目が Project から除かれた)。理由で、後に書くものを分ける (正本は計画の KTD19) |
+| `引き継ぎ` | 管理のセッション | 無し | 前の管理のセッションの作業中の項目を引き継いだ経緯 (本文に前の管理のセッションの名前と ID と理由) |
+| `停滞` | 管理のセッション | `対象`・`割り当て`・`値` | `Agent stuck state` に値を書いた経緯 |
+| `依存の待ち` | 管理のセッション | `Issue` (待つ Issue の数だけ) | 割り当ての無い項目を、開いている blocker があるので `Blocked` にした経緯。宛先と割り当ての番号は持たない (割り当てが無いため) |
+| `依存の解消` | 管理のセッション | 無し | blocker がすべて閉じたので `Ready` に戻した経緯 |
+| `依頼` | 管理のセッション | `対象`・`割り当て`・`種類` と、種類ごとの値: `宣言の書き直し` は `宣言`、`本文の追記` は `PR`、`小さな PR` は `待つ Issue`・`待つ側の宣言`・作り直しなら `前の PR` | 作業のセッションにしてもらうこと (本文に理由と、何をすればよいか) |
+| `着手の宣言` | 作業のセッション | 無し | 変える予定のファイル (本文の様式は U10) |
+| `宣言の更新` | 作業のセッション | 無し | 宣言の更新 (本文の様式は U10) |
+| `小さな PR の報告` | 作業のセッション | `待つ Issue`・`待つ側の宣言`・作り直しなら `前の PR` (依頼の値を写す) | 依頼 `小さな PR` を受けて小さな PR を作ったこと (本文に PR の URL) |
+| `PR の報告` | 作業のセッション | 無し | その Issue の PR を ready for review にしたこと (本文に PR の URL) |
+
+`In review` はコメントにせず、記録のログだけに残す (PR の状態から導けるため)。
+
+### 既投稿の見分け (`comment post`)
+
+投稿の前に、同じ出来事への同じコメントが既に無いことを確かめる (冪等。やり直しで同じ出来事をもう一度書こうとしたときに二重に書かないため)。同じ出来事かは、先頭行の書き手のセッション ID・種類・値で見分け、**名前は比べない** (名前は変わりうる)。種類ごとの規則:
+
+| 種類 | 比べる相手 | 既投稿とする条件 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `待機` | 同じ宣言への最新の `待機` | 待つ理由と相手がすべて同じ。前と同じ理由の待ちに戻ったとき (間に別の理由の `待機` がある) と、待つものの一部が解けて残りを書いたときは投稿する |
+| `依存の待ち` | 最新の `依存の待ち` | 待つ Issue が同じで、間に `依存の解消` が無い |
+| `依存の解消` | 最新の `依存の待ち` より後のコメント (`依存の待ち` が無ければ全部) | 同じ `依存の解消` がある (2 度目の `Blocked` の後の `依存の解消` は投稿する) |
+| `停滞` | 同じ対象・割り当ての `停滞` | 値が同じ (間に別のコメントがあっても投稿しない) |
+| ほか | 全部のコメント | 先頭行 (名前を除く) が同じ。宛先・割り当ての番号・宣言の ID・依頼の PR・待つ Issue が違えば投稿する |
+
+一覧が読めなければ投稿しない (既投稿かを確かめられないまま投稿すると二重になりうるため)。
+
+### 報告と依頼の対応づけ
+
+`小さな PR の報告` は、先頭行の `待つ Issue`・`待つ側の宣言`・`前の PR` (あれば) が同じ `依頼` (種類 `小さな PR`) に答えたものとする。書いたセッションの名前と ID は比べない (小さな PR を作るのは依頼の宛先のセッションだが、名前は変わりうるため)。作り直しの依頼 (`前の PR` を持つ) には、`前の PR` を持つ報告だけが対応する。

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `385f39a..07f60b8`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `07f60b8..6fd8276`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `6fd8276..cd71273`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

content.text:
Review target: `fff416a..a974117`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

     8	
     9	- **ID** は環境変数から決める: `CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID` (Claude Desktop のセッション ID。`local_` で始まる) があればそれ、無ければ `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (会話の記録と同じ UUID。端末の `claude` にはこちらだけがある)。空の値と、空白か `/` を含む値は無いものとして扱う。どちらの環境変数も公式文書に無い振る舞いなので、読むのは関数 `own_session_id` の 1 か所にまとめる。`l

    11	
    12	## 管理のセッションの規約の名前
    13	
    14	管理のセッションの名前は `issue-dispatch <owner>/<number>/<login>` (`<owner>` と `<number>` は設定の `project`、`<login>` は `gh api user` で得たトークンのログイン)。管理のセッションは「Project と利用者 (そのマシンの `gh` が認証しているアカウント) の組」を担当するので、名前にその組を含める (計画の KD23。チームでは利用者ごとに自分のマシンで管理のセッションを開き、合図と
    15	
    16	- 生成は関数 `manager_name` (owner と番号と login から。同じ入力なら同じ名前)、解析は関数 `parse_manager_name` (名前から owner・番号・login を読む。`ListAgents` の行の短い識別子は呼び出し元が外してから渡す)。owner と login は名前に使える文字 (英数字と `.`・`_`・`-`) だけ、番号は 1 以上の整数。
    17	- 名前による管理のセッションの排他 (同じ名前のセッションが `ListAgents` にあれば起動しない) の手順は計画の R18 で、スキルの手順書 (U21・U23) に書く。使われている名前に変えても同じ名前がそのまま付く (下の「実測」) ので、排他は名前を変える前の `ListAgents` で確かめる。
    18	
    19	## 宛先の決め方
    20	
    21	- **宛先は名前にする。** `SendMessage` の `to` に名前をそのまま渡す (空白と `/` を含んでよい。短い識別子は付けない)。返事は、届いた合図の `from` (ソケットのパス `uds:/tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock`) を `to` にして送る。

Review target: `a974117..a6d8b71`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

 管理のセッションの名前は `issue-dispatch <owner>/<number>/<login>` (`<owner>` と `<number>` は設定の `project`、`<login>` は `gh api user` で得たトークンのログイン)。管理のセッションは「Project と利用者 (そのマシンの `gh` が認証しているアカウント) の組」を担当するので、名前にその組を含める (計画の KD23。チームでは利用者ごとに自分のマシンで管理のセッションを開き、合図と `ListAgents` は同じマシンの中にしか届かないため)。作業のセッションは、リポジトリの設定の `project` と自分のトークンのログインから同じ名前を導いて宛先にする。
 
-- 生成は関数 `manager_name` (owner と番号と login から。同じ入力なら同じ名前)、解析は関数 `parse_manager_name` (名前から owner・番号・login を読む。`ListAgents` の行の短い識別子は呼び出し元が外してから渡す)。owner と login は名前に使える文字 (英数字と `.`・`_`・`-`) だけ、番号は 1 以上の整数。
