content.text:
Review target: `5e8adc5..9e8fac4`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

    29	def normalize_path(path):

    88	def _check_split(split, errors):

   127	def parse(obj, rules, default_table):

   133	    """
   134	    errors = []

   137	                "errors": [{"key": "(root)", "message": f"宣言は files・resources・split を持つオブジェクト: {type(obj).__name__}"}]}

   172	def _file_key(f):

   176	def same_files(a, b):

構造を知っている種類 (`indivisible`・`unstable`・`divisible`) は、両方の宣言がそのパスに `units` を書いていれば、節が同じか、一方の配列が他方の配列の先頭部分 (`["dependencies"]` と `["dependencies", "react"]` など) のときだけ競合しうる。`["dependencies", "react"]` と `["dependencies", "zod"]` は競合しない。どちらかが `units` を省けば、同じパスで競合しうる。

節は階層ごとの名前の配列で表す (`["dependencies", "zod"]`)。区切りの文字を使わないのは、名前に `.` や `/` が含まれることがあるため (`package.json` の `exports` のキー `./utils`、`go.mod` のモジュール名 `github.com/foo/bar`、見出し「v1.2 の変更」)。名前はファイルにある文字のまま比べ、正規化しない (`"./utils"` と `"utils"` は JSON では別のキー)。節の名前は作業のセッションがファイルを読んで書き、スクリプトは名前を比べるだけで、ファイルを構文解析しない。

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1	"""資源 (ラベル `resource:<名前>` と宣言の `resources` で表す、同時に使える数が限られるもの)。属性の読み込み (`attributes`。
     2	設定に無い資源と属性はデフォルト値)、持っている資源の求め方 (`held_from_history`。R20 の (1))、契機ごとの判断
     3	(`judge_assign`・`judge_declare`・`judge_update`・`judge_close`・`judge_release`。属性と、U13 が求めた資源の使用と、記録にある
     4	利用者の答えを引数で受ける)。属性の表と契機の表の正本は issue-dispatch/skills/issue-dispatch/references/resources.md。gh は使わない。
     5	
     6	資源の名前は大文字小文字を区別せずに比べる (ラベルの名前を GitHub が区別しないため)。返す名前は、呼び出し元が渡した綴り
     7	(宣言・ラベル・設定) のまま。
     8	"""
     9	
    10	from issue_dispatch import declaration
    11	
    12	# 属性 (名前 → デフォルト値)。意味と値は resources.md の属性の表
    13	DEFAULTS = {"capacity": 1, "reserve": "on_assign", "when_busy": "wait", "release_undeclared": "ask"}
    14	VALUES = {"reserve": ("on_assign", "on_declare"), "when_busy": ("wait", "ask"), "release_undeclared": ("release", "ask")}
    15	TRIGGERS = ("assign", "declare", "update", "close", "release")
    16	# 利用者の答え。when_busy が ask のとき: wait (待つ) / proceed (進める)。release_undeclared が ask のとき: release (解放してよい) / keep (解放してはいけない)
    17	BUSY_ANSWERS = ("wait", "proceed")
    18	UNDECLARED_ANSWERS = ("release", "keep")
    19	
    20	
    21	def _key(name):
    22	    return name.strip().casefold()
    23	
    24	
    25	# --- 属性 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    26	
    27	def attributes(config_resources):
    28	    """設定の `resources` (資源の名前 → 属性のオブジェクト。config が形だけ検査したもの) に、書かれていない属性のデフォルト値を
    29	    当てる。返り値は (表: 名前の casefold → {"name": 設定の綴り, 属性...}, warnings: [{"key", "message"}])。
    30	    未知の属性と誤った値は警告してデフォルト値を使う。綴りだけ違う 2 つ目以降の資源は警告して使わない。"""
    31	    table, warnings = {}, []
    32	    for name, raw in (config_resources or {}).items():
    33	        key = _key(name)
    34	        if key in table:
    35	            warnings.append({"key": f"resources.{name}", "message": f"資源 {name!r} は {table[key]['name']!r} と綴りだけが違う (名前は大文字小文字を区別しない)。使わない"})
    36	            continue
    37	        entry = {"name": name, **DEFAULTS}
    38	        for attr, value in (raw or {}).items():
    39	            if attr not in DEFAULTS:
    40	                warnings.append({"key": f"resources.{name}.{attr}", "message": f"未知の属性 {attr!r} (属性は {', '.join(DEFAULTS)})。使わない"})
    41	                continue
    42	            if attr == "capacity":
    43	                ok = isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 1
    44	            else:
    45	                ok = value in VALUES[attr]
    46	            if not ok:
    47	                expected = "1 以上の整数" if attr == "capacity" else " / ".join(VALUES[attr])
    48	                warnings.append({"key": f"resources.{name}.{attr}", "message": f"{attr} の値 {value!r} は誤り ({expected})。デフォルト値 {DEFAULTS[attr]!r} を使う"})
    49	                continue
    50	            entry[attr] = value
    51	        table[key] = entry
    52	    return table, warnings
    53	
    54	
    55	def attributes_of(table, name):
    56	    """資源の属性。設定に無ければデフォルト値 (name は渡された綴り)。"""
    57	    return dict(table.get(_key(name)) or {"name": name, **DEFAULTS})
    58	
    59	
    60	# --- 持っている資源 (R20 の (1)) ------------------------------------------------------
    61	
    62	def held_from_history(history):
    63	    """今の割り当ての宣言の並び (投稿の順) から持っている資源を求める。history の要素は {"declaration": parse の結果の declaration,
    64	    "go": `開始可` を書いたか, "rejected": 差し戻されたか (省略は偽)}。
    65	    最後に `開始可` を書いた宣言の resources のうち、その後の差し戻されていない更新のすべてに残っているもの (その宣言の綴り)。
    66	    `開始可` の宣言が無ければ空。"""
    67	    accepted = [h for h in history if not h.get("rejected")]
    68	    go_index = max((i for i, h in enumerate(accepted) if h.get("go")), default=None)
    69	    if go_index is None:
    70	        return []
    71	    go = accepted[go_index]["declaration"]
    72	    later = [h["declaration"] for h in accepted[go_index + 1:]]
    73	    return [r for r in go["resources"] if all(_key(r) in {_key(x) for x in d["resources"]} for d in later)]
    74	
    75	
    76	# --- 判断 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    77	
    78	def holders(usage, name, except_item=None):
    79	    """資源を持つ項目 (使用 usage: 資源の名前 → 項目のキーの配列。綴りは問わない) のうち except_item 以外。"""
    80	    out = []

    82	        if _key(key) == _key(name):
    83	            out += [i for i in items if i != except_item]
    84	    return out
    85	
    86	
    87	def _busy(usage, name, item, attrs_table):
    88	    return len(holders(usage, name, item)) >= attributes_of(attrs_table, name)["capacity"]
    89	
    90	
    91	def _answer(answers, name):
    92	    return next((v for k, v in (answers or {}).items() if _key(k) == _key(name)), None)
    93	
    94	
    95	def judge_assign(item, label_resources, usage, attrs_table, answers):
    96	    """契機「割り当て」。label_resources は項目のラベルの資源。answers は when_busy が ask の資源への答え (名前 → wait / proceed)。
    97	    返り値: {"result": "assign" (割り当てて reserve を予約する) / "skip" (候補から外す) / "ask" (利用者に尋ねる),
    98	    "reserve": 予約する資源, "busy": 空いていない資源, "ask": 尋ねる資源}。reserve が on_declare の資源は予約せず、空きも待たない。"""
    99	    reserve, busy, ask = [], [], []
   100	    for name in label_resources:
   101	        a = attributes_of(attrs_table, name)
   102	        if a["reserve"] != "on_assign":
   103	            continue
   104	        if _busy(usage, name, item, attrs_table):
   105	            answer = _answer(answers, name)
   106	            if a["when_busy"] == "ask" and answer != "wait":
   107	                if answer == "proceed":
   108	                    reserve.append(name)
   109	                else:
   110	                    ask.append(name)
   111	            else:
   112	                busy.append(name)
   113	            continue
   114	        reserve.append(name)
   115	    if busy:
   116	        return {"result": "skip", "reserve": [], "busy": busy, "ask": []}
   117	    if ask:
   118	        return {"result": "ask", "reserve": [], "busy": [], "ask": ask}
   119	    return {"result": "assign", "reserve": reserve, "busy": [], "ask": []}
   120	
   121	
   122	def _check_new(item, names, usage, attrs_table, answers):
   123	    """予約していない資源の空きを確かめる。返り値は (reserve, wait_for, ask)。"""
   124	    reserve, wait_for, ask = [], [], []
   125	    for name in names:
   126	        if _busy(usage, name, item, attrs_table):
   127	            answer = _answer(answers, name)
   128	            if attributes_of(attrs_table, name)["when_busy"] == "ask" and answer != "wait":
   129	                (reserve if answer == "proceed" else ask).append(name)
   130	            else:
   131	                wait_for.append(name)
   132	        else:
   133	            reserve.append(name)
   134	    return reserve, wait_for, ask
   135	
   136	
   137	def judge_declare(item, declared, reserved, usage, attrs_table, answers, undeclared_answers):
   138	    """契機「着手の宣言」。declared は宣言の resources、reserved は割り当てで予約した資源。answers は when_busy が ask の資源への答え、
   139	    undeclared_answers は release_undeclared が ask の資源への答え (名前 → release / keep)。
   140	    返り値: {"result": "go" (`開始可` を書くときに reserve を予約する) / "wait" (`待機`。どれも予約しない) / "ask",
   141	    "reserve", "wait_for", "ask", "release" (解放する宣言に無い予約), "keep" (答えを待つ・残す予約), "ask_undeclared" (尋ねる),
   142	    "request_rewrite" (解放してはいけないので書き直しを頼む)}。宣言に無い予約の扱いは go / wait / ask に依らない。"""
   143	    reserved_keys = {_key(r) for r in reserved}
   144	    new = [r for r in declared if _key(r) not in reserved_keys]
   145	    reserve, wait_for, ask = _check_new(item, new, usage, attrs_table, answers)
   146	    declared_keys = {_key(r) for r in declared}
   147	    release, keep, ask_undeclared, request_rewrite = [], [], [], []
   148	    for name in reserved:
   149	        if _key(name) in declared_keys:
   150	            continue
   151	        if attributes_of(attrs_table, name)["release_undeclared"] == "release":
   152	            release.append(name)
   153	            continue
   154	        answer = _answer(undeclared_answers, name)
   155	        if answer == "release":
   156	            release.append(name)
   157	        elif answer == "keep":
   158	            keep.append(name)
   159	            request_rewrite.append(name)
   160	        else:
   161	            keep.append(name)
   162	            ask_undeclared.append(name)
   163	    result = "wait" if wait_for else ("ask" if ask else "go")
   164	    return {"result": result, "reserve": reserve if result == "go" else [], "wait_for": wait_for, "ask": ask,
   165	            "release": release, "keep": keep, "ask_undeclared": ask_undeclared, "request_rewrite": request_rewrite}
   166

   168	def judge_update(item, held, declared, usage, attrs_table, answers):

   170	    ものも含む) は着手の宣言と同じに空きを確かめる。返り値: {"result": "go" / "wait" / "ask", "reserve", "wait_for", "ask", "release"}。"""

   172	    declared_keys = {_key(r) for r in declared}

1	# 資源の扱い
     2	
     3	このファイルが、この仕組み (issue-dispatch) の資源の扱いの正本。資源は、同時に使える数が限られるもの (検証用の DB・GPU など) で、Issue のラベル `resource:<名前>` (正本は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「Issue が持つもの」) と宣言の `resources` (同じ文書の「宣言」) で表す。資源の種類で変わりうる判断はすべて属性にし、属性は管理ディレクトリの設定の `resources` に資源の名前ごとに書く (設定のキーの正本は [project-config.md](project-config.md))。設定に無い資源と、書かれていない属性はデフォルト値で扱い、デフォル�
     4	
     5	**資源の名前は大文字小文字を区別しない** (ラベルの名前を GitHub が区別しないため)。設定の `resources` のキー・ラベル・宣言の `resources`・使用の表の名前を同じ規則で比べ、返す名前は渡された綴りのまま。設定で綴りだけ違う 2 つ目以降の資源は警告して使わない。
     6	
     7	## 属性
     8	
     9	| 属性 | 決めること | 値 | デフォルト値 |
    10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    11	| `capacity` | 同時に資源を持てる (予約か宣言で使っている) 項目の数 | 1 以上の整数 | `1` |
    12	| `reserve` | いつ予約するか | `on_assign` (割り当てのとき) / `on_declare` (着手の宣言のとき。割り当ては資源の空きを待たない) | `on_assign` |
    13	| `when_busy` | 資源を持つ項目の数が `capacity` に達しているときにどうするか | `wait` (割り当てない・コメント `待機` を書く) / `ask` (使用中であることを示して利用者に尋ねる。進める選択肢も示す) | `wait` |
    14	| `release_undeclared` | 予約したのに着手の宣言の `resources` に無い資源をどうするか | `release` (尋ねずに解放する) / `ask` (利用者に尋ねる) | `ask` |
    15	
    16	未知の属性と誤った値は警告してデフォルト値を使う (`resources attributes` の `warnings`)。
    17	
    18	## 資源の使用と持っている資源
    19	
    20	資源の使用 (資源 → 持っている項目) は記録に書かず、割り当て・ラベル・宣言・`開始可` から、ターンのたびに導く (導き方の出どころは計画の KTD19 の表の行「資源の使用」。実装は U13)。項目が持つ資源は、割り当てで予約した資源と、持っている資源 (定義の正本は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「更新の種類」) の両方。関数 `held_from_history` は、今の割り当ての宣言の並び (投稿の順。宣言ごとに `開始可` を書いたか・差し戻されたか) からその定義のとおり持っている資源を求める。差し戻された宣言は数え�
    21	
    22	資源の確保と解放は同じセッションが組で行う: 管理のセッションは割り当てのとき (ラベルの資源) と `開始可` を書くとき (宣言の資源) に予約し、Issue の close と割り当ての解除のときに解放する。作業のセッションは着手の宣言の `resources` で使うと宣言し、使い終えたら資源を外した `宣言の更新` で使い終えたと宣言する。
    23	
    24	## 契機
    25	
    26	判断は契機ごとに 1 つの関数で、属性 (設定から) と資源の使用 (U13 が求める) と利用者の答え (記録にある。読むのは呼び出し元) を引数で受ける。利用者の答えの値: `when_busy` が `ask` の資源には `wait` (待つ) / `proceed` (進める)、`release_undeclared` が `ask` の資源には `release` (解放してよい) / `keep` (解放してはいけない)。
    27	
    28	| 契機 (`--trigger`) | 行うこと | 読む属性 | 結果 |
    29	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    30	| 割り当て `assign` (R19) | ラベルの資源のうち `reserve` が `on_assign` のものについて、資源を持つ項目の数 (自分を除く) が `capacity` に達していれば `when_busy` に従う。`wait` なら候補にしない。`ask` なら割り当てるかを利用者に尋ね、利用者が待つと答えたら `wait` と同じに候補にせず、答えを記録に書いて、その資源が解放されるまで同じ問いを尋ね直さない。進めると答えたら割り当てる。`reserve` が `on_declare` の資源は予約せず、空きも待たない | `reserve`・`capacity`・`when_busy` | `assign` (割り当てて `reserve` の資源を予約�
    31	| 着手の宣言 `declare` (R20) | 宣言の `resources` のうち予約していない資源は空きを確かめ、すべて空いていれば `開始可` を書くときに予約する。空いていないものがあれば、どれも予約せずに `when_busy` に従う (`wait` ならコメント `待機` を書き、合図 `wait` を送る。Status は変えない。`ask` なら利用者に尋ね、答えを待つ間は `待機` を書き、待つと答えたら `wait` と同じ)。待っている宣言は新しく要る資源を持たない。予約したのに宣言に無い資源は `release_undeclared` に従う: `release` なら解放する。`ask` なら尋ね、答えを
    32	| 宣言の更新 `update` (R20。ready for review の前も後も) | 持っている資源から外した資源を解放する。足した資源 (前に外して足し直したものも含む) は、着手の宣言と同じに空きを確かめる。資源を外すだけの更新には `開始可` を書かない (種類の判定は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「更新の種類」) | `capacity`・`when_busy` | `go` / `wait` / `ask` と `reserve`・`wait_for`・`ask`・`release` |
    33	| Issue の close・割り当ての解除 `close` (R21。進行中の Issue の close では、利用者が止めると答えた後) | その項目が持つ資源をすべて解放する | — | `release` に資源 |
    34	| 資源の解放 `release` (宣言の更新で外したとき・着手の宣言で `release_undeclared` に従って解放したとき・Issue の close・割り当ての解除) | その資源で `待機` になっていた宣言を、宣言の投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に判定し直す (ファイルの競合の可能性は、`開始可` を書く直前の比べ直しのとおりに扱う)。`開始可` になった宣言にはコメント `開始可` を書き、合図 `go` を送る (Status が `Blocked` の項目は戻す) | — | `rejudge` に待っていた宣言 (判定し直す順) |
    35	
    36	`開始可` を書くのは、ファイルの競合の可能性でも資源でも待たないときだけ。属性を 1 つ変えたとき、結果が変わるのは、その属性を読む契機だけ。
    37	
    38	## CLI
    39	
    40	| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
    41	| --- | --- | --- |
    42	| `resources attributes --dir <管理ディレクトリ> [--name <資源>]` | 無し | `resources` (設定の資源ごとの属性。`--name` なら その資源 1 つで、設定に無ければデフォルト値)・`defaults`・`warnings` (未知の属性・誤った値・綴りだけ違う名前) |
    43	| `resources judge --dir <管理ディレクトリ> --trigger <契機> (--body <JSON> \| --body-file <ファイル \| ->)` | 無し | 契機の表の「結果」に書いたキー。本文のキーは契機ごと: `assign` は `item`・`resources` (ラベルの資源)・`usage`・`answers`。`declare` は `item`・`declared`・`reserved`・`usage`・`answers`・`undeclared_answers`。`update` は `item`・`held`・`declared`・`usage`・`answers`。`close` は `item`・`usage`。`release` は `resource`・`waiting` (要素は `item`・`declaration`・`posted_at`・`position`・`wait_for`)。`usage` は資源の名前 → 持っている項目 (`owner/repo#番号`) の配列 |

    21	
    22	資源の確保と解放は同じセッションが組で行う: 管理のセッションは割り当てのとき (ラベルの資源) と `開始可` を書くとき (宣言の資源) に予約し、Issue の close と割り当ての解除のときに解放する。作業のセッションは着手の宣言の `resources` で使うと宣言し、使い終えたら資源を外した `宣言の更新` で使い終えたと宣言する。

    25	
    26	判断は契機ごとに 1 つの関数で、属性 (設定から) と資源の使用 (U13 が求める) と利用者の答え (記録にある。読むのは呼び出し元) を引数で受ける。利用者の答えの値: `when_busy` が `ask` の資源には `wait` (待つ) / `proceed` (進める)、`release_undeclared` が `ask` の資源には `release` (解放してよい) / `keep` (解放してはいけない)。

    28	| 契機 (`--trigger`) | 行うこと | 読む属性 | 結果 |

    32	| 宣言の更新 `update` (R20。ready for review の前も後も) | 持っている資源から外した資源を解放する。足した資源 (前に外して足し直したものも含む) は、着手の宣言と同じに空きを確かめる。資源を外すだけの更新には `開始可` を書かない (種類の判定は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「更新の種類」) | `capacity`・`when_busy` | `go` / `wait` / `ask` と `reserve`・`wait_for`・`ask`・`release` |

    35

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `bf8a68c..b1ff3bc`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings

Review target: `bf8a68c..b1ff3bc`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `1121e88..e879c51`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1	"""観測のうちスナップショットと差分。`snapshot.json` (ポーリングの基準になる Project の状態の写し) の読み書き、項目の読み取り
     2	からの作成 (`build_snapshot`)、コメントに URL で書かれた PR の収集 (`pr_urls_in_comments`)、書いた値の反映 (`reflect`)、
     3	スナップショットと今の内容の差分 (`diff`。何が変わったかだけを処理の順に返し、意味づけはしない)。
     4	様式・差分の種類と処理の順の正本は issue-dispatch/skills/issue-dispatch/references/observation.md。置き場は records.md。
     5	
     6	このモジュールは gh を実行しない (項目の読み取りは project.items、PR の状態は issues.pr_state を呼び出し元が行う)。
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import json
    10	import os
    11	import re
    12	
    13	from issue_dispatch import comments, ids
    14	
    15	SNAPSHOT_FILE = "snapshot.json"
    16	SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 1
    17	SNAPSHOT_KEYS = ("version", "taken_at", "project_id", "items", "comment_prs")
    18	ITEM_KEYS = ("item_id", "position", "state", "status", "fields", "assignees", "labels", "blocked_by", "body_edited_at", "comment_ids", "prs")
    19	# 差分の種類と処理の順 (observation.md の表): 人の変更 → close・reopen と項目の除去 → blockedBy → コメント → PR → 項目の追加・並び順・本文の編集
    20	DIFF_KINDS = ("status", "field", "assignees", "labels", "closed", "reopened", "removed", "blocked_by", "comment", "pr", "added", "position", "body_edit")
    21	# コメントの本文から PR を読む種類
    22	PR_URL_COMMENT_KINDS = ("PR の報告",)
    23	_PR_URL_RE = re.compile(rf"https://github\.com/{ids.REPO_NAME_PATTERN}/pull/[1-9][0-9]*")
    24

    26	# --- ファイル ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    27	
    28	def load_snapshot(directory):
    29	    """返り値: {"status": "ok", "snapshot"} / {"status": "missing"} / {"status": "corrupt", "message"}。"""
    30	    path = os.path.join(directory, SNAPSHOT_FILE)
    31	    if not os.path.exists(path):
    32	        return {"status": "missing", "snapshot": None, "path": path}
    33	    try:
    34	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    35	            data = json.load(f)
    36	    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
    37	        return {"status": "corrupt", "snapshot": None, "path": path, "message": f"読めない: {e}"}
    38	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or any(k not in data for k in SNAPSHOT_KEYS) or not isinstance(data["items"], dict) or not isinstance(data["comment_prs"], dict):
    39	        return {"status": "corrupt", "snapshot": None, "path": path, "message": f"キー {', '.join(SNAPSHOT_KEYS)} を持つオブジェクトではない"}
    40	    return {"status": "ok", "snapshot": data, "path": path}
    41	
    42	
    43	def save_snapshot(directory, snapshot):
    44	    """一時ファイルに書いて os.replace で置き換える。返り値はパス。"""
    45	    os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    46	    path = os.path.join(directory, SNAPSHOT_FILE)
    47	    tmp = path + ".tmp"
    48	    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    49	        json.dump(snapshot, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    50	        f.write("\n")
    51	    os.replace(tmp, path)
    52	    return path
    53	
    54	
    55	# --- 作成 -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    56	
    57	def _pr_state(p):
    58	    return {"state": p["state"], "draft": bool(p.get("draft")), "merged": bool(p.get("merged"))}
    59

    61	def snapshot_item(item):

    63	    fields = {name: {"value": v.get("text") if "text" in v else v.get("name"), "updated_at": v.get("updated_at")} for name, v in (item.get("fields") or {}).items()}

    66	            "status": (item.get("status") or {}).get("name"), "fields": fields,
    67	            "assignees": sorted(item.get("assignees") or []), "labels": sorted(item.get("labels") or []),
    68	            "blocked_by": {b["key"]: b["state"] for b in item.get("blocked_by") or []},
    69	            "body_edited_at": max(edits) if edits else None,
    70	            "comment_ids": sorted(c["database_id"] for c in item.get("comments") or [] if c.get("database_id") is not None),

    17	| `version` | 様式の版 (`1`) |
    18	| `taken_at` | Project を読んだ時刻 (UTC) |
    19	| `project_id` | Project の ID |
    20	| `items` | 項目のキー (`owner/repo#番号`) → 下の表。Issue 以外の項目 (draft issue・PR) は持たない |

    25	| キー | 内容 |
    26	| --- | --- |
    27	| `item_id` / `position` | 項目の ID・位置 (1 始まり) |
    28	| `state` | `OPEN` / `CLOSED` |
    29	| `status` | Status の名前 (無ければ null) |
    30	| `fields` | フィールド名 → `value` (テキストか選択肢の名前) と `updated_at`。Status は含まない |

    33	| `body_edited_at` | 本文の最新の編集の時刻 (作成も編集に数える) |
    34	| `comment_ids` | 読んだコメントの `database_id` (昇順) |
    35	| `prs` | Issue を閉じる参照の PR の URL → `state`・`draft`・`merged` (閉じたものも含む) |

    39	`observe diff` は、スナップショットと今の Project (と PR の状態) の違いを、下の表の順 (計画の R12 の処理の順: 人の変更 → close・reopen と項目の除去 → `blockedBy` → コメント → PR → 項目の追加・並び順・本文の編集) に並べて返す。同じ種類の中は今の位置の順。要素は `kind`・`item` (コメントの URL の PR は null) と、種類ごとの値。

    44	| 2 | `field` | フィールドの値が違う (前にあって今は無い = 人が空にした、も含む。`Agent stuck state` を空にした・`Agent session ID` を別の値にした、はこれ) | `field`・`before`・`after` |
    45	| 3 | `assignees` | 担当者が違う | `added`・`removed` |
    46	| 4 | `labels` | ラベルが違う | `added`・`removed` |
    47	| 5 | `closed` | 開いていた Issue が閉じた (`Done` を書く呼び出しは無い。組み込みワークフローが書く) | `before`・`after` |
    48	| 6 | `reopened` | 閉じていた Issue が開いた | `before`・`after` |
    49	| 7 | `removed` | 項目が Project から除かれた | `position` (前の位置) |
    50	| 8 | `blocked_by` | blocker が足された・外された・開閉が変わった | `added`・`removed`・`state_changed` (`key`・`before`・`after`) |
    51	| 9 | `comment` | コメントが足された | `ids` (足されたコメントの `database_id`) |
    52	| 10 | `pr` | PR の状態 (`state`・`draft`・`merged`) が違う、または PR が現れた・消えた | `url`・`source` (`reference` Issue を閉じる参照 / `comment` コメントの URL)・`before`・`after` |
    53	| 11 | `added` | 項目が Project に足された | `position` |
    54	| 12 | `position` | 位置が変わった | `before`・`after` |
    55	| 13 | `body_edit` | 本文の最新の編集の時刻が違う | `before`・`after` |
    56	
    57	確認の対象か・割り当て中か・誰が足した blocker か・どの宣言が待っていたか、といった意味づけはここではしない (U13)。
    58

    61	書き込みのサブコマンド (`project set-status` / `issue add-label` / `blocked-by add` / `comment post`。後の単位の書き込みのサブコマンドも同じ) は、引数 `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` があれば、書いた値だけをスナップショットに反映する (関数 `reflect`)。読み取りの後にほかの人が変えた値は反映しない。スナップショットが無い・壊れている・項目が無いときは反映せず、出力の `snapshot.warnings` で知らせ、書き込みの結果は変えない。作業のセッシ�

    64

    66	
    67	| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
    68	| --- | --- | --- |
    69	| `project items --project <owner>/<番号> --write-snapshot --dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` (GitHub には書かない) | 引数 `--write-snapshot` は `--dir` と一緒に指定する。`project items` の出力に `snapshot` (`path`・`taken_at`・`comment_prs`) を足す。コメントの URL の PR が読めなければ `problems` (`what`: `comment-pr`) に入れて `partial` |
    70	| `observe diff --dir <管理ディレクトリ> --project <owner>/<番号>` | 無し | `diffs` (上の表の順)・`snapshot_taken_at`・`problems`・`rate_limit`。スナップショットが無い・壊れていれば `errors` (key `snapshot`) で、`gh` は実行しない。スナップショットにある `comment_prs` の PR は、コメントが消えていても状態を読み直す (待っていた PR の変化を見つけるため) |
    71	| 書き込みのサブコマンドの `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` | 出力に `snapshot` (`reflected`・`warnings`) を足す |

findings.summary: observe diff builds the current snapshot from a partial project.items result (a later items page or a comments page could not be read) and diffs it against the full snapshot, so items that were merely not read come back as `removed` (and, with --write-snapshot, a partial read is saved and the next diff reports them as `added`).
findings.short_summary: Partial items read reported as removed items
findings.failure_scenario: snapshot written from 2 pages (5 items); observe diff where page 2 fails with HTTP 502 → status partial, diffs [(removed, verify-b#8), (removed, verify-b#9)], problems [items-page]

findings.summary: save_snapshot writes to the fixed name `snapshot.json.tmp`, which does not follow records.md's temp-name rule (start with `.`, end with `.tmp`) that record.save follows with mkstemp, so two writers in the same turn share the temp file and the file is not fsynced.
findings.short_summary: Snapshot temp name breaks records.md rule
findings.failure_scenario: records.md says temp names start with `.`; observe.py uses path + ".tmp" (snapshot.json.tmp), while record.save uses tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".record-", suffix=".json.tmp")

findings.summary: position is the 1-based index of the read, so adding or removing one item shifts the index of every later item and diff reports a `position` change for each of them, although nobody reordered them.
findings.short_summary: One added item yields position diffs for all after it
findings.failure_scenario: snapshot items at positions 1..5; an item is added at the top → diff has one added plus five position diffs (before n, after n+1)

## 目的

スナップショットは、前のターンの終わりの Project の状態 (と、コメントに URL で書かれた PR の GitHub 上の状態) の写しで、GitHub から導出し直せるキャッシュ (計画の KTD5)。使うのは 2 つ: 待機が変化に気づいて管理のセッションを起こすこと (U14) と、人の変更を 1 回だけ報告すること (計画の R22)。**何を行うかはスナップショットからは決めない** — 導いた項目の状態 (U13) で決める。差分は「何が変わったか」だけを返し、意味づけ (管理のセッションが足した blocker か・どの宣言が待つか) はしない。

書き手は管理のセッションの再入のターンだけ。Project を読んだとき (`project items --write-snapshot`) に書き、そのターンの CLI の書き込みのたびに書いた値を反映する。待機の直前には読み直さない (読み直すと、ターンの最初の読み取りから読み直しまでの間にほかの人が起こした変化が、処理されないままスナップショットに入り、待機がその変化に気づかない)。書き込みに失敗したのに反映した値は、次の差分が食い違いとして見つけ、次のターンで直す。壊れていれば作り直す。

## `snapshot.json` の様式

持つ値は、計画の R21 の「見つける変化」の一覧から決め、一覧に無い値 (タイトル・本文・出来事など) は持たない。

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | 様式の版 (`1`) |
| `taken_at` | Project を読んだ時刻 (UTC) |
| `project_id` | Project の ID |
| `items` | 項目のキー (`owner/repo#番号`) → 下の表。Issue 以外の項目 (draft issue・PR) は持たない |
| `comment_prs` | 開いている項目のコメント (`PR の報告` の本文の URL と、`待機` の理由 `小さな PR` の PR。書き手がトークンのログインのものだけ) に書かれた PR の URL → `state`・`draft`・`merged`。どの割り当てのものかは区別しない (意味づけは U13)。閉じた項目のコメントは読まない |

項目の値:

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `item_id` / `position` | 項目の ID・位置 (1 始まり) |
| `state` | `OPEN` / `CLOSED` |
| `status` | Status の名前 (無ければ null) |
| `fields` | フィールド名 → `value` (テキストか選択肢の名前) と `updated_at`。Status は含まない |
| `assignees` / `labels` | 担当者のログイン・ラベルの名前 (名前の順) |
| `blocked_by` | blocker のキー → `OPEN` / `CLOSED` |
| `body_edited_at` | 本文の最新の編集の時刻 (作成も編集に数える) |
| `comment_ids` | 読んだコメントの `database_id` (昇順) |
| `prs` | Issue を閉じる参照の PR の URL → `state`・`draft`・`merged` (閉じたものも含む) |

## 差分の種類と処理の順

`observe diff` は、スナップショットと今の Project (と PR の状態) の違いを、下の表の順 (計画の R12 の処理の順: 人の変更 → close・reopen と項目の除去 → `blockedBy` → コメント → PR → 項目の追加・並び順・本文の編集) に並べて返す。同じ種類の中は今の位置の順。要素は `kind`・`item` (コメントの URL の PR は null) と、種類ごとの値。

| 順 | 種類 (`kind`) | 条件 | 値 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `status` | Status の名前が違う | `before`・`after` |
| 2 | `field` | フィールドの値が違う (前にあって今は無い = 人が空にした、も含む。`Agent stuck state` を空にした・`Agent session ID` を別の値にした、はこれ) | `field`・`before`・`after` |
| 3 | `assignees` | 担当者が違う | `added`・`removed` |
| 4 | `labels` | ラベルが違う | `added`・`removed` |
| 5 | `closed` | 開いていた Issue が閉じた (`Done` を書く呼び出しは無い。組み込みワークフローが書く) | `before`・`after` |
| 6 | `reopened` | 閉じていた Issue が開いた | `before`・`after` |
| 7 | `removed` | 項目が Project から除かれた | `position` (前の位置) |
| 8 | `blocked_by` | blocker が足された・外された・開閉が変わった | `added`・`removed`・`state_changed` (`key`・`before`・`after`) |
| 9 | `comment` | コメントが足された | `ids` (足されたコメントの `database_id`) |
| 10 | `pr` | PR の状態 (`state`・`draft`・`merged`) が違う、または PR が現れた・消えた | `url`・`source` (`reference` Issue を閉じる参照 / `comment` コメントの URL)・`before`・`after` |
| 11 | `added` | 項目が Project に足された | `position` |
| 12 | `position` | 位置が変わった | `before`・`after` |
| 13 | `body_edit` | 本文の最新の編集の時刻が違う | `before`・`after` |

確認の対象か・割り当て中か・誰が足した blocker か・どの宣言が待っていたか、といった意味づけはここではしない (U13)。

## 書いた値の反映

書き込みのサブコマンド (`project set-status` / `issue add-label` / `blocked-by add` / `comment post`。後の単位の書き込みのサブコマンドも同じ) は、引数 `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` があれば、書いた値だけをスナップショットに反映する (関数 `reflect`)。読み取りの後にほかの人が変えた値は反映しない。スナップショットが無い・壊れている・項目が無いときは反映せず、出力の `snapshot.warnings` で知らせ、書き込みの結果は変えない。作業のセッションは管理ディレクトリを持たないので指定しない。

反映の操作: `status` (`value`)・`field` (`field`・`value`)・`comment` (`id`)・`blocked_by` (`action` `add` / `remove`・`blocker`・`state`)・`labels` / `assignees` (`add`・`remove`)。

| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project items --project <owner>/<番号> --write-snapshot --dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` (GitHub には書かない) | 引数 `--write-snapshot` は `--dir` と一緒に指定する。`project items` の出力に `snapshot` (`path`・`taken_at`・`comment_prs`) を足す。コメントの URL の PR が読めなければ `problems` (`what`: `comment-pr`) に入れて `partial` |
| `observe diff --dir <管理ディレクトリ> --project <owner>/<番号>` | 無し | `diffs` (上の表の順)・`snapshot_taken_at`・`problems`・`rate_limit`。スナップショットが無い・壊れていれば `errors` (key `snapshot`) で、`gh` は実行しない。スナップショットにある `comment_prs` の PR は、コメントが消えていても状態を読み直す (待っていた PR の変化を見つけるため) |
| 書き込みのサブコマンドの `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` | 出力に `snapshot` (`reflected`・`warnings`) を足す |

## 目的

スナップショットは、前のターンの終わりの Project の状態 (と、コメントに URL で書かれた PR の GitHub 上の状態) の写しで、GitHub から導出し直せるキャッシュ (計画の KTD5)。使うのは 2 つ: 待機が変化に気づいて管理のセッションを起こすこと (U14) と、人の変更を 1 回だけ報告すること (計画の R22)。**何を行うかはスナップショットからは決めない** — 導いた項目の状態 (U13) で決める。差分は「何が変わったか」だけを返し、意味づけ (管理のセッションが足した blocker か・どの宣言が待つか) はしない。

書き手は管理のセッションの再入のターンだけ。Project を読んだとき (`project items --write-snapshot`) に書き、そのターンの CLI の書き込みのたびに書いた値を反映する。待機の直前には読み直さない (読み直すと、ターンの最初の読み取りから読み直しまでの間にほかの人が起こした変化が、処理されないままスナップショットに入り、待機がその変化に気づかない)。書き込みに失敗したのに反映した値は、次の差分が食い違いとして見つけ、次のターンで直す。壊れていれば作り直す。

## `snapshot.json` の様式

持つ値は、計画の R21 の「見つける変化」の一覧から決め、一覧に無い値 (タイトル・本文・出来事など) は持たない。

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | 様式の版 (`1`) |
| `taken_at` | Project を読んだ時刻 (UTC) |
| `project_id` | Project の ID |
| `items` | 項目のキー (`owner/repo#番号`) → 下の表。Issue 以外の項目 (draft issue・PR) は持たない |
| `comment_prs` | 開いている項目のコメント (`PR の報告` の本文の URL と、`待機` の理由 `小さな PR` の PR。書き手がトークンのログインのものだけ) に書かれた PR の URL → `state`・`draft`・`merged`。どの割り当てのものかは区別しない (意味づけは U13)。閉じた項目のコメントは読まない |

項目の値:

| キー | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `item_id` / `position` | 項目の ID・位置 (1 始まり) |
| `state` | `OPEN` / `CLOSED` |
| `status` | Status の名前 (無ければ null) |
| `fields` | フィールド名 → `value` (テキストか選択肢の名前) と `updated_at`。Status は含まない |
| `assignees` / `labels` | 担当者のログイン・ラベルの名前 (名前の順) |
| `blocked_by` | blocker のキー → `OPEN` / `CLOSED` |
| `body_edited_at` | 本文の最新の編集の時刻 (作成も編集に数える) |
| `comment_ids` | 読んだコメントの `database_id` (昇順) |
| `prs` | Issue を閉じる参照の PR の URL → `state`・`draft`・`merged` (閉じたものも含む) |

## 差分の種類と処理の順

`observe diff` は、スナップショットと今の Project (と PR の状態) の違いを、下の表の順 (計画の R12 の処理の順: 人の変更 → close・reopen と項目の除去 → `blockedBy` → コメント → PR → 項目の追加・並び順・本文の編集) に並べて返す。同じ種類の中は今の位置の順。要素は `kind`・`item` (コメントの URL の PR は null) と、種類ごとの値。

| 順 | 種類 (`kind`) | 条件 | 値 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `status` | Status の名前が違う | `before`・`after` |
| 2 | `field` | フィールドの値が違う (前にあって今は無い = 人が空にした、も含む。`Agent stuck state` を空にした・`Agent session ID` を別の値にした、はこれ) | `field`・`before`・`after` |
| 3 | `assignees` | 担当者が違う | `added`・`removed` |
| 4 | `labels` | ラベルが違う | `added`・`removed` |
| 5 | `closed` | 開いていた Issue が閉じた (`Done` を書く呼び出しは無い。組み込みワークフローが書く) | `before`・`after` |
| 6 | `reopened` | 閉じていた Issue が開いた | `before`・`after` |
| 7 | `removed` | 項目が Project から除かれた | `position` (前の位置) |
| 8 | `blocked_by` | blocker が足された・外された・開閉が変わった | `added`・`removed`・`state_changed` (`key`・`before`・`after`) |
| 9 | `comment` | コメントが足された | `ids` (足されたコメントの `database_id`) |
| 10 | `pr` | PR の状態 (`state`・`draft`・`merged`) が違う、または PR が現れた・消えた | `url`・`source` (`reference` Issue を閉じる参照 / `comment` コメントの URL)・`before`・`after` |
| 11 | `added` | 項目が Project に足された | `position` |
| 12 | `position` | 位置が変わった | `before`・`after` |
| 13 | `body_edit` | 本文の最新の編集の時刻が違う | `before`・`after` |

確認の対象か・割り当て中か・誰が足した blocker か・どの宣言が待っていたか、といった意味づけはここではしない (U13)。

## 書いた値の反映

書き込みのサブコマンド (`project set-status` / `issue add-label` / `blocked-by add` / `comment post`。後の単位の書き込みのサブコマンドも同じ) は、引数 `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` があれば、書いた値だけをスナップショットに反映する (関数 `reflect`)。読み取りの後にほかの人が変えた値は反映しない。スナップショットが無い・壊れている・項目が無いときは反映せず、出力の `snapshot.warnings` で知らせ、書き込みの結果は変えない。作業のセッションは管理ディレクトリを持たないので指定しない。

反映の操作: `status` (`value`)・`field` (`field`・`value`)・`comment` (`id`)・`blocked_by` (`action` `add` / `remove`・`blocker`・`state`)・`labels` / `assignees` (`add`・`remove`)。

## CLI

| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project items --project <owner>/<番号> --write-snapshot --dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` (GitHub には書かない) | 引数 `--write-snapshot` は `--dir` と一緒に指定する。`project items` の出力に `snapshot` (`path`・`taken_at`・`comment_prs`) を足す。コメントの URL の PR が読めなければ `problems` (`what`: `comment-pr`) に入れて `partial` |
| `observe diff --dir <管理ディレクトリ> --project <owner>/<番号>` | 無し | `diffs` (上の表の順)・`snapshot_taken_at`・`problems`・`rate_limit`。スナップショットが無い・壊れていれば `errors` (key `snapshot`) で、`gh` は実行しない。スナップショットにある `comment_prs` の PR は、コメントが消えていても状態を読み直す (待っていた PR の変化を見つけるため) |
| 書き込みのサブコマンドの `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` | `snapshot.json` | 出力に `snapshot` (`reflected`・`warnings`) を足す |

- Skill ツールで code-review を、引数 `high 1121e88..e879c51` で呼びました。

**誤りの報告:** 結果の YAML を最初に書いたとき、テストを実行しないまま「OK」と書いていました。その後で実行すると失敗が 1 件あったので、`tests_run` を正しい結果に直し、指摘 4 を足しました。

**指摘**
1. **P2・confidence high** — ファイル `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch.py` の L286
   - CLI の `observe diff` は、Project の一部しか読めなかった結果をそのまま全量のスナップショットと比べます。
   - そのため、読めなかっただけの項目を「Project から除かれた」(`removed`) として返します。
   - 偽の gh で、2 ページ目の読み取りを HTTP 502 で失敗させると、2 項目が `removed` として返りました。
   - `project items --write-snapshot` も、一部だけの読み取りをそのまま保存します。そのため次の差分では、読めなかった項目が「足された」(`added`) になります。
2. **P3** — ファイル `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/observe.py` の L47
   - スナップショットの一時ファイルの名前が `snapshot.json.tmp` に固定されています。
   - これは、文書 `records.md` の一時名の決まり (`.` で始まり `.tmp` で終わる名前) に合いません。
   - 名前が固定なので、2 つの書き手が同じ一時ファイルを使います。
3. **P3・confidence medium** — 同じファイルの L183
   - 位置 (`position`) は読んだ順の番号です。そのため、項目を 1 つ足すと後ろの項目の番号がすべてずれ、並べ替えていないのに全部に「位置が変わった」差分が出ます。
   - 先頭に 1 項目を足すと、残りの 3 項目すべてに `position` の差分が出ることを確かめました。
4. **P3・confidence high** — ファイル `issue-dispatch/tests/test_observe.py` の L332
   - テスト `test_doc_lists_kinds` が失敗します。
   - テストは、文書に「`` `--snapshot-dir` ``」と書かれていることを確かめます。一方、文書は値まで含めて「`` `--snapshot-dir <管理ディレクトリ>` ``」と書いています。
   - 2 回実行して、どちらも 320 件中 1 件の失敗でした。作業ツリーは HEAD のままです。

**`residual` に入れたもの**
- スナップショットの読み込みは、項目の中の形を確かめません。そのため、形が崩れたファイルでは差分の計算が KeyError で終わります。
- `project set-status` の `--snapshot-dir` は、スナップショットを 2 回読みます。

- 偽の gh の置き場は、シンボリックリンクを見て確かめてから使いました。偽の gh が受けた引数の記録を見ると、呼び出しは `api graphql` と `api user` だけで、すべて偽の gh に届いていました。本物の gh は実行していません。

surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR

or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.

path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each

already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.
