content.text:
Review target: `2b6a12d..0508b3b`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `0508b3b..c1bc1cd`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

 issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/observe.py   | 82 ++++++++++++++--------

diff --git a/issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/observe.py b/issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/observe.py
index 1ab875e..00439be 100644
--- a/issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/observe.py
+++ b/issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/observe.py
@@ -21,6 +21,9 @@ ITEM_KEYS = ("item_id", "position", "state", "status", "fields", "assignees", "l
 LIST_PROBLEMS = ("items-page", "graphql-errors")
 # 差分の種類と処理の順 (observation.md の表): 人の変更 → close・reopen と項目の除去 → blockedBy → コメント → PR → 項目の追加・並び順・本文の編集
 DIFF_KINDS = ("status", "field", "assignees", "labels", "closed", "reopened", "removed", "blocked_by", "comment", "pr", "added", "position", "body_edit")
+# 1 項目の中の欠けの種類 (project items の problems の what) → その欠けが狂わせる値の差分の種類 (比べない)。対応に無い種類は項目全体を比べない
+PARTIAL_SKIPS = {"labels-truncated": ("labels",), "blocked_by-truncated": ("blocked_by",), "body_edits-truncated": ("body_edit",),
+                 "prs-truncated": ("pr",), "fields-truncated": ("field",), "comments": ("comment",), "events": ()}
 # コメントの本文から PR を読む種類
 PR_URL_COMMENT_KINDS = ("PR の報告",)
 _PR_URL_RE = re.compile(rf"https://github\.com/{ids.REPO_NAME_PATTERN}/pull/[1-9][0-9]*")
@@ -100,7 +103,8 @@ def build_snapshot(items_result, comment_prs, taken_at):
 
 
 def skipped(before, after):
-    """2 つのスナップショットで比べない項目と PR (どちらかで欠けがあるもの)。返り値は {"items": {キー: 欠けの種類}, "prs": {URL: 理由}}。"""
+    """2 つのスナップショットで欠けがある項目と PR (どちらかで欠けがあるもの)。項目は欠けの種類が狂わせる値だけを比べず (diff)、
+    PR は比べない。返り値は {"items": {キー: 欠けの種類}, "prs": {URL: 理由}}。"""
     items = {}
     for snap in (before, after):
         for key, it in snap["items"].items():
@@ -183,46 +187,64 @@ def _kind_index(kind):
     return DIFF_KINDS.index(kind)
 
 
+def _omitted_kinds(partial):
+    """項目の欠けの種類 (前後の partial の和) から、比べない差分の種類の集合を返す。対応 (PARTIAL_SKIPS) に無い種類があれば、
+    どの値が狂うか分からないので None (項目のすべての値を比べない)。"""
+    if any(what not in PARTIAL_SKIPS for what in partial):
+        return None
+    return {kind for what in partial for kind in PARTIAL_SKIPS[what]}
+

+def _item_diffs(key, b, a):
+    """両方にある 1 項目の値の違い (欠けは見ない)。"""
+    out = []

content.text:
Review target: `c1bc1cd..b68a27e`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `b68a27e..4f88e38`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or

patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared

content.text:
Review target: `b23b5e7..5814ae0`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

    90	def current_pr(item, cs, asg, pr_states, login):

   103	            if got.get("author") == login and got.get("pr"):

   147	def assignment_end(item, cs, asg, pr):

   149	    正常な終わりは、Issue が閉じていて進行中でない (今の割り当ての PR が、読んだ時点で ready for review かマージ済み) こと。
   150	    Issue が開いている (reopen された) ときは、今の割り当ての最新の `ClosedEvent` があり、その close の時点で PR が ready for review か
   151	    マージ済みだった (PR がマージ済み、または close より前に作られた PR が読んだ時点で draft でない) ことで正常な終わりと読む
   152	    (PR の timeline は読まないので、close の時点で draft だった PR が reopen の後に ready になった場合は見分けられない。flow.md)。

   178	def declaration_json(text):
   179	    """宣言の本文の JSON のコードブロックを読む。返り値は (dict, None) か (None, 理由)。"""
   180	    m = _JSON_BLOCK_RE.search(text or "")
   181	    if not m:
   182	        return None, "JSON のコードブロック (```json ... ```) が無い"
   183	    try:
   184	        obj = json.loads(m.group(1))
   185	    except ValueError as e:
   186	        return None, f"JSON として読めない: {e}"
   187	    if not isinstance(obj, dict) or not isinstance(obj.get("files"), list) or not isinstance(obj.get("resources"), list) \
   188	            or any(not isinstance(f, dict) or "path" not in f or "units" not in f for f in obj["files"]):
   189	        return None, "宣言の形 (files の配列 (path と units) と resources の配列) ではない"
   190	    return obj, None

   193	def declarations(cs, asg):

   195	    out = []
   196	    for c in _for_assignment(cs, asg):
   197	        if c["header"]["role"] != "worker" or c["header"]["kind"] not in ("着手の宣言", "宣言の更新"):
   198	            continue
   199	        obj, error = declaration_json(c["text"])
   200	        out.append({"comment_id": c["database_id"], "at": c["created_at"], "kind": c["header"]["kind"], "declaration": obj, "error": error})

   204	def results_for(cs, asg, decl_id):
   205	    """宣言 (コメントの ID) への判定の結果: {"go": 最新の `開始可`, "waits": `待機` の配列 (投稿の順), "returned": 最新の `依頼` (宣言の書き直し)}。
   206	    要素は {"comment_id", "at"} (`待機` は "reasons" も)。"""
   207	    out = {"go": None, "waits": [], "returned": None}
   208	    for c in _for_assignment(cs, asg):
   209	        h = c["header"]
   210	        if h["role"] != "manager" or h["values"].get("declaration") != decl_id:
   211	            continue
   212	        entry = {"comment_id": c["database_id"], "at": c["created_at"]}
   213	        if h["kind"] == "開始可":
   214	            out["go"] = entry
   215	        elif h["kind"] == "待機":
   216	            out["waits"].append({**entry, "reasons": h["values"]["waits"]})
   217	        elif h["kind"] == "依頼" and h["values"].get("request_kind") == "宣言の書き直し":
   218	            out["returned"] = entry
   219	    return out

   226	def declaration_stage(item, cs, asg, project_number):
   227	    """今の割り当ての判定の要る最新の宣言 (R20) と、その段階・判定の結果・管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` か・戻り先・自分が足した blockedBy・
   228	    持っている資源。判定の要る宣言は、着手の宣言と宣言の更新のうち、`開始可` の後の資源を外すだけの更新 (resources-removed-only) を除いたもの。
   229	    差し戻された宣言を書き直した更新は、資源を外しただけでも判定の要る宣言。段階は、その宣言への最新の判定の結果 (`開始可` → go、
   230	    `待機` → waiting、`依頼` (宣言の書き直し) → returned、無ければ undecided)。"""
   231	    go_declaration, later, judged, prev_returned = None, [], None, False
   232	    for d in declarations(cs, asg):
   233	        res = results_for(cs, asg, d["comment_id"])
   234	        if d["declaration"] is None:
   235	            kind, needs = None, True
   236	        else:
   237	            kind = declaration.update_kind(go_declaration, d["declaration"], declaration.held_resources(go_declaration, later))
   238	            needs = kind != "resources-removed-only" or prev_returned
   239	        if needs:
   240	            judged = {**d, "update_kind": kind}
   241	        prev_returned = res["returned"] is not None
   242	        if prev_returned or d["declaration"] is None:
   243	            continue
   244	        if res["go"]:
   245	            go_declaration, later = d["declaration"], []
   246	        else:
   247	            later.append(d["declaration"])
   248	    held = sorted(declaration.held_resources(go_declaration, later))
   249	    out = {"judged": judged, "stage": None, "go": None, "wait": None, "returned": None, "manager_blocked": False, "blocked_wait": None,
   250	           "return_status": None, "own_blockers": [], "go_declaration": go_declaration, "held": held}
   251	    if judged is None:
   252	        return out
   253	    res = results_for(cs, asg, judged["comment_id"])
   254	    out["go"], out["returned"] = res["go"], res["returned"]
   255	    out["wait"] = res["waits"][-1] if res["waits"] else None
   256	    latest = max([x for x in (("go", res["go"]), ("waiting", out["wait"]), ("returned", res["returned"])) if x[1]], key=lambda x: x[1]["at"], default=None)
   257	    out["stage"] = latest[0] if latest else "undecided"
   258	    # 管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked`: 理由に Issue か 小さな PR を含む `待機` の後に `開始可` が無く、Status が Blocked で、Blocked への変化がその `待機` より後
   259	    go_at = res["go"]["at"] if res["go"] else None
   260	    blocking_waits = [w for w in res["waits"] if _blocking_reasons(w["reasons"]) and (go_at is None or w["at"] > go_at)]
   261	    if blocking_waits:
   262	        out["own_blockers"] = sorted({ids.issue_key(r["issue"]) for w in blocking_waits for r in _blocking_reasons(w["reasons"])})
   263	        first = blocking_waits[0]
   264	        status_events = [e for e in _events(item, "ProjectV2ItemStatusChangedEvent")
   265	                         if e.get("project_number") == project_number and e.get("status") == "Blocked" and (e.get("at") or "") >= first["at"]]
   266	        if (item.get("status") or {}).get("name") == "Blocked" and status_events:
   267	            out["manager_blocked"], out["blocked_wait"], out["return_status"] = True, first["comment_id"], "In Progress"
   268	    return out

   273	def labels_at(item, at):
   274	    """ある時点 (at) に付いていたラベル: その時点までの LabeledEvent・UnlabeledEvent を時刻の順に全部読んで求める (R24 の決まり (6))。"""
   275	    labels = set()
   276	    for e in item.get("events") or []:
   277	        if (e.get("at") or "") > at or not e.get("label"):
   278	            continue
   279	        if e.get("type") == "LabeledEvent":
   280	            labels.add(e["label"])
   281	        elif e.get("type") == "UnlabeledEvent":
   282	            labels.discard(e["label"])
   283	    return labels

   286	def reserved_resources(item, asg, attrs_table):

   288	    names = sorted(l[len(LABEL_PREFIX):] for l in labels_at(item, asg["at"]) if l.startswith(LABEL_PREFIX) and len(l) > len(LABEL_PREFIX))

   292	def resource_usage(states):
   293	    """資源の使用 (資源の名前 → 持つ項目のキーの配列。resources.judge_* の usage): 割り当て中の項目の予約した資源と持っている資源。
   294	    待っている宣言が新しく要る資源は `開始可` まで持たない (held は `開始可` の宣言から導くため)。"""
   295	    usage = {}
   296	    for s in states:
   297	        if not s.get("assigned"):
   298	            continue
   299	        for name in list(s.get("reserved") or []) + list((s.get("declaration") or {}).get("held") or []):
   300	            key = next((k for k in usage if k.casefold() == name.casefold()), name)
   301	            if s["key"] not in usage.setdefault(key, []):
   302	                usage[key].append(s["key"])
   303	    return usage

   308	def _request_done(req, cs, asg, pr_states):
   309	    """`依頼` を行ったか (GitHub から判断できるものだけ。R28)。"""
   310	    v = req["header"]["values"]
   311	    kind = v["request_kind"]
   312	    later = _after(cs, req["created_at"])
   313	    if kind == "宣言の書き直し":
   314	        return any(c["header"]["role"] == "worker" and c["header"]["kind"] == "宣言の更新" for c in later)
   315	    if kind == "本文の追記":
   316	        got = pr_states.get(ids.parse_pr_url(v["pr"])["url"]) or {}
   317	        return got.get("status") == "ok" and bool(got.get("pr")) and any(ids.same_issue(i["key"], asg["item_key"]) for i in got["pr"].get("issues") or [])
   318	    if kind == "小さな PR":
   319	        return any(comments.match_report(req["header"], c["header"]) for c in later)
   320	    return False

   314	        return any(c["header"]["role"] == "worker" and c["header"]["kind"] == "宣言の更新" for c in later)
   315	    if kind == "本文の追記":
   316	        got = pr_states.get(ids.parse_pr_url(v["pr"])["url"]) or {}
   317	        return got.get("status") == "ok" and bool(got.get("pr")) and any(ids.same_issue(i["key"], asg["item_key"]) for i in got["pr"].get("issues") or [])
   318	    if kind == "小さな PR":
   319	        return any(comments.match_report(req["header"], c["header"]) for c in later)
   320	    return False
   321	
   322	
   323	def pending_requests(item, cs, asg, session_id, pr_states):
   324	    """自分宛てで今の割り当ての番号の `依頼` のうち、まだ行っていないもの (投稿の順)。要素は {"comment_id", "at", "kind", "values"}。"""
   325	    out = []
   326	    for c in _for_assignment(cs, asg):
   327	        h = c["header"]
   328	        if h["role"] != "manager" or h["kind"] != "依頼" or h["values"]["to"] != session_id:
   329	            continue
   330	        if not _request_done(c, cs, {**asg, "item_key": item["key"]}, pr_states or {}):
   331	            out.append({"comment_id": c["database_id"], "at": c["created_at"], "kind": h["values"]["request_kind"], "values": h["values"]})
   332	    return out
   333	
   334	
   335	def third_party_edits(item, asg, login):
   336	    """コメント `割り当て` より後の、トークンのログイン以外による本文の編集 (時刻の順)。"""
   337	    return [{"editor": e.get("editor"), "edited_at": e.get("edited_at")} for e in sorted(item.get("body_edits") or [], key=lambda e: e.get("edited_at") or "")
   338	            if (e.get("edited_at") or "") > asg["at"] and e.get("editor") != login]
   339	
   340	
   341	def work_check(item, session_id, login, pr_states):
   342	    """作業のセッションの確認 (`work check`。R27): フィールドが自分の ID か・自分宛ての今の割り当ての `割り当て` があるか・今の番号の `解放`・
   343	    まだ行っていない `依頼`・`割り当て` より後の第三者の本文の編集 (確認の対象かは呼び出し元が決める)。"""
   344	    cs = parsed_comments(item, login)
   345	    asg = assignment(cs)
   346	    field = ((item.get("fields") or {}).get("Agent session ID") or {}).get("text")
   347	    out = {"key": item["key"], "field_is_mine": field == session_id, "assignment": asg, "assigned_to_me": bool(asg) and asg["to"] == session_id,
   348	           "released": None, "pending_requests": [], "third_party_edits": []}
   349	    if not out["assigned_to_me"]:
   350	        return out
   351	    out["released"] = release(cs, asg)
   352	    out["pending_requests"] = pending_requests(item, cs, asg, session_id, pr_states)
   353	    out["third_party_edits"] = third_party_edits(item, asg, login)
   354	    return out
   355	
   356	
   357	def work_held(items, session_id, login, pr_states, project_number):
   358	    """作業のセッションが持っている Issue (`work held`。R26): 自分宛ての今の割り当てで割り当て中 (閉じて利用者の答えを待つ Issue を含む) のものを
   359	    Project の順に。要素は key・state・status・判定の要る宣言の ID (judged) と更新の種類・それへの `開始可`・`待機` の有無・
   360	    `Blocked` が管理のセッションのものか・まだ行っていない `依頼`。"""

   370	                    "judged": d["judged"]["comment_id"] if d["judged"] else None, "update_kind": d["judged"]["update_kind"] if d["judged"] else None,
   371	                    "stage": d["stage"], "has_go": d["go"] is not None, "has_wait": d["wait"] is not None, "manager_blocked": d["manager_blocked"],
   372	                    "pending_requests": pending_requests(item, parsed_comments(item, login), s["assignment"], session_id, pr_states)})

   378	def derive(item, login, pr_states, project_number, attrs_table=None):

1	# 処理の流れ (項目の状態)
     2	
     3	このファイルが、この仕組み (issue-dispatch) の、管理のセッションがターンのたびに導く**項目の状態**の正本 (計画の R24・KTD19)。状態ごとの出どころ (GitHub のどこから導くか) と判断の基準、場面ごとの扱い、`item state` と作業のセッションの確認 (`work check`・`work held`) が返す値をここに書く。宣言の判定の節は U15 で、割り当ての節は U16 で、状態遷移の図と決定表は U21 で足す。モジュール `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/itemstate.py` が導出を実装し、`gh` は実行しない (項目は `project items`、`PR の報告` の PR の状態は `pr 
     4	
     5	割り当ての無い項目の `Blocked` の導出・人の変更の見分け・途中で止まった書き込みの続き・利用者に尋ねる場面・記録を失ったときの扱いは、この文書の次の版 (U13 の後半) で足す。
     6	
     7	## 項目の状態の出どころ
     8	
     9	状態ごとに出どころを 1 つに決める。導出・作業のセッションの確認・待機の終わる条件 (U14) は、どれもこの表の出どころを読む。Status (利用者と組み込みワークフローも変える) と担当者では決めない。
    10	
    11	| 状態 | 出どころ | 書き手と書く順 |
    12	| --- | --- | --- |
    13	| 割り当て中か (`assigned`) | 今の割り当てのコメント `割り当て` (宛先と番号) があり、その番号の `解放` が無く、正常な終わり (下の行) もしていない。進行中の Issue が閉じて、利用者の問いに答えが出ていない間は割り当て中。担当者と Status では決めない | 管理 (`Agent session ID` は排他の印で、コメントより先) |
    14	| 割り当ての終わり (`end`) と reopen (`reopened`) | 終わり = 今の番号の `解放` (`kind` が `released`) か、正常な終わり (`kind` が `normal`): Issue が閉じていて、進行中 (`in_progress`) でない。進行中 = 今の割り当ての PR が無いか、読んだ時点で ready for review にもマージ済みにもなっていない。閉じたもの (`ClosedEvent` の `closer`) は問わない。Issue が開いている (reopen された) ときは、今の割り当ての最新の `ClosedEvent` の時点で PR が ready for review かマージ済みだった (PR がマージ済み、または close より前に作られた PR が読んだ時点で dr
    15	| 宣言の段階 (`declaration`) | 今の割り当ての判定の要る最新の宣言 (`judged`) と、その宣言への `開始可`・`待機`・宣言の書き直しの `依頼` のうち最新のもの | 作業 (宣言)・管理 (結果のコメント → Status → 合図) |
    16	| 待っているもの・自分が足した `blockedBy` (`own_blockers`)・管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` (`manager_blocked`) | 判定の要る最新の宣言への、最新の `開始可` より後の `待機` の理由と相手。管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` かは、理由に `Issue` か `小さな PR` を含む最初の `待機` と、`Blocked` への Status の変化の時刻で見分ける (下の基準) | 管理 (`待機` → 理由が `Issue` か `小さな PR` のときだけ `blockedBy` → `Blocked` → 合図。資源・設定・利用者の答えの理由では Status を変えない) |
    17	| 今の割り当ての PR (`pr`) | 今の割り当て (`割り当て` より後) の最新の `PR の報告` の本文の URL の PR (作者がトークンのログインと違えば無いものとする)。無ければ、Issue を閉じる参照の PR (`closedByPullRequestsReferences`) のうち、作者がトークンのログインで、作成が `割り当て` より後のもの (複数なら作成が最新)。この行が「今の割り当ての PR」の唯一の出どころ。`PR の報告` の PR が読めなければ、PR は無しとして `problems` (`what` が `pr-unreadable`) で知らせ、閉じる参照の PR には戻らない (読めるようになれば報告の PR 
    18	| 資源の使用 (`reserved`・`held`) | 予約 = コメント `割り当て` の時点で付いていたラベル `resource:<名前>` のうち、属性 `reserve` が `on_assign` のもの。持っている資源 (定義の正本は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「更新の種類」。差し戻された宣言は数えない)。空いていない資源がある宣言は、`開始可` まで何も持たない | 利用者 (ラベル)・作業 (宣言)・管理 (`開始可`) |
    19	| 小さな PR | `待機` の理由の `小さな PR` と依頼先の Issue (と、報告の後は PR の URL) | 管理 (依頼・`待機`)・作業 (報告) |
    20	| 割り当ての無い項目の `Blocked`・担当者の変化・記録だけにあるもの | 次の版で書く | |
    21	
    22	**判断の基準** (場面ごとの扱いを決めるときに使う):
    23	
    24	- 時刻は、コメントの投稿の時刻と Issue の出来事 (`ClosedEvent`・`ReopenedEvent`・`LabeledEvent`・`UnlabeledEvent`・`ProjectV2ItemStatusChangedEvent` など) の時刻で比べる。出来事の書き手 (`actor`) は使えない (管理のセッションと利用者は同じアカウントで書く)。Status の出来事は、この Project のもの (`project_number`) だけを見る。
    25	- ある時点の状態 (そのとき付いていたラベルなど) は、その時点までの出来事を時刻の順に全部読んで求める。最初や最新の出来事だけで決めない。
    26	- 書き手がトークンのログインと違う先頭行のコメントは、この仕組みのコメントとして扱わない ([issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「コメント」)。
    27	- 宛先と番号を持つ種類のコメント (`開始可`・`待機`・`解放`・`依頼`) は、今の割り当ての宛先と番号のものだけを使う。前の割り当てのものは使わない。
    28	- 同じ場面に 2 つの決まりが当たるときは、利用者の変更を上書きしないほうを選ぶ。
    29	
    30	**決めたこと**:
    31	
    32	- マージされずに閉じた PR は、draft でなければ ready for review と読む (読んだ時点の `state`・`merged`・`draft` で判定するため)。
    33	- 今の割り当ての PR の候補が複数あるとき (閉じる参照の PR が今の割り当ての後に複数) は、作成が最新のものを使う。
    34	- 開いている Issue の正常な終わりの判定は、close の時点で PR が draft だった後に ready になった場合を見分けられない (PR の timeline を読まないため)。見分けが要ると分かったら、`pr observe` に PR の出来事を足す。
    35	- 管理のセッションが書いた `Blocked` は、判定の要る最新の宣言への `待機` のうち、理由に `Issue` か `小さな PR` を含み、最新の `開始可` より後の最初のものがあり、Status が `Blocked` で、`Blocked` への Status の変化の時刻がその `待機` 以後のもの。変化が `待機` より前なら利用者が付けたもの (`manager_blocked` は偽)。戻り先 (`return_status`) は `In Progress`。
    36	- JSON のコードブロックが読めない宣言も、判定の要る宣言にする (`declaration` は null で `error` に理由。管理のセッションが差し戻す)。
    37	
    38	## 宣言の段階
    39	
    40	判定の要る宣言は、着手の宣言と宣言の更新のうち、`開始可` の後の資源を外すだけの更新 (`resources-removed-only`) を除いたもの。差し戻された (宣言の書き直しの `依頼` がある) 宣言を書き直した更新は、資源を外しただけでも判定の要る宣言。差し戻された宣言は、持っている資源の計算に入れない。
    41	
    42	| 段階 (`stage`) | 条件 |
    43	| --- | --- |
    44	| null | 今の割り当ての宣言が無い (何も求めず、作業のセッションの宣言を待つ) |
    45	| `undecided` | 判定の要る最新の宣言に、判定の結果 (`開始可`・`待機`・宣言の書き直しの `依頼`) が無い |
    46	| `go` | 最新の結果が `開始可` (作業中) |
    47	| `waiting` | 最新の結果が `待機` (`wait` に理由と相手) |
    48	| `returned` | 最新の結果が宣言の書き直しの `依頼` |
    49	
    50	## 場面ごとの扱い
    51	
    52	テストで決めた扱い (テストの名前に場面を書く。`issue-dispatch/tests/test_itemstate.py`)。
    53	
    54	| 場面 | 読み方 |
    55	| --- | --- |
    56	| フィールドに ID があるが、コメント `割り当て` が無い | 割り当て中ではない (出どころはコメント) |
    57	| 前の割り当ての `解放` があり、新しい `割り当て` がある | 新しい割り当てが今の割り当て。前の `解放` は数えない |
    58	| 割り当て中の項目の Status が `Todo` にされた | 終わりでも reopen でもない。割り当て中のまま (割り当てを解除するかの問いは次の版) |
    59	| Issue が閉じていて、今の割り当ての PR がマージ済み・ready for review (開いている)・マージされずに閉じた (draft でない) | 正常な終わり (`end.kind` が `normal`) |
    60	| Issue が閉じていて、今の割り当ての PR が無い・draft | 進行中の close。割り当て中のまま (利用者の答えを待つ) |
    61	| reopen の後の割り当てで、前の割り当てのマージ済みの PR だけがある | 今の割り当ての PR は無い。進行中 |
    62	| 正常な終わりか `解放` の後に `ReopenedEvent` | `reopened` (次の版でフィールドを空にして報告する) |
    63	| 進行中の close の後の `ReopenedEvent` | 終わった後の reopen ではない (答えを待つ間の reopen) |
    64	| `PR の報告` の PR の作者がトークンのログインと違う | 無いものとし、閉じる参照の PR を使う |
    65	| `PR の報告` の PR が Issue を閉じる参照を持たない | `pr.closing` が偽 (`In review` にせず本文の追記を頼む材料) |
    66	| `待機` の理由が `利用者の答え`・`資源`・`設定` だけ | Status を変えない理由なので、Status が `Blocked` でも管理のセッションのものではない |
    67	| `待機` (理由に `Issue` か `小さな PR`) の後に `開始可` | 作業中 (`go`)。`own_blockers` は空 |
    68	| `開始可` の後の、資源を外すだけの更新 | 判定の要る宣言は `開始可` の宣言のまま。持っている資源は減る |
    69	| `開始可` の後の、ファイルを変えた更新 | 判定の要る宣言はその更新 (`undecided`)。持っている資源は `開始可` の宣言のもののまま |
    70	| 割り当ての後に利用者が足したラベルの資源 | 予約していない (`reserved` に入らない。宣言のときに空きを確かめる) |
    71	
    72	## `item state` が返す値
    73	
    74	| キー | 内容 |
    75	| --- | --- |
    76	| `key` | 項目 (`owner/repo#番号`) |
    77	| `assignment` | 今の割り当て (`to` 宛先・`number` 番号・`comment_id`・`at`)。無ければ null (以下のキーは初期値) |
    78	| `release` | 今の番号の `解放` (`comment_id`・`at`・`reason`)。無ければ null |
    79	| `pr` | 今の割り当ての PR (`url`・`source` (`report` / `reference`)・`state`・`draft`・`merged`・`closing` (Issue を閉じる参照に割り当ての Issue を含むか)・`base_ref`・`created_at`)。無ければ null |
    80	| `in_progress` | 進行中か |
    81	| `end` | 割り当ての終わり (`kind` が `released` / `normal`・`at`・`released` なら `reason`)。無ければ null |
    82	| `assigned` | 割り当て中か |
    83	| `reopened` | 終わった後の reopen (`at`)。無ければ null |
    84	| `declaration` | `judged` (判定の要る最新の宣言: `comment_id`・`at`・`kind`・`declaration` (JSON。読めなければ null)・`error`・`update_kind`)・`stage`・`go`・`wait` (`comment_id`・`at`・`reasons`)・`returned`・`manager_blocked`・`blocked_wait` (その `待機` の ID)・`return_status`・`own_blockers` (Issue の参照の配列)・`go_declaration`・`held` (名前の順) |
    85	| `reserved` | 割り当てのときに予約した資源 (名前の順) |
    86	| `problems` | 導出を続けられるが知らせるもの (`what` が `pr-unreadable`: `PR の報告` の PR が読めない) |
    87	
    88	出力の `usage` は、割り当て中の項目の `reserved` と `held` から導いた資源の使用 (資源の名前 → 持つ項目の配列。[resources.md](resources.md) の判断が読む)。
    89	
    90	## 作業のセッションの確認
    91	
    92	同じ導出の、自分の項目についての読み出し (計画の R26・R27)。書き込みの `gh` は実行しない。
    93	
    94	| サブコマンド | 返すもの |
    95	| --- | --- |
    96	| `work check` | `field_is_mine` (フィールド `Agent session ID` が自分の ID か)・`assignment`・`assigned_to_me` (今の割り当ての宛先が自分か)・`released` (今の番号の `解放`)・`pending_requests` (自分宛てで今の割り当ての番号の `依頼` のうち、まだ行っていないもの: `comment_id`・`at`・`kind`・`values`)・`third_party_edits` (`割り当て` より後の、トークンのログイン以外による本文の編集。確認の対象かは呼び出し元が決める) |

content.text:
Review target: `5814ae0..f000bad`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:

content.text:
Review target: `d8704e9..3126be4`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

+    """割り当ての無い項目の `Ready` ⇄ `Blocked` の再導出 (KTD7)。範囲は担当者が自分 1 人で、割り当て中でなく、Status が Ready か Blocked の項目。
+    開いている blocker があれば `依存の待ち` → `Blocked`、すべて閉じたら `依存の解消` → `Ready` (コメントが先)。`依存の待ち` の無い `Blocked` は
+    利用者が手で付けたものなので書き換えない。コメントの後に止まった書き込み (Status の変化がコメントより後に無い) は続きを書き (continuation)、
+    コメントより後に Status の変化があれば利用者の変更として報告する。返り値は (actions, reports)。"""
+    status = (item.get("status") or {}).get("name")
+    if state.get("assigned") or not _in_scope(item, login) or status not in STATUS_OPTIONS_FOR_DEPENDENCY:
+        return [], []
+    open_blockers = sorted(b["key"] for b in item.get("blocked_by") or [] if b.get("state") == "OPEN")
+    deps = [c for c in parsed_comments(item, login) if c["header"]["role"] == "manager" and c["header"]["kind"] in ("依存の待ち", "依存の解消")]
+    latest = deps[-1] if deps else None
+    waiting = latest is not None and latest["header"]["kind"] == "依存の待ち"
+    changed_after = bool(latest) and bool(_status_events_after(item, latest["created_at"], project_number))
+    if status == "Ready":
+        if not open_blockers:
+            return [], []
+        if waiting:
+            if changed_after:
+                return [], [_report(item, "status-changed", status=status, after_comment=latest["database_id"])]
+            return [_action_status(item, "Blocked", continuation=True)], []
+        body = "開いている blocker: " + "、".join(open_blockers)
+        return [_action_comment(item, "依存の待ち", {"blockers": open_blockers}, body), _action_status(item, "Blocked")], []

+    if waiting:
+        if open_blockers:
+            return [], []
+        return [_action_comment(item, "依存の解消", {}, "blocker がすべて閉じた"), _action_status(item, "Ready")], []

+        return [_action_status(item, "Ready", continuation=True)], []

+def human_blocked_by(item, state):

+    own = set((state.get("declaration") or {}).get("own_blockers") or [])

+# --- 記録の読み出し ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def record_lost(rec):
+    """記録を失ったか (記録が無い・管理のセッションが無い・前の記録が ended)。R24。"""

+
+
+def _rec_item(rec, key):
+    for k, v in ((rec or {}).get("items") or {}).items():
+        if ids.same_issue(k, key):
+            return v
+    return None
+
+
+def _unanswered(rec, key):
+    """項目への未回答の問い (question_id 付き)。"""
+    return [dict(q, question_id=qid) for qid, q in sorted(((rec or {}).get("questions") or {}).items())
+            if ids.same_issue(q.get("item"), key) and q.get("answered_at") is None]
+
+
+def _is_reported(rec, key, kind):
+    ri = _rec_item(rec, key)
+    return bool(ri) and kind in (ri.get("reported") or {})
+
+
+def _question(item, kind, **extra):
+    return {"kind": kind, "item": item["key"], "options": list(QUESTION_OPTIONS[kind]), **extra}
+
+
+# --- 割り当て中の項目の場面 -------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def expected_statuses(state):
+    """割り当て中の開いている項目で、管理のセッションの書き込みとして説明できる Status。理由に Issue か 小さな PR を含む `待機` の後なら Blocked、
+    それ以外は In Progress か In review。"""
+    d = state.get("declaration") or {}
+    if d.get("own_blockers"):
+        return {"Blocked"}
+    return {"In Progress", "In review"}
+
+
+def _handover_action(item, cs, rec, own_id, lost):
+    """初めて扱う項目 (記録にその項目の情報が無い) で、最後に書いた管理のセッションの ID が自分と違えば `引き継ぎ` を書く (自分の `引き継ぎ` が既にあれば書かない)。"""
+    if _rec_item(rec, item["key"]) is not None:
+        return None
+    managers = [c for c in cs if c["header"]["role"] == "manager"]
+    if not managers or sessions.same_session_id(managers[-1]["header"]["session_id"], own_id):
+        return None
+    if any(c["header"]["kind"] == "引き継ぎ" and sessions.same_session_id(c["header"]["session_id"], own_id) for c in managers):
+        return None
+    prev = managers[-1]["header"]

+    return _action_comment(item, "引き継ぎ", {}, body)

+

+    """割り当てのある項目の場面ごとの扱い (flow.md の「場面ごとの扱い」)。返り値は (actions, questions, reports)。
+    未回答の問いがある項目には手を付けない (答えを待つ間の reopen による問いの取り下げを除く)。"""
+    actions, questions, reports = [], [], []
+    cs = parsed_comments(item, login)
+    asg = state["assignment"]
+    key = item["key"]
+    status = (item.get("status") or {}).get("name")
+    handover = _handover_action(item, cs, rec, own_id, lost)
+    if handover:
+        actions.append(handover)
+    pending = _unanswered(rec, key)
+    if pending and item.get("state") == "OPEN":

+                actions.append(_action_status(item, restore))

+        if state["end"] and state["end"]["kind"] == "normal" and state["pr"] and state["pr"]["state"] == "OPEN":
+            reports.append(_report(item, "pr-left-open", url=state["pr"]["url"]))
+        return actions, questions, reports
+    if item.get("state") == "CLOSED" and state["in_progress"]:
+        questions.append(_question(item, "close-in-progress", record_lost=lost))

+    field = (item.get("fields") or {}).get(FIELD_ID) or {}
+    value, updated = field.get("text"), field.get("updated_at")
+    if value != asg["to"]:
+        if updated and updated > asg["at"]:
+            questions.append(_question(item, "field-cleared" if not value else "field-changed", value=value))
+        else:
+            actions.append({"kind": "set-field", "item": key, "item_id": item["item_id"], "field": FIELD_ID, "value": asg["to"], "continuation": True})
+            if intent.get("session_title"):
+                actions.append({"kind": "set-field", "item": key, "item_id": item["item_id"], "field": FIELD_TITLE, "value": intent["session_title"], "continuation": True})
+    expected = expected_statuses(state)
+    d = state.get("declaration") or {}
+    if item.get("state") == "OPEN" and status not in expected and not (status == "Blocked" and d.get("manager_blocked")):
+        if status not in ASSIGNED_STATUSES:
+            if _status_events_after(item, asg["at"], project_number):
+                questions.append(_question(item, "status-changed", status=status))
+            else:
+                actions.append(_action_status(item, "In Progress", continuation=True))
+    # `待機` (Issue か 小さな PR) の続き: blockedBy と Blocked
+    if d.get("own_blockers") and d.get("wait") and not d.get("manager_blocked"):
+        wait_at = d["wait"]["at"]
+        present = {b["key"] for b in item.get("blocked_by") or []}
+        for blocker in d["own_blockers"]:
+            if any(ids.same_issue(blocker, k) for k in present):
+                continue
+            removed = [e for e in _events(item, "BlockedByRemovedEvent") if e.get("blocking") and ids.same_issue(e["blocking"], blocker) and (e.get("at") or "") > wait_at]
+            if removed:
+                reports.append(_report(item, "blocked-by-removed", blockers=[blocker]))
+            else:
+                actions.append({"kind": "blocked-by-add", "item": key, "blocker": blocker, "continuation": True})
+        if status != "Blocked" and item.get("state") == "OPEN":
+            if _status_events_after(item, wait_at, project_number):

+def human_changes(diffs, items_by_key, states_by_key, rec, workflows):
+    """スナップショットの差分のうち、記録の意図 (自分の部分書き込み) と組み込みワークフローの遷移と利用者が着手を決める遷移で説明できないものを

+    for diff in diffs or []:
+        key = diff.get("item")
+        if not key:
+            continue
+        item, st = items_by_key.get(key), states_by_key.get(key)
+        assigned = bool(st and st.get("assigned"))
+        intent = (_rec_item(rec, key) or {}).get("intent") or {}
+        reopened = bool(item and _events(item, "ReopenedEvent"))
+        kind = diff.get("kind")
+        if kind == "status":
+            before, after = diff.get("before"), diff.get("after")
+            if assigned or intent.get("status") == after:
+                continue
+            if after == "Done" and item and item.get("state") == "CLOSED":
+                continue
+            if after == "Todo" and reopened and (workflows or {}).get("Item reopened"):
+                continue
+            if after == "Ready" and (before in (None, "Todo") or (before == "Done" and reopened)):
+                continue
+            reports.append({"kind": "status-changed", "item": key, "before": before, "after": after})

+        elif kind == "blocked_by" and assigned:

+            added = [b for b in diff.get("added") or [] if not any(ids.same_issue(b, o) for o in own)]

+# --- ターン ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+def derive_turn(items, rec, login, own_id, project_number, attrs_table, pr_states, diffs, workflows, config):
+    """管理のセッションのターンで、項目の状態と、行うこと (actions)・尋ねること (questions)・1 回だけ報告するもの (reports)・答えを待つ項目 (pending) を導く。
+    書き込みはしない。rec は記録 (無ければ None)。diffs は observe diff の差分 (無ければ空)。workflows は Project のワークフローの名前 → 有効か。"""
+    lost = record_lost(rec)
+    states, actions, questions, reports, pending = [], [], [], [], []
+    items_by_key, states_by_key = {}, {}
+    for item in items:
+        if not item.get("key"):
+            continue
+        st = derive(item, login, pr_states, project_number, attrs_table)
+        states.append(st)
+        items_by_key[item["key"]], states_by_key[item["key"]] = item, st
+        if st["assignment"]:
+            a, q, r = assigned_scenes(item, st, rec, login, own_id, project_number, config, pr_states, lost)
+            actions += a
+            questions += q
+            reports += r
+        a, r = dependency_actions(item, st, login, project_number)
+        actions += a
+        reports += r
+        pending += [{"question_id": q["question_id"], "item": item["key"], "kind": q["kind"], "asked_at": q["asked_at"]} for q in _unanswered(rec, item["key"])]
+    reports += human_changes(diffs, items_by_key, states_by_key, rec, workflows)
+    # 記録の意図にある項目が一覧に無い: Project から除かれた (割り当ての解除を尋ねる)
+    for key, ri in sorted(((rec or {}).get("items") or {}).items()):
+        if ri.get("intent") and not any(ids.same_issue(key, k) for k in items_by_key) and not any(q["kind"] == "removed" for q in _unanswered(rec, key)):
+            questions.append({"kind": "removed", "item": key, "options": list(QUESTION_OPTIONS["removed"])})
+    seen = set()
+    unique = []
+    for r in reports:
+        mark = (r["item"], r["kind"])
+        if mark in seen or _is_reported(rec, r["item"], r["kind"]):
+            continue
+        seen.add(mark)
+        unique.append(r)
+    return {"items": states, "usage": resource_usage(states), "actions": actions, "questions": questions, "reports": unique, "pending": pending,
