content.text:
Review target: `3126be4..0091b99`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

Review target: `96b60f7..9b1a969`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

   159	    def _sleep(self, seconds):

content.text:
Review target: `9b1a969..1b65049`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name

Review target: `28bc061..d5126eb`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

    24	def _questions(rec, item, kind, subject):
    25	    """記録の問いのうち、項目 (owner/repo の大文字小文字を区別しない)・種類・対象 (subject。大文字小文字を区別しない) が同じもの。"""

    28	            if ids.same_issue(q.get("item"), item) and q.get("kind") == kind
    29	            and (q.get("subject").casefold() if isinstance(q.get("subject"), str) else None) == folded]

    32	def answer_for(rec, item, kind, subject):
    33	    """項目・種類・対象が同じ問いの最新の答え。答えが無い (未回答・取り下げ (answer が null)) なら None。"""
    34	    answered = [q for q in _questions(rec, item, kind, subject) if q.get("answer") is not None]
    35	    if not answered:

   277	def judge_one(entry, others, rec, usage, attrs_table, repo_config, table, login):
   278	    """宣言 1 件の判定 (flow.md の「1 件の判定」)。others は比べる相手 (go_declarations の要素)、usage は資源の使用 (usage_for の結果)。
   279	    返り値: {"item", "declaration", "to", "assignment", "update_kind", "repo_config", "result" (RESULTS), "waits" (`待機` の理由), "compared" (比べた相手の宣言の ID),
   280	    "recompared" (ファイルの競合の可能性を比べたか), "reserve", "release", "keep", "parsed" (検査した宣言), "actions", "questions", "signals"}。"""
   281	    item, st, judged = entry["item"], entry["state"], entry["judged"]
   282	    key, asg, d = item["key"], st["assignment"], st["declaration"]
   283	    decl_id = judged["comment_id"]
   284	    base = {"to": asg["to"], "assignment": asg["number"], "declaration": decl_id}
   285	    j = {"item": key, "declaration": decl_id, "to": asg["to"], "assignment": asg["number"], "update_kind": judged.get("update_kind"),
   286	         "repo_config": repo_config["status"], "result": None, "waits": [], "compared": [], "recompared": False, "reserve": [], "release": [], "keep": [],
   287	         "parsed": None, "actions": [], "questions": [], "signals": []}
   288	    # 1. リポジトリの設定
   289	    rules, rule_text = rules_for(repo_config)
   290	    if rules is None:
   291	        j["result"], j["waits"] = "wait", [{"kind": "設定"}]
   292	        body = (f"リポジトリ {item['repo']} の設定を読めないので、この宣言の判定を止めている。理由: {repo_config.get('message')}。"
   293	                f"直し方: {repo_config.get('fix') or '-'}。直したら管理のセッションに知らせる (設定を直したことは GitHub に現れないため)。")
   294	        j["actions"].append(_comment(key, "待機", {**base, "waits": j["waits"]}, body))
   295	        j["signals"].append(_signal("wait", asg["to"], key, decl_id))
   296	        return j
   297	    # 2. 宣言の形
   298	    parsed, errors = _parse_mine(item, judged, rules, table)
   299	    if parsed is None:
   300	        j["result"] = "request"
   301	        body = "宣言の形の誤り:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {e}" for e in errors) + f"\n\n使った規則: {rule_text}。直した宣言を `宣言の更新` で投稿する。"
   302	        j["actions"].append(_comment(key, "依頼", {**base, "request_kind": "宣言の書き直し"}, body))
   303	        j["signals"].append(_signal("request", asg["to"], key, decl_id, "宣言の書き直し"))
   304	        return j
   305	    j["parsed"] = parsed
   306	    # 3. 競合の可能性 (ready for review の後の資源だけの更新は比べない)
   307	    recompare = not (st.get("pr") and itemstate.pr_ready(st["pr"]) and judged.get("update_kind") == "resources-only")
   308	    j["recompared"] = recompare
   309	    waits, blockers, requests, request_signals, proceeds = [], [], [], [], []
   310	    unanswered = False
   311	    if recompare:
   312	        same = [o for o in others if o["repo"].casefold() == item["repo"].casefold() and not ids.same_issue(o["item"], key)]
   313	        result = declaration.conflictability({"repo": item["repo"], "declaration": parsed},
   314	                                             [{"id": o["id"], "repo": o["repo"], "declaration": _other_files(o, rules, table)} for o in same])
   315	        j["compared"] = [o["id"] for o in same]
   316	        for o, r in zip(same, result["others"]):
   317	            other_ref = {"item": o["item"], "declaration": o["id"], "to": o["to"]}
   318	            conflict_paths = [p for p in r["paths"] if p["result"] == "conflict"]
   319	            if not conflict_paths:
   320	                # unknown-content の同じパス: 競合しうるかを利用者に尋ねる (相手の宣言とパスが対象)
   321	                for p in [p for p in r["paths"] if p["result"] == "needs-user"]:
   322	                    subject = f"{o['item']}:{o['id']}:{p['path']}"
   323	                    answer = answer_for(rec, key, "unknown-content", subject)
   324	                    if answer == "conflict":
   325	                        conflict_paths.append(p)
   326	                    elif answer is None:
   327	                        unanswered = True
   328	                        if not asked(rec, key, "unknown-content", subject):
   329	                            j["questions"].append(_question("unknown-content", key, subject, decl_id, other=other_ref, path=p["path"]))
   330	            if not conflict_paths:
   331	                continue
   332	            subject = f"{o['item']}:{o['id']}"
   333	            answer = answer_for(rec, key, "conflict", subject)
   334	            if answer is None:
   335	                unanswered = True
   336	                if not asked(rec, key, "conflict", subject):
   337	                    j["questions"].append(_question("conflict", key, subject, decl_id, other=other_ref, paths=conflict_paths))
   338	            elif answer == "wait":

24	    24	def _questions(rec, item, kind, subject):
25	    25	    """記録の問いのうち、項目 (owner/repo の大文字小文字を区別しない)・種類・対象 (subject。大文字小文字を区別しない) が同じもの。"""

1	"""宣言の判定 (計画の U15。正本は flow.md の「判定」)。
     2	
     3	項目の状態 (itemstate) が導いた「判定の要る宣言」を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定し、`開始可`・`待機`・`依頼`
     4	の書き込みの候補 (actions)・利用者に尋ねること (questions)・作業のセッションに送る合図 (signals) を返す。gh は実行せず、書き込みもしない。
     5	競合の可能性は declaration.conflictability、資源は resources.judge_declare / judge_update、リポジトリの設定は repo.read_repo_config の結果で判断する。
     6	"""
     7	
     8	import re
     9	
    10	from . import comments, declaration, filekinds, ids, itemstate, resources
    11	
    12	RESULTS = ("go", "wait", "ask", "request")
    13	SIGNAL_KINDS = ("go", "wait", "request")
    14	# 判定の問い (種類 → 選択肢)。種類の名前と選択肢の正本は records.md の問いの表
    15	QUESTION_OPTIONS = {"conflict": ["wait", "small-pr", "proceed"], "unknown-content": ["conflict", "none"], "resource-busy": ["wait", "proceed"],
    16	                    "release-undeclared": ["release", "keep"], "small-pr-closed": ["wait-issue", "redo", "proceed"]}
    17	QUESTION_KINDS = tuple(QUESTION_OPTIONS)
    18	_USER_ANSWER = {"kind": "利用者の答え"}
    19	_PR_URL_RE = re.compile(rf"https://github\.com/{ids.REPO_NAME_PATTERN}/pull/[1-9][0-9]*")
    20	
    21	
    22	# --- 記録の問いの答え ------------------------------------------------------------------
    23	
    24	def _questions(rec, item, kind, subject):
    25	    """記録の問いのうち、項目 (owner/repo の大文字小文字を区別しない)・種類・対象 (subject。大文字小文字を区別しない) が同じもの。"""
    26	    folded = subject.casefold() if isinstance(subject, str) else None
    27	    return [q for q in ((rec or {}).get("questions") or {}).values()
    28	            if ids.same_issue(q.get("item"), item) and q.get("kind") == kind
    29	            and (q.get("subject").casefold() if isinstance(q.get("subject"), str) else None) == folded]
    30	
    31	
    32	def answer_for(rec, item, kind, subject):
    33	    """項目・種類・対象が同じ問いの最新の答え。答えが無い (未回答・取り下げ (answer が null)) なら None。"""
    34	    answered = [q for q in _questions(rec, item, kind, subject) if q.get("answer") is not None]
    35	    if not answered:
    36	        return None
    37	    return max(answered, key=lambda q: q.get("answered_at") or "")["answer"]
    38	
    39	
    40	def asked(rec, item, kind, subject):
    41	    """項目・種類・対象が同じ未回答の問い (答えも取り下げも無い) が記録にあるか。あれば尋ね直さない。"""
    42	    return any(q.get("answered_at") is None for q in _questions(rec, item, kind, subject))
    43	
    44	
    45	# --- 判定の順と比べる相手 ----------------------------------------------------------------
    46	
    47	def _items_by_key(items):
    48	    return {it["key"]: it for it in items if it.get("key")}
    49	
    50	
    51	def pending(items, states):
    52	    """未判定の宣言 (判定の要る最新の宣言で、`開始可`・`待機`・`依頼` のどれも無いもの) を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に。
    53	    要素は {"item": 項目, "state": 状態, "judged": 判定の要る宣言}。"""
    54	    by_key = _items_by_key(items)
    55	    out = []
    56	    for st in states:
    57	        d = st.get("declaration") or {}
    58	        if not st.get("assigned") or not d.get("judged") or d.get("stage") != "undecided" or st["key"] not in by_key:
    59	            continue
    60	        out.append({"item": by_key[st["key"]], "state": st, "judged": d["judged"]})
    61	    return sorted(out, key=lambda e: (e["judged"]["at"] or "", e["item"].get("position") if e["item"].get("position") is not None else 0))
    62	
    63	
    64	def go_declarations(items, states, pr_states, login):
    65	    """比べる相手: 既に `開始可` になった宣言 (項目ごとに最新の `開始可` の宣言)。ready for review の後の PR が変えた、宣言に無いファイル (pr_paths) も相手に加える。
    66	    要素は {"id", "item", "repo", "declaration", "pr_paths", "to", "assignment", "comments" (項目の解析済みのコメント)}。"""
    67	    by_key = _items_by_key(items)
    68	    out = []

content.content:
## 判定

宣言の判定 (計画の R20・KTD9・KTD14・AE32・AE54)。モジュール `issue-dispatch/scripts/issue_dispatch/judge.py` (関数 `judge.judge`) と CLI の `declaration judge` がこれに従う。競合の可能性の規則は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「競合の可能性」、資源の判断は [resources.md](resources.md) の契機の表、リポジトリの設定の読み方は [repositories.md](repositories.md) が正本で、ここでは言い直さない。

**判定の順序と比較の相手**: 未判定の宣言 (判定の要る最新の宣言で、段階が `undecided` のもの) を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定する。比較の相手は、その時点で `開始可` になっている宣言 (項目ごとに最新の `開始可` の宣言) だけで、未判定の宣言どうしは比較しない。同じ実行で先に `開始可` にした宣言は後の宣言の相手になり、予約した資源は後の宣言には空いていない。相手の項目の PR が ready for review の後なら、PR が変更したファイルのうち相手の宣言に無いものも、節なしのファイルとして相手に加える (「PR が変えたファイルとの照合」と同じ出どころ)。比較の規則 (同じリポジトリの同じパスごと。別のリポジトリは競合しない) 

**1 件の判定**: 上から順に分岐し、結果 (`result`) を `go`・`wait`・`ask`・`request` のどれかに決める。

| 順 | 条件 | 結果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | リポジトリの設定が読めない (`repo.read_repo_config` が `unreadable`) | `wait`: `待機` (理由 `設定`)。本文に理由と直し方と、直したら管理のセッションに知らせることを書く。そのリポジトリの宣言は判定しない。設定ファイルが無い (`missing`) は読めないことではなく、デフォルトの表だけで照合して進む |
| 2 | 宣言の形の誤り (コメントの JSON を、リポジトリの規則で種類を付けて `declaration.parse` で検査する) | `request`: `依頼` (宣言の書き直し)。本文に誤りの一覧と使った規則 (リポジトリの設定とデフォルトの表か、デフォルトの表だけか) を書く |
| 3 | 競合の可能性 (`declaration.conflictability`) の相手ごとの結果 | 相手ごとに、記録の質問の回答で扱いを決める (下の表)。ready for review の後の資源だけを変える更新 (`resources-only`) は比較しない |
| 4 | 宣言の資源 (着手の宣言は `resources.judge_declare`、更新は `judge_update`) | [resources.md](resources.md) の契機 `declare` / `update` の行のとおり。結果 `wait` は `待機` (理由 `資源`)、`ask` は質問 `resource-busy` (対象は資源の名前) を出して回答まで `待機` (理由 `利用者の答え`)。3 で待機・質問になった宣言は 4 に進まない |
| 5 | 割り当てで予約したのに宣言に無い資源 (着手の宣言だけ。`judge_declare` の `release`・`keep`・`ask_undeclared`・`request_rewrite`) | 同じ行のとおり。`ask_undeclared` は `開始可` を書いてから質問 `release-undeclared` (対象は資源の名前) を出す。`request_rewrite` は `依頼` (宣言の書き直し: その資源を加える) にし、`開始可` は書かない |
| 6 | どれにも当たらない | `go`: `開始可`。本文に比較した相手の数・予約した資源・解放した資源を書く |

競合の可能性の相手ごとの扱い:

content.text:
Review target: `d5126eb..f18c440`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

# CLAUDE.md ## 会話と文章の規約 **日本語の文章すべてに適用する。** 会話・PR / Issue の本文・コミットメッセージ・レビューコメント・文書 ( 各リポジトリの `docs/` `.claude/` 配下を含む)・コードのコメントと docstring — 置き場所を問わない。 読み手は**その作業のコンテキストを把握していない日本語圏のエンジニア**を想定する。 書いた本人と同じ作業を追っている人には通じる書き方でも、後から読む人には意味が取れないため。 > [!NOTE] > **適用先を列挙しないのは、列挙から漏れた場所が「対象外」と読めてしまうため。** > 何を対象外にするかは各リポジトリの規約を優先する。規約がない場合は以下の2つを対象外とする。 - **コード中の識別子** (変数名・関数名・型名)。コードの一部であって文章ではない - **ログのメッセージ** テストのアサーションメッセージと `make help` の説明文は、実行時の出力だが Cloud Logging には入らないため**日本語で書く** **CI の step 名は英語でよい。** ツール名やコマンド名をそのまま使うことが多く、訳すとかえって何を実行する step か分かりにくくなるため。日本語で書いてもよい（このリポジトリには両方ある）。 ### 会話 - 常に日本語で会話する - 利用者に求めること (実行してほしいコマンド・選んでほしい選択肢・質問) は、そのターンの最後の返答に書く。デスクトップアプリはツールの実行のあいだの文章を折りたたむか要約に置き換えることがあるので、途中の文章に書いたものも最後の返答で繰り返し、「前に書いた」で済ませずに、その場で言い直す ### 語彙と文章 - CLAUDEと人間が対象を取り違えないために、正式な名称をそのまま使う。対象は、製品やサービス、ツール、ライブラリ、コマンドだけでなく、ドキュメント、セクション、UI等の画面、画面の部品など。略したり、翻訳したりする場合は明示的に略していること、翻訳していることを初出時に説明する。 - 説明のない省略・比喩・安直な英語の翻訳は使わない（**日本語圏のエンジニアに通じる言葉は許容する**） - 正しい英語を翻訳するのではなく、**日本語の文章として正しい文章**を書く - 専門用語やコンテキスト依存の造語は、**初出で説明を付ける**（不自然になる場合は括弧等を使う） - **識別子は、初出でその種類を前に添える。** テーブル・RPC・関数・型・コマンド・フラグ・環境変数・ファイル・ディレクトリなどは、「テーブル `sites`」「RPC `AssignApplication`」「関数 `CreateDeploymentPlan`」「コマンド `lappds-cli site register`」のように書く。識別子だけを書くと、読み手はそれが何の名前か (表なのか関数なのか) を文脈から推測することになる。 - **ファイルとディレクトリは、初出ではリポジトリのルートからの相対パスで書く。** 「ファイル `internal/store/site.go`」「ディレクトリ `docs/manual/units/`」のように書き、ファイル名だけ (`site.go`) を書かない。名前だけでは同名のファイルが複数あり、読み手が見つけられないことが多いため。2 回目以降は名前だけでよい。 - **識別子・製品名・サービス名は日本語に訳さない**（`main` を「主ブランチ」と書かない） - 浸透しているカタカナ語を**漢語（漢字の訳語）に置き換えない**（「既定値」ではなく「デフォルト値」） - ただし漢語も同程度に通じる言葉（検証 / 雛形 / 上書き 等）はどちらでもよい #### 避ける言い回しと言い換えの例 | 避ける | 理由 | 言い換え | |---|---|---| | テストで固定する / pin する | 「固定」「pin」が何を指すか分からない | テストで検証する / 回帰テストを足す | | 同じ型の欠陥 | 「型」を type の意味で使うと別の意味に読める | 同じ種類の / 同じパターンの | | 黙って〜する | プログラムは黙らない。擬人化した比喩 | 利用者に知らせずに / エラーを出さずに | | 黙って緑になる / 全緑 / 赤になる | 「緑」「赤」は CI の色の比喩で、文脈がないと通じない | 検査が成功したように見える / すべて成功する / 失敗する | | 穴を塞ぐ | 何の穴か分からない比喩 | 検出できない条件をなくす | | 〜に化ける | 通じない比喩 | 〜として扱われてしまう | | 素通りする | 説明のない慣用表現 | 検査されないまま通過する | | 規則に抵触する | 法律用語の流用 | 規則に反する / 規則と矛盾する | | 変異を落とす / 変異が生き残る | mutation testing（コードを意図的に壊し、検査が失敗することを確かめる手法）の用語を説明なしで使っている | 変異を検出できる / 変異が検出されずに残る | **この表は例であって、列挙で網羅するものではない。** 同種の言い回しは上の原則に照らして判断する。 **表にある表現の同義語も同じく避ける**（「素通りする」に対する「すり抜ける」「見逃す」など）。 表にある字面だけを避けて同義の表現に置き換えても、読み手に通じない点は変わらないため。 **同じ比喩を繰り返し使わない。** 一度使った不自然な言い回しは、以降の文章に複製されやすい。 ## 作成するコードについて ### 仕様や設計にないフォールバックを作成しない 例えば通信できなくて問題が起きる場合に、それが処理に必要なものであればフォールバックで別の方法で実現するのではなく、 サーバーサイドならば開発者あるいは管理者が確認できるようにエラーログを出力を行う。 CLIやブラウザ上で動くコードならばユーザーが問題を知ることができるように画面や標準エラー出力等に出力する。 ## 実装計画を立てるとき **実装計画は、層 (DB のマイグレーション・API の定義・実装・テストなど、同じ種類の作業) でまとめず、ドメインで分ける。** ドメインは、作ろうとしているゴールを分けた小さなゴールで、データモデルの単位になることが多い。層でまとめると、すべての層がそろうまで動作を確かめられず、テストまでなかなかたどり着けないため。 1. ゴールを、いくつかのドメインに分ける 2. ドメインの順序を決める。データモデルなどの参照から依存関係を確かめ、依存されるドメインを先にする 3. ドメインごとに、次の順でタスクを洗い出す 1. そのドメインのゴールを確かめるために必要なテスト (主に単体テスト) を作る作業 2. テストを通すために必要な実装の作業 3. 実装に必要なもの (API の定義・DB のマイグレーションなど) を用意する作業 4. 進める順は、ドメインごとに「実装に必要なものを用意する → テストを書く → 実装する」とする 5. Go のようにパッケージを分けられる言語では、ドメインをパッケージを分ける単位にすることも検討する。1 つのパッケージに多くのドメインが入ると、分かりにくくなるため 例: 社員と所属部署があり、社員は必ず 1 つの所属部署に属し、どちらも管理 API で扱う。社員が所属部署を参照するので、所属部署を先にする。 | 避ける (層でまとめる) | 推奨 (ドメインで分ける) | |---|---| | 1. テーブル departments と employees のマイグレーションを足す
2. department API と employee API の定義を足す
3. department API と employee API のテストと実装を足す | 1. ドメイン department: テーブル departments のマイグレーション → department API の定義 → department API のテストと実装
2. ドメイン employee: テーブル employees のマイグレーション → employee API の定義 → employee API のテストと実装 | ## Issue の作り方 ### コンテキストを残す 結論や論点を整理することは重要だが、経緯が失われると理由の正当性を検証できなくなる。 できるだけコンテキストを残す。関連する Issue や PR 、外部ドキュメント、ソースコードへのリンクを残す。 ### 解決策ではなく問題や要望を記録する Issueを作成する際には、タスクではなくその問題自身を Issue として記録する。 問題として記録せず、解決策のみを Issue として作成すると動機となった問題の原因や検討した内容などが失われてしまう。 ## 決まりを作るとき 決まり (規約・方針・書き方のルール) を、利用者に相談せずに作らない。 次のどれも、文面と理由を利用者に示して承認を得てから行う。 - CLAUDE.md・文書・skill・設定に、決まりを足す・変える - これまでの書き方の癖を、決まりとして明文化する - いまの書き方を「このリポジトリの決まり」として説明する。決まりかどうかは推測で言わず、誰がいつ決めたかを履歴 (コミット・Issue・PR) で確かめてから書く。決めた記録が無ければ、決まりではなく、これまでの書き方として説明する 理由: Claude がファイルを操作している以上、Claude が明文化した決まりは、利用者が決めたものと区別がつかなくなるため。

# コミットルール

## 基本原則

コミットは**ファイルの種類**（コード/設定/ドキュメント等）ではなく、**そのファイルを変更した動機**でグルーピングする。
以下の動機について一つのコミットの複数の動機が混じらないようにコミットする。

- ファイルの内容の追加/変更/削除
- ファイルの内容の修正
- linter による指摘への対応
- リファクタリング
- ツールによる自動のファイルの作成/更新/削除

特に linter が複数指定した場合には、一つのコミットにまとめるのではなく、項目ごとに別のコミットに分ける。


### 基本原則を実現するために

- ある作業が終わったとき: 次の作業に進む前に未コミットの変更があればコミットするべきか確認してコミットする。


## 関連する変更はまとめる

- 機能追加のコード変更 + 関連ドキュメント更新 → 同一コミット
- バグ修正のコード変更 + テスト追加 → 同一コミット
- リファクタリング + それに伴う関連コード修正 → 同一コミット
- インターフェース変更 + 全呼び出し元の修正 → 同一コミット
- 関数の削除 + 参照元の修正 → 同一コミット

## 無関係な変更は分離する

- リファクタリング（♻️）と新機能追加（✨）は別コミット
- コードのリファクタリングとドキュメントの更新は別コミット
- バグ修正と新機能の追加は別コミット
- コードの変更と無関係な設定ファイルの変更は別コミット

# CLAUDE.md

このリポジトリの文書 (Markdown) を書く・直すときの規則。

## 文書の言い回し

文書を読んだ人間やエージェントは、そこで使われている語をそのまま新しい文書・コミットメッセージ・記録に複製する。規範文書が不自然な語彙を供給すると、それがリポジトリ全体に広がる。次の 3 原則に従って書く。

2. **正しい英語を翻訳するのではなく、日本語の文章として正しい文章を書く。**

網羅的な避ける言い回しの一覧は作らない。列挙を検査の範囲にすると、一覧に無いものが検査されないまま残る。例として一覧を作ることは許容する。そのときは、一覧が例であって範囲ではないことを一覧の側に書く。一覧に無い言い回しも、この 3 原則に照らして判断する。

言い換えを決めた語と、使い続けると決めた語は、ファイル `.claude/akm-claude-plugins/wording-guard/terms.toml` に例として記録している (様式の正本はファイル [wording-guard/skills/wording-guard/references/terms.md](wording-guard/skills/wording-guard/references/terms.md))。

2. ドメイン employee: テーブル employees のマイグレーション → employee API の定義 → employee API のテストと実装 | ## Issue の作り方 ### コンテキストを残す 結論や論点を整理することは重要だが、経緯が失われると理由の正当性を検証できなくなる。 できるだけコンテキストを残す。関連する Issue や PR 、外部ドキュメント、ソースコードへのリンクを残す。 ### 解決策ではなく問題や要望を記録する Issueを作成する際には、タスクではなくその問題自身を Issue として記録する。 問題として記録せず、解決策のみを Issue として作成すると動機となった問題の原因や検討した内容などが失われてしまう。 ## 決まりを作るとき 決まり (規約・方針・書き方のルール) を、利用者に相談せずに作らない。 次のどれも、文面と理由を利用者に示して承認を得てから行う。 - skills.content:
Review target: `d5126eb..f18c440`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:setup-claude: Guided setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- skill-creator:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance.
