ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

資源の使用 (資源 → 持っている項目) は記録に書かず、割り当て・ラベル・宣言・`開始可` から、ターンのたびに導く (出どころの正本は [flow.md](flow.md) の「項目の状態の出どころ」の行「資源の使用」。関数 `itemstate.resource_usage` が導き、判定は `開始可` の後に宣言に無い予約のうち解放するものを除く (正本は [flow.md](flow.md) の「判定」の「資源の使用」))。項目が持つ資源は、割り当てで予約した資源と、持っている資源 (定義の正本は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「更新の種類」) の両方。関数 `held_from_history` は、今の割り当ての宣言の並び (投稿の順。宣言ごとに `開始可` を書いたか・差し戻されたか) からその定義のとおり持っている資源を求める。差し戻された宣言は数えず、比べる相手にもしない。

資源の確保と解放は同じセッションが組で行う: 管理のセッションは割り当てのとき (ラベルの資源) と `開始可` を書くとき (宣言の資源) に予約し、Issue の close と割り当ての解除のときに解放する。作業のセッションは着手の宣言の `resources` で使うと宣言し、使い終えたら資源を外した `宣言の更新` で使い終えたと宣言する。

## 契機

判断は契機ごとに 1 つの関数で、属性 (設定から) と資源の使用 (U13 が求める) と利用者の答え (記録にある。読むのは呼び出し元) を引数で受ける。利用者の答えの値: `when_busy` が `ask` の資源には `wait` (待つ) / `proceed` (進める)、`release_undeclared` が `ask` の資源には `release` (解放してよい) / `keep` (解放してはいけない)。

| 契機 (`--trigger`) | 行うこと | 読む属性 | 結果 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 割り当て `assign` (R19) | ラベルの資源のうち `reserve` が `on_assign` のものについて、資源を持つ項目の数 (自分を除く) が `capacity` に達していれば `when_busy` に従う。`wait` なら候補にしない。`ask` なら割り当てるかを利用者に尋ね、利用者が待つと答えたら `wait` と同じに候補にせず、答えを記録に書いて、その資源が解放されるまで同じ問いを尋ね直さない。進めると答えたら割り当てる。`reserve` が `on_declare` の資源は予約せず、空きも待たない | `reserve`・`capacity`・`when_busy` | `assign` (割り当てて `reserve` の資源を予約する) / `skip` (候補から外す。`busy` に資源) / `ask` (`ask` に資源) |
| 着手の宣言 `declare` (R20) | 宣言の `resources` のうち予約していない資源は空きを確かめ、すべて空いていれば `開始可` を書くときに予約する。空いていないものがあれば、どれも予約せずに `when_busy` に従う (`wait` ならコメント `待機` を書き、合図 `wait` を送る。Status は変えない。`ask` なら利用者に尋ね、答えを待つ間は `待機` を書き、待つと答えたら `wait` と同じ)。待っている宣言は新しく要る資源を持たない。予約したのに宣言に無い資源は `release_undeclared` に従う: `release` なら解放する。`ask` なら尋ね、答えを待つ間もほかの判定が済んでいれば `開始可` を書き、その資源は答えが出るまで予約のまま残す。解放してよいと答えたら解放し、解放してはいけないと答えたら予約を残してコメント `依頼` (宣言の書き直し) と合図 `request` でその資源を足した更新を頼む。宣言の資源が Issue のラベルに無ければ、ラベルを足すことを提案し、承認の後に `issue add-label` で足す (ラベルの提案は呼び出し元) | `capacity`・`when_busy`・`release_undeclared` | `go` (`reserve` の資源を予約する) / `wait` (`wait_for` の資源を待つ) / `ask` (`ask` の資源を尋ねる)。宣言に無い予約は結果に依らず `release`・`keep`・`ask_undeclared`・`request_rewrite` に分ける |
| 宣言の更新 `update` (R20。ready for review の前も後も) | 持っている資源から外した資源を解放する。足した資源 (前に外して足し直したものも含む) は、着手の宣言と同じに空きを確かめる。資源を外すだけの更新 (種類 `resources-removed-only`。種類の判定は [issue-format.md](issue-format.md) の「更新の種類」で、呼び出し元が渡す) は判定せず `開始可` を書かない | `capacity`・`when_busy` | `skip` (資源を外すだけの更新。`release` だけ) / `go` / `wait` / `ask` と `reserve`・`wait_for`・`ask`・`release` |
| Issue の close・割り当ての解除 `close` (R21。進行中の Issue の close では、利用者が止めると答えた後) | その項目が持つ資源をすべて解放する | — | `release` に資源 |
| 資源の解放 `release` (宣言の更新で外したとき・着手の宣言で `release_undeclared` に従って解放したとき・Issue の close・割り当ての解除) | その資源で `待機` になっていた宣言を、宣言の投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に判定し直す (ファイルの競合の可能性は、[flow.md](flow.md) の「判定」の「`開始可` を書く直前の比較」のとおりに扱う)。`開始可` になった宣言にはコメント `開始可` を書き、合図 `go` を送る (Status が `Blocked` の項目は戻す) | — | `rejudge` に待っていた宣言 (判定し直す順) |

`開始可` を書くのは、ファイルの競合の可能性でも資源でも待たないときだけ。属性を 1 つ変えたとき、結果が変わるのは、その属性を読む契機だけ。

## CLI

| サブコマンド | 書き込み | 返すもの |
| --- | --- | --- |

資源の確保と解放は同じセッションが組で行う: 管理のセッションは割り当てのとき (ラベルの資源) と `開始可` を書くとき (宣言の資源) に予約し、Issue の close と割り当ての解除のときに解放する。作業のセッションは着手の宣言の `resources` で使うと宣言し、使い終えたら資源を外した `宣言の更新` で使い終えたと宣言する。

## 契機

判断は契機ごとに 1 つの関数で、属性 (設定から) と資源の使用 (U13 が求める) と利用者の答え (記録にある。読むのは呼び出し元) を引数で受ける。利用者の答えの値: `when_busy` が `ask` の資源には `wait` (待つ) / `proceed` (進める)、`release_undeclared` が `ask` の資源には `release` (解放してよい) / `keep` (解放してはいけない)。

| 着手の宣言 `declare` (R20) | 宣言の `resources` のうち予約していない資源は空きを確かめ、すべて空いていれば `開始可` を書くときに予約する。空いていないものがあれば、どれも予約せずに `when_busy` に従う (`wait` ならコメント `待機` を書き、合図 `wait` を送る。Status は変えない。`ask` なら利用者に尋ね、答えを待つ間は `待機` を書き、待つと答えたら `wait` と同じ)。待っている宣言は新しく要る資源を持たない。予約したのに宣言に無い資源は `release_undeclared` に従う: `release` なら解放する。`ask` なら尋ね、答えを待つ間もほかの判定が済んでいれば `開始可` を書き、その資源は答えが出るまで予約のまま残す。解放してよいと答えたら解放し、解放してはいけないと答えたら予約を残してコメント `依頼` (宣言の書き直し) と合図 `request` でその資源を足した更新を頼む。宣言の資源が Issue のラベルに無ければ、ラベルを足すことを提案し、承認の後に `issue add-label` で足す (ラベルの提案は呼び出し元) | `capacity`・`when_busy`・`release_undeclared` | `go` (`reserve` の資源を予約する) / `wait` (`wait_for` の資源を待つ) / `ask` (`ask` の資源を尋ねる)。宣言に無い予約は結果に依らず `release`・`keep`・`ask_undeclared`・`request_rewrite` に分ける |

CLI のテストは偽の gh (tests/fake-gh) と固定データと、clone に見えるリポジトリ (test_repo.make_clone) で動く。場面はテストの名前に書く (計画の U15)。"""

import json

                            mcomment, node_of, observed, rec_with, t, wcomment)
from test_project import FakeGhCase  # noqa: E402
from test_repo import make_clone  # noqa: E402

_CLI = os.path.join(_SCRIPTS, "issue_dispatch.py")

A9, A5, A6 = f"{A}#9", f"{A}#5", f"{A}#6"

W8, W9 = "W-8", "W-9"
TABLE = filekinds.load_default_table()


def ok_config(rules=()):
    """read_repo_config の結果 (読める)。rules は設定の files の規則 (config.load_text でそろえる)。"""
    loaded = config.load_text(json.dumps({"files": list(rules)}), "repo", "/clone/.claude/akm-claude-plugins/issue-dispatch/config.json")
    return {"status": "ok", "reason": None, "message": None, "fix": None, "root_hint": "/clone", "path": "/clone", "config": loaded["config"],
            "warnings": loaded["warnings"], "errors": []}


MISSING_CONFIG = {"status": "missing", "reason": None, "message": "既定のブランチに設定ファイルが無い", "fix": None, "root_hint": "/clone", "path": "/clone",
                  "config": config.load_text("{}", "repo", "x")["config"], "warnings": [], "errors": []}
UNREADABLE_CONFIG = {"status": "unreadable", "reason": "not-in-repositories", "message": "管理ディレクトリの設定の repositories に akm/issue-dispatch-verify-a が無い",
                     "fix": "設定の repositories に owner/repo → clone の絶対パスを足す", "root_hint": None, "path": None, "config": None, "warnings": [], "errors": []}


def reader(result=None, by_repo=None):
    """リポジトリの設定の読み取りの差し替え。by_repo は owner/repo (小文字) → 結果。"""
    def read(repo):
        if by_repo:
            return by_repo[repo.lower()]
        return result if result is not None else ok_config()
    return read


def assign(to, number=1, at=None, cid=None):
    return mcomment("割り当て", {"to": to, "assignment": number}, at or t(10), cid or 100)


def decl(cid, at, files=(("src/a.py", None),), resources=(), to=W7, split=False, body=None, kind="着手の宣言"):
    return wcomment(kind, None, at, cid, body=body if body is not None else decl_body(files, resources, split), sid=to)


def go(decl_id, at, cid, to=W7, number=1):
    return mcomment("開始可", {"to": to, "assignment": number, "declaration": decl_id}, at, cid)


def wait(decl_id, at, cid, waits, to=W7, number=1):
    return mcomment("待機", {"to": to, "assignment": number, "declaration": decl_id, "waits": waits}, at, cid)


def item(key, comments_, position=1, status="In Progress", session=W7, labels=(), blocked_by=(), events=(), state="OPEN", prs=()):
    return make_item(key=key, comments_=list(comments_), position=position, status=status, session_field=session, labels=labels,
                     blocked_by=list(blocked_by), events=list(events), state=state, prs=list(prs))

CLI のテストは偽の gh (tests/fake-gh) と固定データと、clone に見えるリポジトリ (test_repo.make_clone) で動く。場面はテストの名前に書く (計画の U15)。"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from issue_dispatch import comments, config, filekinds, itemstate, judge, record, resources  # noqa: E402

                            mcomment, node_of, observed, rec_with, t, wcomment)
from test_project import FakeGhCase  # noqa: E402
from test_repo import make_clone  # noqa: E402

_CLI = os.path.join(_SCRIPTS, "issue_dispatch.py")
_FLOW = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "skills", "issue-dispatch", "references", "flow.md")
_RECORDS = os.path.join(_HERE, "..", "skills", "issue-dispatch", "references", "records.md")
A9, A5, A6 = f"{A}#9", f"{A}#5", f"{A}#6"
OTHER_REPO_ITEM = "akm/other-repo#2"
W8, W9 = "W-8", "W-9"
TABLE = filekinds.load_default_table()


def ok_config(rules=()):
    """read_repo_config の結果 (読める)。rules は設定の files の規則 (config.load_text でそろえる)。"""
    loaded = config.load_text(json.dumps({"files": list(rules)}), "repo", "/clone/.claude/akm-claude-plugins/issue-dispatch/config.json")
    return {"status": "ok", "reason": None, "message": None, "fix": None, "root_hint": "/clone", "path": "/clone", "config": loaded["config"],
            "warnings": loaded["warnings"], "errors": []}


MISSING_CONFIG = {"status": "missing", "reason": None, "message": "既定のブランチに設定ファイルが無い", "fix": None, "root_hint": "/clone", "path": "/clone",
                  "config": config.load_text("{}", "repo", "x")["config"], "warnings": [], "errors": []}
UNREADABLE_CONFIG = {"status": "unreadable", "reason": "not-in-repositories", "message": "管理ディレクトリの設定の repositories に akm/issue-dispatch-verify-a が無い",
                     "fix": "設定の repositories に owner/repo → clone の絶対パスを足す", "root_hint": None, "path": None, "config": None, "warnings": [], "errors": []}


def reader(result=None, by_repo=None):
    """リポジトリの設定の読み取りの差し替え。by_repo は owner/repo (小文字) → 結果。"""
    def read(repo):
        if by_repo:
            return by_repo[repo.lower()]
        return result if result is not None else ok_config()
    return read


def assign(to, number=1, at=None, cid=None):
    return mcomment("割り当て", {"to": to, "assignment": number}, at or t(10), cid or 100)


def decl(cid, at, files=(("src/a.py", None),), resources=(), to=W7, split=False, body=None, kind="着手の宣言"):
    return wcomment(kind, None, at, cid, body=body if body is not None else decl_body(files, resources, split), sid=to)


def go(decl_id, at, cid, to=W7, number=1):
    return mcomment("開始可", {"to": to, "assignment": number, "declaration": decl_id}, at, cid)


def wait(decl_id, at, cid, waits, to=W7, number=1):
    return mcomment("待機", {"to": to, "assignment": number, "declaration": decl_id, "waits": waits}, at, cid)


def item(key, comments_, position=1, status="In Progress", session=W7, labels=(), blocked_by=(), events=(), state="OPEN", prs=()):
    return make_item(key=key, comments_=list(comments_), position=position, status=status, session_field=session, labels=labels,
                     blocked_by=list(blocked_by), events=list(events), state=state, prs=list(prs))


def states_of(items, pr_states=None, attrs=None):
    return [itemstate.derive(it, LOGIN, pr_states or {}, PROJECT_NUMBER, attrs) for it in items]


def question(kind, item_key, subject, answer=None, qid="q1", asked=None):
    return {qid: {"item": item_key, "kind": kind, "options": list(judge.QUESTION_OPTIONS[kind]), "asked_at": asked or t(5), "answer": answer,
                  "answered_at": t(6) if answer is not None else None, "subject": subject}}

Review target: `f18c440..6720357`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text:
Review target: `6720357..14e5409`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `14e5409..6ecd902`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

     """割り当てで予約した資源 (reserved) のうち、宣言に無い予約として解放したもの (名前の順)。解放は GitHub への書き込みが無い導出なので、

         return []
     if d.get("go_declaration_id") is not None and before is None:

-    else:

-        sets = []
-        for x in d.get("declared_resources") or []:
-            if x["comment_id"] == before:
-                break
-            sets.append({r.casefold() for r in x["resources"]})
+        # `開始可` の後: 持っている資源 (held) が今の状態 (後の宣言で足し直して予約し直したものを含む)。`開始可` の前の宣言は見ない。
+        # held に無い予約は 2 つに分ける: `開始可` の宣言にあった資源は更新で外したものなので結果に依らず解放 (契機 update)、
+        # 無かった資源は宣言に書かれなかった予約なので release_undeclared に従う (契機 declare)
+        held = {h.casefold() for h in d.get("held") or []}
+        in_go = {r.casefold() for r in d["go_declaration"]["resources"]}
+        return sorted(name for name in reserved if name.casefold() not in held
+                      and (name.casefold() in in_go or _releasable(name, st["key"], rec, attrs_table)))
+    # `開始可` の前: 項目はまだ何も持たないので、読めた着手の宣言 (before より前) のどれかに無ければ解放した (release_undeclared に従う)

+**資源の使用** (`judge.usage_for`): `item state` の `usage` から、宣言に無い予約として解放したもの (`judge.released_reservations`) を除く。解放したとみなす予約は、`開始可` の後は持っている資源 (`held`) に無い予約 (後の宣言で足し直して予約し直したものは持っている) のうち、`開始可` の宣言にあったもの (更新で外した資源。[resources.md](resources.md) の契機 `update` のとおり結果に依らず解放) と、無かったもの (宣言に書かれなかった予約) で属性 `release_undeclared` が `release` か質問 `release-undeclared` の回答が `release` のもの。`開始可` の前は今の割り当ての読めた着手の宣言 (書き直しを含む) のどれかに無い予約で、属性か回答が `release` のもの。判定する宣言より前の宣言で解放した予約は、その宣言の判定で予約済みとして扱わない (足し直せば新しい資源として空きを確かめる)。解放は GitHub への書き込みが無い導出なので、判定と資源の使用が同じ関数で決める。

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

Review target: `28bc061..b9f4489`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

1	"""宣言の判定 (計画の U15。正本は flow.md の「判定」)。
2	
3	項目の状態 (itemstate) が導いた「判定の要る宣言」を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に 1 件ずつ判定し、`開始可`・`待機`・`依頼`
4	の書き込みの候補 (actions)・利用者に尋ねること (questions)・作業のセッションに送る合図 (signals) を返す。gh は実行せず、書き込みもしない。
5	競合の可能性は declaration.conflictability、資源は resources.judge_declare / judge_update、リポジトリの設定は repo.read_repo_config の結果で判断する。
6	"""
7	
8	import re
9	
10	from . import comments, declaration, filekinds, ids, itemstate, resources
11	
12	RESULTS = ("go", "wait", "ask", "request")
13	SIGNAL_KINDS = ("go", "wait", "request")
14	# 判定の問い (種類 → 選択肢)。種類の名前と選択肢の正本は records.md の問いの表
15	QUESTION_OPTIONS = {"conflict": ["wait", "small-pr", "proceed"], "unknown-content": ["conflict", "none"], "resource-busy": ["wait", "proceed"],
16	                    "release-undeclared": ["release", "keep"], "small-pr-closed": ["wait-issue", "redo", "proceed"]}
17	QUESTION_KINDS = tuple(QUESTION_OPTIONS)
18	_USER_ANSWER = {"kind": "利用者の答え"}
19	_PR_URL_RE = re.compile(rf"https://github\.com/{ids.REPO_NAME_PATTERN}/pull/[1-9][0-9]*")
20	
21	
22	# --- 記録の問いの答え ------------------------------------------------------------------
23	
24	def _questions(rec, item, kind, subject):
25	    """記録の問いのうち、項目 (owner/repo の大文字小文字を区別しない)・種類・対象 (subject。大文字小文字を区別しない) が同じもの。"""
26	    folded = subject.casefold() if isinstance(subject, str) else None
27	    return [q for q in ((rec or {}).get("questions") or {}).values()
28	            if ids.same_issue(q.get("item"), item) and q.get("kind") == kind
29	            and (q.get("subject").casefold() if isinstance(q.get("subject"), str) else None) == folded]
30	
31	
32	def answer_for(rec, item, kind, subject):
33	    """項目・種類・対象が同じ問いの最新の答え。答えが無い (未回答・取り下げ (answer が null)) なら None。"""
34	    answered = [q for q in _questions(rec, item, kind, subject) if q.get("answer") is not None]
35	    if not answered:
36	        return None
37	    return max(answered, key=lambda q: q.get("answered_at") or "")["answer"]
38	
39	
40	def asked(rec, item, kind, subject):
41	    """項目・種類・対象が同じ未回答の問い (答えも取り下げも無い) が記録にあるか。あれば尋ね直さない。"""
42	    return any(q.get("answered_at") is None for q in _questions(rec, item, kind, subject))
43	
44	
45	# --- 判定の順と比べる相手 ----------------------------------------------------------------
46	
47	def _items_by_key(items):
48	    return {it["key"]: it for it in items if it.get("key")}
49	
50	
51	def pending(items, states):
52	    """未判定の宣言 (判定の要る最新の宣言で、`開始可`・`待機`・`依頼` のどれも無いもの) を、投稿の順 (同じなら Project の中の順) に。
53	    要素は {"item": 項目, "state": 状態, "judged": 判定の要る宣言}。"""
54	    by_key = _items_by_key(items)
55	    out = []
56	    for st in states:
57	        d = st.get("declaration") or {}
58	        if not st.get("assigned") or not d.get("judged") or d.get("stage") != "undecided" or st["key"] not in by_key:
59	            continue
60	        out.append({"item": by_key[st["key"]], "state": st, "judged": d["judged"]})
61	    return sorted(out, key=lambda e: (e["judged"]["at"] or "", e["item"].get("position") if e["item"].get("position") is not None else 0))
62	
63

223	        if h["role"] == "worker" and h["kind"] == "小さな PR の報告" and ids.same_issue(h["values"].get("waiting_issue"), item_key):
224	            m = _PR_URL_RE.search(c["text"] or "")
225	            if m:
226	                return ids.parse_pr_url(m.group(0))["url"]
227	    return None
228	
229	
230	def _small_pr_requested(other, item_key):
231	    """相手の今の割り当てのセッションに、待つ Issue がこの項目の `依頼` (小さな PR) を既に書いたか (宣言の書き直しで待つ側の宣言の ID が変わっても、同じ依頼とみなす)。"""
232	    for c in other["comments"]:
233	        h = c["header"]
234	        v = h["values"]
235	        if (h["role"] == "manager" and h["kind"] == "依頼" and v.get("request_kind") == "小さな PR" and v.get("to") == other["to"]
236	                and v.get("assignment") == other["assignment"] and ids.same_issue(v.get("waiting_issue"), item_key)):
237	            return True
238	    return False
239	
240	
241	def _wait_body(waits, usage, j=None):
242	    lines = []
243	    for w in waits:
244	        if w["kind"] == "利用者の答え":
245	            lines.append("利用者の答え: 管理のセッションが利用者に尋ねている (競合しうる相手の扱い・unknown-content のファイルの判定・資源の使用)")
246	        elif w["kind"] == "Issue":
247	            lines.append(f"Issue {w['issue']}: 競合しうる相手の作業が終わるまで待つ (利用者の答え: wait)")
248	        elif w["kind"] == "小さな PR":
249	            lines.append(f"小さな PR {w['issue']}: 相手に共通の変更を先に小さな PR にすることを依頼した" + (f" (PR {w['pr']})" if w.get("pr") else "") + " (利用者の答え: small-pr)")
250	        elif w["kind"] == "資源":
251	            holders = usage.get(_usage_key(usage, w["resource"]) or w["resource"]) or []
252	            lines.append(f"資源 {w['resource']}: 使用中 (持つ項目: {', '.join(holders) or '-'})")
253	    body = "待つもの:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {line}" for line in lines)
254	    return body + _undeclared_lines(j) if j else body

258	    lines = []
259	    if j["release"]:
260	        lines.append(f"解放した資源 (宣言に無い予約・更新で外した資源): {', '.join(j['release'])}")
261	    if j["keep"]:
262	        lines.append(f"答えを待つ予約 (宣言に無い資源。解放してよいか利用者に尋ねている): {', '.join(j['keep'])}")
263	    return ("\n" + "\n".join(lines)) if lines else ""

265	
266	def _blocking_actions(item, blockers):
267	    """`待機` の理由の Issue・小さな PR の相手を blockedBy に足し、Status を Blocked にする (既にあるものは書かない)。"""
268	    actions = []
269	    present = [b["key"] for b in item.get("blocked_by") or []]
270	    for blocker in blockers:
271	        if not any(ids.same_issue(blocker, k) for k in present):
272	            actions.append({"kind": "blocked-by-add", "item": item["key"], "blocker": blocker, "continuation": False})
273	    if blockers and item.get("state") == "OPEN" and (item.get("status") or {}).get("name") != "Blocked":
274	        actions.append({"kind": "set-status", "item": item["key"], "item_id": item["item_id"], "status": "Blocked", "continuation": False})
275	    return actions
276	
277

279	    """前の宣言の `待機` のために書いた Blocked と blockedBy の扱い。新しい判定で Issue・小さな PR を待たないなら Status を In Progress に戻し、
280	    自分が足した blockedBy のうち待たなくなった相手は外す候補 (承認を得て `blocked-by remove`)。"""
281	    actions = []

283	    if not blockers and own and item.get("state") == "OPEN" and (item.get("status") or {}).get("name") == "Blocked":
284	        actions.append({"kind": "set-status", "item": item["key"], "item_id": item["item_id"], "status": "In Progress", "continuation": False})

content.text:
Review target: `b9f4489..95174be`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Review target: `b9f4489..95174be`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.

findings as text.
